Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved to explore outside. One day she walked to a big cliff in the countryside. It was a tall cliff surrounded by trees and flowers, with a pretty view. 

The little girl looked around and noticed something strange. She saw a shimmering light coming from the edge of the cliff. She walked closer and saw that it was a small, smelly ball of light. It was shining brightly. 

The girl asked, â€œWhat are you?â€
The little ball of light replied, â€œI am a starfish! I live on this cliff and get my energy from the sun. I shine so that other starfish can find me!â€ 

The girl smiled and said, â€œI love how you shine! I am going to come back and visit you again.â€ And she did! She came back every day to see her new friend. 
The starfish and the girl were very happy in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and always carried her favorite pencil with her. One day, she met a boy named Max.

Max said, "I have a plan. Let's draw a picture of a fair together!"

Lily loved the idea and they started to draw. They drew a big ferris wheel, a carousel, and lots of people having fun. But suddenly, Lily accidentally broke her pencil.

"I can't finish the picture," she said sadly.

"Don't worry," said Max. "I have an extra pencil."

So they continued to draw, but when they finished, a gust of wind blew the picture away.

Lily and Max were very sad that their picture was gone. But they promised each other that they would plan another fair and draw it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and cuddle with her teddy bear. One day, Lily's grandma came to visit and brought her a new toy. It was a shiny red car that could go vroom vroom!

Lily was so happy and gave her grandma a big hug. She played with her new toy all day long and it became a special memory for her. Every time she played with the car, she remembered how her grandma gave it to her and how much she loved her. From that day on, Lily cherished her new toy and the special memory it brought her.

name_of_work: I am not that Woman by Kishwar Naheed
content: I am not that woman Selling you socks and shoes! Remember me, I am the one you hid In your walls of stone, while you roamed Free as the breeze, not knowing That my voice cannot be smothered by stones, I am the one you crushed With the weight of custom and tradition Not knowing That light cannot be hidden in darkness. Remember me, I am the one in whose lap You picked flowers And planted thorns and embers Not knowing That chains cannot smother my fragrance I am the woman Whom you bought and sold In the name of my own chastity Not knowing That I can walk on water When I am drowning. I am the one you married off To get rid of a burden Not knowing That a nation of captive minds Cannot be free. I am the commodity you traded in, My chastity, my motherhood, my loyalty. Now it is time for me to flower free. The woman on that poster, half-naked, selling socks and shoes- No, no, I am not that woman!

Once upon a time, there were four friends. They were having a lot of fun together outside on a sunny day. 

"What should we do now?" asked one of the friends.

The group thought for a while. Then one of the friends came up with an idea. 

"Let's squeeze each other tight and feel very comfortable!" she said with a big smile. 

So the friends all squeezed each other tight. They all felt so happy and comfortable together. 

And after a few minutes, they all said goodbye to each other with another big squeeze before going home. 

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very excited. She was going to the doctor.
She had never been to the doctor before.
At the doctor's office she felt a bit scared, but excited at the same time.
When the doctor opened the door all of a sudden, the little girl was surprised!
The doctor smiled and said, "Hello, I'm the doctor. What can I help you with?"
The little girl smiled back and told the doctor all about her tummy ache.
The doctor was very kind and friendly. She examined the little girl and said, "Everything seems fine. You must have eaten too much candy!"
The little girl was so surprised. She thanked the doctor and was so excited to go home.
The end.

name_of_work: Constantly Risking Absurdity by Lawrence Ferlinghetti
content: Constantly risking absurdity and death whenever he performs above the heads of his audience the poet like an acrobat climbs on rime to a high wire of his own making and balancing on eyebeams above a sea of faces paces his way to the other side of day performing entrechats and sleight-of-foot tricks and other high theatrics and all without mistaking any thing for what it may not be For he's the super realist who must perforce perceive taut truth before the taking of each stance or step in his supposed advance toward that still higher perch where Beauty stands and waits with gravity to start her death-defying leap And he a little charleychaplin man who may or may not catch her fair eternal form spreadeagled in the empty air of existence

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was very happy and loved to see the world around her. One day after school she saw a beautiful butterfly. It was yellow and she couldn't take her eyes off it.

Daisy quickly ran over and tried to catch it in her hands. But the butterfly was too fast and it flew away. Daisy was a bit sad. Then she saw her friend Maria. Maria had a butterfly net and she wanted to catch it too.

But Daisy was so envious of Maria's butterfly net that she decided to delay. She quickly closed her eyes and counted to ten. When she opened them the butterfly had flown away. Daisy was sad again, but then she saw another beautiful butterfly. She couldn't wait to catch it. 

The next day Daisy said goodbye to Maria and they agreed to catch butterflies together the next day. Daisy was so excited and couldn't wait. When it was time to meet up, she ran with her butterfly net to the same spot as before. 

Sure enough, the butterfly was still there! Daisy was so happy and couldn't believe her luck. She quickly used her net to capture the butterfly. Daisy and Maria cheered and laughed together. What a wonderful day!

I AM singing to you Soft as a man with a dead child speaks; Hard as a man in handcuffs, Held where he cannot move: Under the sun Are sixteen million men, Chosen for shining teeth, Sharp eyes, hard legs, And a running of young warm blood in their wrists. And a red juice runs on the green grass; And a red juice soaks the dark soil. And the sixteen million are killing. . . and killing and killing. I never forget them day or night: They beat on my head for memory of them; They pound on my heart and I cry back to them, To their homes and women, dreams and games. I wake in the night and smell the trenches, And hear the low stir of sleepers in lines-- Sixteen million sleepers and pickets in the dark: Some of them long sleepers for always, Some of them tumbling to sleep to-morrow for always, Fixed in the drag of the world's heartbreak, Eating and drinking, toiling. . . on a long job of killing. Sixteen million men.

Tommy was excited to go to the park. He looked at the colourful swings and slides. Suddenly, he saw a hidden massage chair. He had never seen such a thing before! He walked up to it and touched it. The chair suddenly came to life and started to display a massage. It moved around Tommy's shoulders and back, giving him the best massage ever! Tommy was so happy, he hopped up and down with glee. He kept telling everyone he saw about the amazing massage chair. Everyone was in awe of the hidden massage chair!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sun with her toys. One day, she saw a lizard crawling on the ground. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Lily was enthusiastic and wanted to catch the lizard. She tried to grab it with her hands, but the lizard ran away. 

Later that day, Lily's mom made her a popsicle. Lily was so happy and ate it very fast. But then, she accidentally dropped the popsicle on the ground. The popsicle started to melt and freeze on the hot ground. Lily saw the frozen popsicle and thought it looked like a little ice castle. She touched it with her finger, and it was very cold. She thought it was like the lizard, because it was also cold-blooded.

Once upon a time, there was a big clock in the middle of a park. The clock had a big face and two long hands. It helped people know the time. Every day, kids would play near the clock and have fun.

One sunny day, a rude boy came to the park. He saw a small pond near the clock. The boy had a naughty idea. He took a big stick and started to splash water on the clock. The clock's face got all wet, and it was not happy.

The clock said, "Please stop! That's not nice!" The rude boy felt bad and said sorry. He helped clean the clock's face with a soft cloth. From that day on, the boy was kind and never splashed water on anyone. The clock and the boy became good friends, and they all played happily in the park together.

One day, Andy and his Dad went to the zoo. Andy's Dad had a backpack. He carried it wherever they went. In the backpack, he had a lunch and some blankets. 

When they arrived at the zoo, they saw a red bus waiting. Andy was so excited. He said, "Dad, can we ride the bus?"

His Dad said, "Sure, let's go!" Andy and his dad walked up the steps. The driver said, "Welcome, take a seat."

They found two red seats in the back of the bus. Andy's Dad asked, "What do you think of the seat?"

Andy said, "I like it!" He gave the seat a big hug. 

Andy and his Dad rode the bus around the zoo all day. Everywhere they stopped, more people came on and found red seats. Everyone was happy and welcomed the new passengers into the bus. 

At the end of the day, Andy and his Dad left the zoo and said goodbye to the bus driver. Andy said, "I had a great day. I'm glad we got to ride the red bus!"

Elder sister vomits blood, younger sister's breathing fire while sweet little Tomino just spits up the jewels.2 All alone does Tomino go falling into that hell, a hell of utter darkness, without even flowers. Is Tomino's big sister the one who whips him? The purpose of the scourging hangs dark in his mind.3 Lashing and thrashing him, ah! But never quite shattering. One sure path to Avici,4 the eternal hell. Into that blackest of hells guide him now, I pray-- to the golden sheep, to the nightingale. How much did he put in that leather pouch to prepare for his trek to the eternal hell? Spring is coming to the valley, to the wood, to the spiraling chasms of the blackest hell. The nightingale in her cage, the sheep aboard the wagon, and tears well up in the eyes of sweet little Tomino.5 Sing, o nightingale, in the vast, misty forest-- he screams he only misses his little sister. His wailing desperation echoes throughout hell-- a fox peony opens its golden petals. Down past the seven mountains and seven rivers of hell-- the solitary journey of sweet little Tomino. If in this hell they be found, may they then come to me, please, those sharp spikes of punishment from Needle Mountain.6 Not just on some empty whim Is flesh pierced with blood-red pins: they serve as hellish signposts for sweet little Tomino.

name_of_work: A Ballad of Two Knights by Sara Teasdale
content: Two knights rode forth at early dawn A-seeking maids to wed, Said one, "My lady must be fair, With gold hair on her head." Then spake the other knight-at-arms: "I care not for her face, But she I love must be a dove For purity and grace." And each knight blew upon his horn And went his separate way, And each knight found a lady-love Before the fall of day. But she was brown who should have had The shining yellow hair, I ween the knights forgot their words Or else they ceased to care. For he who wanted purity Brought home a wanton wild, And when each saw the other knight I seen that each knight smiled.

Once upon a time, there was an octopus who lived in a distant ocean. He loved to explore, and so, he swam from one end of the sea to the other. 

One day, as he was swimming, he started to sneeze. The noise was loud, and it echoed through the waves. "What was that noise?" wondered a passing fish. 

The octopus replied, "It was me. I was sneezing!" 

The fish smiled. "Why were you sneezing?" 

The octopus explained that he had gone on a long swim and was tired. "Now I'm resting," he said. 

The fish nodded and continued swimming away, and the octopus giggled. He was happy that he had been able to explore the distant ocean.

Lord, who createdst man in wealth and store, Though foolishly he lost the same, Decaying more and more, Till he became Most poore: With thee O let me rise As larks, harmoniously, And sing this day thy victories: Then shall the fall further the flight in me. My tender age in sorrow did beginne And still with sicknesses and shame. Thou didst so punish sinne, That I became Most thinne. With thee Let me combine, And feel thy victorie: For, if I imp my wing on thine, Affliction shall advance the flight in me.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Jack. They were having lots of fun together, playing in the garden. But then one day, something sad happened. They started to argue and Tom got so angry that he split with Jack.

It was so quiet and lonely after Tom split with Jack. Tom wanted to talk to his friend again, but he didn't know how. Then one day, Tom saw a tiny sparkle in the sky. He realised it was a special kind of magic and he knew he had to follow it!

So Tom followed the sparkle to a deep, dark cave. There, he found his old friend, Jack. But Jack was scared to touch. Tom knew he needed to show Jack he was sorry, so he gave him a big hug.

When they hugged, they both felt a spark. They realised they never needed to split in the first place and that they could be friends forever. They hugged and laughed and it was a very happy ending!

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy named Max. Max loved to run and jump in the grass. One day, Max and his friend, a little bird named Tweet, saw the sunset. The sunset was so pretty! Max asked Tweet, "What is that?" Tweet said, "That's the sunset. It happens every evening." Max had a lot of questions about the sunset. Tweet answered all of his questions. Max and Tweet watched the sunset together and had a lot of fun playing.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to collect junk. He would pick up old toys, broken pencils, and even empty candy wrappers. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play.

"Wow, Timmy! You have a lot of junk!" said Billy.

"I know," replied Timmy. "But I like it. Sometimes I can match the broken pieces to make something new."

"That's honest cool," said Billy.

Suddenly, Timmy's mom called them for lunch. As they sat down to eat, Timmy's mom asked, "Did you boys have fun playing?"

"Yes," said Timmy. "Billy thinks my junk is cool."

"Well, as long as you're happy and honest with yourself, that's all that matters," said Timmy's mom.

Searching for pillowcases trimmed with lace that my mother-in-law once made, I open the chest of drawers upstairs to find that mice have chewed the blue and white linen dishtowels to make their nest, and bedded themselves among embroidered dresser scarves and fingertip towels. Tufts of fibers, droppings like black caraway seeds, and the stains of birth and afterbirth give off the strong unforgettable attar of mouse that permeates an old farmhouse on humid summer days. A couple of hickory nuts roll around as I lift out the linens, while a hail of black sunflower shells falls on the pillowcases, yellow with age, but intact. I'll bleach them and hang them in the sun to dry. There's almost no one left who knows how to crochet lace.... The bright-eyed squatters are not here. They've scuttled out to the fields for summer, as they scuttled in for winter--along the wall, from chair to skirted chair, making themselves flat and scarce while the cat dozed with her paws in the air, and we read the mail or evening paper, unaware.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved strawberries very much. One day, Lily went to the store with her mom and saw a great big box of strawberries. She asked her mom if they could buy them, and her mom said yes.

When they got home, Lily decided to make a strawberry smoothie. She put some strawberries in the blender and added some milk. Then she turned on the blender and watched as the strawberries changed into a yummy pink drink.

Lily was so happy with her great strawberry smoothie that she drank it all up. From that day on, Lily knew that she could change strawberries into something even more delicious.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly little girl named Bella who loved to play with string. She enjoyed making shapes and designs out of the colorful string. The string gave her so much joy.

One day, Bella's mommy took her to a tall tree in the woods. She encouraged Bella to climb the slippery tree. Bella was very fearful, but she knew it would be fun to try. With mommy's help, she managed to climb up to the top of the tree.

Bella was so proud of herself. She looked down and smiled when she felt the gentle breeze on her face. She made a game out of the string by weaving it around the branches of the tree. She was so excited when she made a beautiful bird out of the string.

Bella was happy that her mommy had encouraged her to do something brave. She knew that with her own encourage she could do anything!

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent bunny. He had a big smile and liked to wink. 

One day, the bunny found some carrots in the garden. He was very excited and wanted to share them with his friends. He quickly gathered the carrots into his basket, and hopped away. 

He delivered the basket of carrots to his friends. They were very thankful and hugged the bunny. They shared the carrots and played together. 

The bunny also provided his friends with a surprise. He gave them each a funny hat. The hats made everyone laugh and giggle and everyone was so happy! 

To finish their fun day, the bunny gave one last wink. He was so happy to have been able to provide his friends with joy and smiles. His friends thanked the bunny and hugged him one last time before he hopped away.

Once upon a time there was a family who loved stores. They would often go and explore the store together. On one of their visits, they tasted something new. It was a harmless treat and everyone liked the taste. Afterwards, they went around the store looking for more tasty treats, but they never found any that tasted as good as the first one! In the end, they went home happy with the knowledge they had found something that tasted so harmless and delicious. The end.

name_of_work: I Dream a World by Langston Hughes
content: I dream a world where man No other man will scorn, Where love will bless the earth And peace its paths adorn I dream a world where all Will know sweet freedom's way, Where greed no longer saps the soul Nor avarice blights our day. A world I dream where black or white, Whatever race you be, Will share the bounties of the earth And every man is free, Where wretchedness will hang its head And joy, like a pearl, Attends the needs of all mankind- Of such I dream, my world!

The little boy was in a dangerous forest all alone. He didn't know what to do, so he decided to surrender. He closed his eyes and waited. Suddenly, he heard the soft rustling of wings and looked up to see a small bird. Its feathers were so colourful, the little boy smiled.

The bird flew right up to the little boy and then settled next to him. It opened its beak and dropped a small, blue journal. The little boy was so excited! He reached out and picked it up, carefully opening it. Inside, he saw colourful pictures and stories of different kinds of creatures.

The little boy thanked the bird and looked around at the dangerous forest. He felt different now - he could explore this place without fear. He snuggled the journal under his arm and walked off into the forest, ready for adventure!

Once there was a girl named Jill. Jill was three years old and loved to play. One day, Jill found a funny-looking object in the junk pile. She picked it up and shook it. It started to ring loudly. She was scared and dropped it. Then she felt hurt. She cried for her mom. 

Her mom came running and hugged her tightly. Together, they looked at the strange object that was making the loud noise. After a few moments, Jill's mom picked up the object. She showed Jill that it was a toy that had been broken. 

Jill smiled and said, "Can we fix it?" Her mom found some glue and they worked together to make the toy as good as new. When they finished, the toy made a gentle ringing noise that made both Jill and her mom smile. From then on, the toy was one of Jill's favorite toys. It didn't hurt her anymore.

Once there was a naughty bear named Bandit. Bandit always seemed to get into trouble. One day he was wandering around the woods and he came across a bag. He was so curious he decided to open the bag. Inside the bag was a delicious drink. 

Bandit picked up the drink and was about to drink it, but he heard a voice. It said, â€œMove away! That drink belongs to me!â€ Bandit was so startled he dropped the drink. He looked around and saw it was a rabbit.

The rabbit told him, â€œYou were very naughty for taking something that isn't yours. Next time you see something you should stop and think!â€ 

Bandit said he was very sorry and from that day on he always stopped and thought before he touched something that wasnâ€™t his. He learned his lesson and realized it was much better to be nice than naughty.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to church with her family every Sunday. One day, her mom told her they were going to prepare a surprise for the church. Lily was very excited to help.

When they arrived at the church, Lily noticed something was different. The church was empty and quiet. Her mom explained that they had to prepare the surprise before everyone arrived. Lily didn't understand what the surprise was, but she knew it was going to be fun.

Together, they set up a big table with colorful decorations and yummy treats. Lily helped her mom put up balloons and streamers. She felt proud to be a part of preparing the surprise for the church.

Finally, the surprise was ready and the church was full of people. Everyone was happy and surprised when they saw the decorations and treats. Lily smiled and felt happy too. She knew that preparing the surprise was worth it.

Once upon a time there was a pretty girl called Daisy. Daisy loved to explore and one day she decided to go for a walk in the forest. As Daisy walked, she saw a glistening light appear in the distance. She quickly ran towards it and found a beautiful glass house. It was so charming and sparkly that Daisy couldn't believe her eyes. 

Curious, Daisy walked into the glass house. She saw that inside the house were lots of shiny glass boxes with the most fascinating creatures in them. Daisy had never seen anything like them before. She wanted to get closer to them and to see what they looked like, so she moved closer. 

Suddenly, Daisy heard a voice calling out to her. It was a kind voice and it asked Daisy if she wanted to take one of the glass creatures home with her. Daisy quickly thought it over and decided she would take one of them home. She chose the cutest little creature and put it in her pocket. It was the most charming thing she had ever seen. 

On the way home, Daisy imagined what life would be like with her new creature. She was so excited about all the new adventures she and her creature would have together. 

That's the story of Daisy and her special glass creature. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow bird named Billy. Billy had a big hole in his wing. He could not fly. He was very sad. His friend, Mr. Fox, wanted to help him.

Mr. Fox said, "I can repair your wing, Billy. I will use a stitch to fix the hole." Billy was happy. He wanted to fly again. Mr. Fox took a needle and thread. He began to stitch the hole in Billy's wing.

But Mr. Fox was not good at repairing wings. He made a mistake. The hole was still there. Billy tried to fly, but he fell down. He was very sad. Mr. Fox said, "I am sorry, Billy. I tried my best."

Billy could not fly anymore. He had to walk everywhere. His wing never got better. The end.

Lily likes to draw with her pen. She makes pictures of her family, her dog, and her toys. She is very playful and happy when she draws.

One day, she draws on the wall. She thinks it is fun to make a big picture on the white wall. She draws a sun, a flower, and a smiley face. She does not know that it is bad to draw on the wall.

Mom sees the wall and is not happy. She says, "Lily, what did you do? You cannot draw on the wall. That is naughty. You have to wash the wall and say sorry."

Lily feels sad. She does not want to wash the wall. She likes her picture. She says, "But Mom, I made a pretty picture. I was playful. I did not mean to be naughty."

Mom says, "I know you were playful, but you have to learn the rules. The wall is not for drawing. The paper is for drawing. You have to wash the wall and then you can draw on the paper. I will help you wash the wall and then we can draw together."

Lily nods. She says, "Okay, Mom. I am sorry. I will wash the wall and then I will draw on the paper with you." She takes a cloth and some water and starts to wash the wall. Mom helps her. They wash the wall until it is white again.

Then, they sit on the floor and draw on the paper. Lily draws a heart and writes, "I love Mom". Mom draws a star and writes, "I love Lily". They hug and smile. They are playful and happy again.

One sunny day, Mary was playing in the garden. She was looking for something to play with when she saw a huge cauliflower growing in the garden. She was so excited, it was so big! She ran over and picked it up.

Mary wanted to show everyone how big it was, so she decided to take it to the park. She carried it in her little hands and everyone she passed looked at her with big eyes.

When she got to the park, she found a nice spot and put down the cauliflower. The sun shone on it and it sparkled in the sweet summer light. Mary smiled at how beautiful it looked.

Mary took out her crayons and drew pictures of the cauliflower. Everyone who walked past stopped and smiled at the huge cauliflower. Mary was very proud of her cauliflower and she kept looking at it until the sun went down and it was time to go home.

Lily and Sam were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They wanted to see the whales in the water. They looked and looked, but they could not see any whales.

"Where are the whales, mom?" Lily asked.

"They are hiding, sweetie. They are shy. Maybe they will come out soon," mom said.

Lily and Sam were upset. They wanted to see the whales so much. They started to cry.

"Shh, don't cry, kids. Look, there is a whale!" dad said, pointing to the water.

Lily and Sam stopped crying and looked. They saw a big, gray whale with a white belly. It was swimming near the boat. It made a loud sound, like a horn.

"Wow, it's a whale! It's so big and beautiful!" Lily said.

"Hello, whale! Thank you for coming out!" Sam said.

The whale heard them and looked at them. It smiled and waved its tail. It splashed some water on the boat.

Lily and Sam laughed and clapped. They were so happy. They settled down and watched the whale for a long time. They forgot why they were upset. They had a wonderful day with the whale.

Mary had a big smile on her face. She was so excited that she was going to the freezer. She had heard from her parents that it was full of yummy treats.

When she opened the door, the cold, rough air hit her nose. She shivered and starting rubbing her hands together to keep warm. But soon enough, all the treats made her forget all about the cold.

All around her were stacks of frozen popsicles, cushions of ice cream and ice cubes in delicious flavors. Mary couldn't believe her luck! She went around the freezer and picked her favorite ones.

As she left the freezer, Mary could feel the same big smile on her face as when she went in. She had a treat in her hand and was ready to enjoy the summer day.

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk. She wore her unusual coat with many colors. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing.

As she walked, she met a small cat. The cat said, "Meow, Lily, you should warn your mom that it might rain later." Lily looked at the sky, but it was still blue and sunny. "Thank you, cat," she said, "I will tell her."

Lily ran back home and told her mom about the cat's warning. Her mom smiled and said, "That's very kind of the cat, but I think we will be okay." They both looked outside, and the sun was still shining. Lily felt happy that she had helped, and she went back to play outside with her unusual coat.

One day, Mommy and Daddy took their little girl to the store. She was so excited to be there. Daddy showed her all the different kinds of glue and asked her which one she wanted. She picked out the pink glue and was even more excited. 

They took the glue home and the little girl had an idea. She grabbed some of her toys and paper, and began to make something new. She was hoping it would turn out exactly how she wanted. 

Since it was a special project, Mommy and Daddy stayed with her the entire time to help. They helped her glue everything together and the finished project turned out much better than they all expected. Daddy said he was really proud of her. 

The little girl was so happy with her project and smiled at Mommy and Daddy. She was full of hope that her project had turned out great.

Lily and Max were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Lily had a big pot and Max had a wooden spoon. They put some water in the pot and turned on the faucet. The water was cold and made a loud noise.

"Let's make soup!" Lily said. "What do we need?"

Max looked around and saw some brown things on the table. They were potatoes. He grabbed one and tried to cut it with the spoon. It was hard and did not cut.

"We need a knife!" Max said. "I saw one in the drawer."

Lily nodded and opened the drawer. She found a shiny knife and gave it to Max. He smiled and started to cut the potato. He cut it into small pieces and put them in the pot.

"Be careful!" Lily said. "The knife is sharp. It can hurt you."

Max nodded and cut another potato. He was having fun. He did not see that the water in the pot was getting hot. He did not see that the flame under the pot was getting bigger. He did not smell the smoke.

Lily saw the smoke and smelled the fire. She was scared. She ran to the faucet and turned it off. She ran to the pot and tried to move it. It was heavy and hot. It burned her hand. She screamed.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Lily cried. "It burns! It burns!"

Max heard Lily and dropped the knife. He saw the fire and the smoke. He saw Lily's hand. It was red and hurt. He was sorry. He ran to Lily and hugged her.

"I'm sorry! I'm sorry!" Max said. "Are you okay?"

Lily shook her head. She was not okay. She was in pain. She wanted her mom.

"Mom! Mom!" Lily and Max shouted. "Help! Help!"

Mom heard the shouts and ran to the kitchen. She saw the fire and the smoke. She saw Lily and Max. She was angry and worried. She grabbed a towel and put out the fire. She turned on the faucet and ran cold water over Lily's hand. She hugged Lily and Max.

"What were you doing?" Mom asked. "You could have been hurt. You could have burned the house. You should never play with knives or fire. They are dangerous."

Lily and Max nodded. They were sorry. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not mean to hurt Lily. They did not mean to scare Mom. They learned their lesson.

"We're sorry, Mom," Lily and Max said. "We won't do it again. We love you."

Mom smiled and kissed them. She loved them too. She was glad they were safe. She took them to the couch and put a bandage on Lily's hand. She gave them some cookies and milk. She told them a story. They were happy. They forgot about the soup.

Once upon a time, there was a large, strong bull. Every day, the bull would stand in the middle of the field and he would charge, bellowing and snorting.

One day, a little mouse scampered out from among the grass and cried out to the bull, "Please! Please stop! Youâ€™re scaring all the animals in the field!"

The bull was taken aback. He stopped charging and bowed his head. He whispered to the tiny mouse, "Iâ€™m sorry, little one. I didnâ€™t realize I was scaring you."

The mouse smiled and said, "Itâ€™s okay! But why donâ€™t you just use your horn when you want to be heard? That way, you wonâ€™t have to scare anyone!"

name_of_work: Passion For Solitude by Cesare Pavese
content: I'm eating a little supper by the bright window. The room's already dark, the sky's starting to turn. Outside my door, the quiet roads lead, after a short walk, to open fields. I'm eating, watching the sky--who knows how many women are eating now. My body is calm: labor dulls all the senses, and dulls women too. Outside, after supper, the stars will come out to touch the wide plain of the earth. The stars are alive, but not worth these cherries, which I'm eating alone. I look at the sky, know that lights already are shining among rust-red roofs, noises of people beneath them. A gulp of my drink, and my body can taste the life of plants and of rivers. It feels detached from things. A small dose of silence suffices, and everything's still, in its true place, just like my body is still. All things become islands before my senses, which accept them as a matter of course: a murmur of silence. All things in this darkness--I can know all of them, just as I know that blood flows in my veins. The plain is a great flowing of water through plants, a supper of all things. Each plant, and each stone, lives motionlessly. I hear my food feeding my veins with each living thing that this plain provides. The night doesn't matter. The square patch of sky whispers all the loud noises to me, and a small star struggles in emptiness, far from all foods, from all houses, alien. It isn't enough for itself, it needs too many companions. Here in the dark, alone, my body is calm, it feels it's in charge.

Once there was a patch in the ground. It was full of holes, fierce with its sharp edges. Every day, a little girl came by and looked at the patch. One day she decided to try something. She got a rock and started counting the holes.

She filled one after another with the rock. She kept counting and counting until she was done. On the last day she stepped back to admire her work.

The patch was now flat with no holes! But something seemed different. The little girl counted one, two, three and there it was - a big four-leaf clover! It was so special, it must have been hiding in the patch the whole time! 

The little girl smiled at her fierce discovery. She was so proud of it, she would never forget the patch.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Ben. Ben was only three years old and was very curious. One day, he decided he wanted to explore the world around him. He began to wander through the dark, musty corridors of an old, forgotten chamber.

The chamber was filthy, with cobwebs in every corner and dust covering the ground. Ben looked around in awe, but soon became scared. He didn't understand why it was so dark and silent. All of a sudden, he heard a voice.

"Don't be scared Ben," said the voice.

Startled, Ben quickly looked around. He soon spotted a little, furry creature with a friendly face.

"What are you?" asked Ben.

"I'm a Mouse." Replied the creature.

The Mouse explained to Ben that the chamber was his home and he had been sleeping in a small corner when Ben arrived. Ben was fascinated and asked the Mouse if he could stay for a bit. The Mouse was happy to agree and even showed Ben his cozy bed.

The two shared the chamber for a few hours, until Ben's parents called for him. eventuallly, Ben had to return home and the Mouse wished him a safe journey. Ben thanked the Mouse for his hospitality and promised to come back one day.

Before he left, the Mouse reminded Ben to never be scared, even in a filthy chamber.

He asked his mom, â€œWhatâ€™s in the package?â€ 

Mom said, â€œItâ€™s a surprise. Open it and see.â€ James was so happy, he couldn't wait to find out.
 
He opened the box and he saw that it was a toy castle. He climbed on it to take a look. He was so proud of himself.

Suddenly, his mom shouted at him. â€œJames! You canâ€™t climb on that. Itâ€™s not for playing.â€

James was embarrassed. He quickly jumped down from the castle and said, â€œIâ€™m sorry, mommy.â€ 

Mom said, â€œThatâ€™s ok. Itâ€™s ok to make a mistake. Just remember not to climb on it.â€

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Antonio. He was three years old and wanted to have a wagon. Every day, he asked his daddy for a wagon, but his daddy said "No, Antonio. Sorry, wagons are too expensive for us". Antonio's daddy worked hard to make money and still could not afford to buy him a wagon. 

One day Antonio found a cheap wagon in the street. He was so happy and he decided to take it home. He asked his daddy "Daddy, can I make this wagon mine?". His daddy was worried and said "No, Antonio. This is not our wagon. It belongs to someone else".

Antonio was disappointed but he decided to put the wagon back where he found it. Then he said "Okay daddy, I understand that it is wrong to take things that do not belong to me". 

His daddy was proud of Antonio and said "You should always remember that it is wrong to take something that is not yours. It is better to buy something with the money you have saved".

When Antonio got older, he never forgot this lesson. He worked hard to save the money he needed and finally, he was able to buy his own wagon. He was so happy. 

The moral of this story is that it is important to save money and important to respect other's property.

Once upon a time, there was a mama, who loved to cook. She was always looking for the perfect spot to cook her meals.

One day, mama found the perfect spot, near a calm lake and some big trees. She spread out her blanket and knew that this was the spot for her cooking.

Mama pulled out her ok and started to cook. She added some veggies, some cheese and some spices. She stirred and mixed it all together and wouldn't stop until it was just perfect.

When the food was done cooking, mama ate it all up. It tasted so yummy and she was so happy. She decided that she would come back to this perfect spot to cook again and again and again.

One morning, Sarah and her mom were in the car. Sarah asked, "Where are we going, Mom?" Her mother replied, "We're going to see something fun!" 

The driver drove through a colorful town. Everywhere Sarah looked, there were bright colors and beautiful sights. They stopped in front of a tall building with lots of windows. Mom said, "We're going in here!" 

Mom and Sarah stepped inside. Sarah saw a big room filled with shiny vehicles. She asked Mom, "What are these?" Mom said, "These are buses. All the drivers stay here and get ready to go." 

Sarah watched as the drivers talked and laughed. They began to get in their buses and the engines started. One of the buses pulled away and the others followed. Sarah said, "Look at all the colorful buses! I wish I could stay here with the drivers!"

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Sarah. One day she went outside to play. She ran around the garden until she saw a big red bubble. Sarah was so excited. She ran and jumped up and down, trying to reach the bubble. After a few tries, she managed to touch it. She smiled and gave out a big sigh of relief. The bubble bobbed around in the air and then popped. She couldn't believe it. All the colors inside the bubble sparkled in the sunlight before it disappeared. Sarah felt sad that her red bubble was gone but happy she'd been able to touch it. She went inside with a smile.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Bob. Bob wanted to win a race. Every day he practiced running, jumping and hopping. One day, the race day came. 

Bob was nervous but he tried to be brave. He lined up with the other kids. When the race began Bob ran as fast as he could. He beat the other kids and was first to the finish line. Everyone cheered for him!

Bob felt so happy to win the race. He was so pleased that he shouted out loud. He enjoyed being the winner and laughed as he ran back to his Mom.

The next day, he had to compete against the other kids again. This time, Bob finished last. He was sad and felt terrible. 

But then his mom told him it was okay; being brave and trying his best was more important than winning. Bob smiled and knew that he could still enjoy the race, even if he didn't win.

One day, Bob went to the store with his mom. He was cheerful and excited as they went inside. Inside, Bob saw a toy he wanted to grab with his hands. He kept asking his mom if he could have it, but she kept saying no. Bob was getting impatient.

Finally, they left the store. But then his mom stopped by a candy store, and told him to grab something if he wanted. Bob was so happy and he quickly grabbed a lollipop. His mom smiled and tied the candy around his waist.

Bob smiled and went back home. He was so excited because he knew he was going to get the toy from the store. When they got to the house, Bob saw the toy he wanted on the kitchen table. His mom told him that she had grabbed it from the store afterall. 

Bob was overjoyed and thanked his mom very sweetly. He hugged her waist gleefully and ran off to play with the toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to go outside and play. He saw a strange open door and decided to follow it. As he walked closer, he could hear voices coming from inside. He looked carefully to see what was happening.

When he opened the door, he saw two mean men. They were arguing and it seemed very scary. He tried to run away, but it was too late. The men saw him and they were angry. They grabbed him and threw him in a dark room.

The little boy was very scared and couldn't find a way out. He could only hear the men's voices in the other room and he knew they were plotting something bad. He tried to escape, but the door was locked. He took a big look around but everything was dark and he had no way out.

The little boy was never seen again. He was gone forever, as if he had been swallowed up in the darkness.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Jack. One day, he wanted to go out and explore the outside world. So he put on his hat and shoes, and went outside. 

He saw a stream and he was so excited. He wanted to take a closer look, so he ran up to it. 

When he got there, he saw a little fishing boat in the stream. He said to himself, "Oh, I want to go fishing!" 

But he didn't know how to do it. His mum came over, and she said "Hi, Jack! Are you ready to go fishing?"

Jack was so happy, and he said "Yes, I am ready! Please send me out, Mum. I want to catch a big fish in the stream!"

His mum smiled, and then she sent Jack out in the little boat. He had an amazing time fishing in the stream and soon, he caught the biggest fish ever!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and make funny faces in the mirror. One day, Lily's mommy left her makeup on the table. Lily wanted to look pretty like mommy, so she put on some lipstick and blush. 

After playing with makeup, Lily's room was a mess. Her toys were everywhere and the floor was dirty. Lily knew she had to tidy up before mommy came back. She picked up her toys and put them in the toy box. Then, she used a cloth to clean the floor. 

Suddenly, Lily heard the doorbell ring. It was her mommy! She was so happy to see that Lily had tidied up her room. Lily felt proud of herself and gave her mommy a big hug. The end.

name_of_work: To Helen by Edgar Allan Poe
content: Helen, thy beauty is to me Like those Nicean barks of yore, That gently, o'er a perfumed sea, The weary, way-worn wanderer bore To his own native shore. On desperate seas long wont to roam, Thy hyacinth hair, thy classic face, Thy Naiad airs have brought me home To the glory that was Greece, And the grandeur that was Rome. Lo! in yon brilliant window-niche How statue-like I see thee stand, The agate lamp within thy hand! Ah, Psyche, from the regions which Are Holy-Land!

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma. She was very excited because today was the day she was going on a special trip! She was going to a faraway country and she was happy but also a little bit scared. 

Emma quickly got ready for her trip and raced outside. She jumped in a big van and zoomed away. On the way to the airport, Emma started to feel sour in her stomach. She thought about the long trip and all the strange things she would see in the new country. She started to scream in excitement and fear. 

When they finally arrived, Emma ran through the airport. She quickly found the desk and handed over her passport. The lady behind the desk smiled and gave Emma a big stamp in her passport. 

Emma was very excited, she screamed out loud and ran through the airports doors to her special trip.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big balloon that was tied to a fence. The balloon was red and shiny and had a smiley face on it.

"Wow, look at that balloon!" Lila said. "I want it!"

"Me too!" Tom said. "But who does it belong to?"

They looked around, but they did not see anyone. The balloon looked lonely and sad.

"Maybe we can take it," Lila said. "No one will miss it."

"But that is not nice," Tom said. "Someone paid money for it. They might come back for it."

Lila thought for a moment. She liked the balloon, but she did not want to hurt anyone's feelings.

"You are right, Tom," she said. "We should not take it. Maybe we can ask if we can play with it."

They waited for a while, but no one came. They decided to knock on the door of the house next to the fence. A lady opened the door and smiled at them.

"Hello, children," she said. "What can I do for you?"

"Hello, lady," Lila said. "We like your balloon. Can we play with it, please?"

The lady looked surprised. She said, "That is not my balloon. It belongs to a boy who lives down the street. He left it here by mistake. He will come back for it soon."

Lila and Tom felt sorry for the boy. They said, "Oh, we are sorry. We did not know. We will not touch it."

The lady was impressed by their honesty. She said, "You are very kind, children. You can play with the balloon until he comes back. But be careful not to let it go. It might rise up and fly away."

Lila and Tom thanked the lady and played with the balloon. They had fun making it bounce and float. They did not let it go. They were happy and proud of themselves.

Soon, the boy came back. He was happy to see his balloon. He said, "Thank you for taking care of my balloon. You are very nice, children. Do you want to be my friends?"

Lila and Tom said, "Yes, we do. We are happy to meet you."

They all played together and became friends. They learned that it is better to share than to take, and that being kind and honest makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Dave. He was always very reliable. One day, Dave had to get to his friend's house, but his car wouldn't start. He was worried he wouldn't make it in time. He asked his neighbour for help.

His neighbour smiled, and said she'd be happy to help. She offered Dave her bike. Dave thanked her, and set off on the bike. He pedalled hard, but it was still slow going.

Eventually, Dave arrived at his friend's house. He was only a few minutes late - his friend was very happy to see him. Dave learned an important lesson that day - it's ok to be reliable, even if you're a bit late.

Annie was feeling very lucky. She had just been given a shiny new red bike! She hopped on and raced down the street, feeling the wind in her hair. Suddenly, she saw a large pine tree. It was so tall and Annie knew that she wanted to see what it would be like to climb it. 

When she got to the foot of the tree she saw a sign. It said, â€œNo Climbing!â€ Annie thought for a moment and then she decided to go ask her dad if she could climb the tree. 

When she found him, Annie asked, â€œCan I climb the pine? I saw a sign that said no climbing.â€ Her dad smiled and said, â€œYes, you can climb the pine, but be very careful!â€

Annie was very excited and she quickly scrambled up the tree. She made it to the top and looked out from on high. Annie was so happy and felt so lucky to be able to climb the pine.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy was feeling sick and his mommy used a thermometer to check his temperature. She showed him the thermometer and said, "Timmy, you have a fever."

Timmy didn't want to stay in bed, he wanted to go outside and play. But his mommy said, "No, Timmy. You need to rest and get better."

Timmy didn't listen to his mommy and went outside to play with his friends. He played and ran around, but soon he started to feel worse. He went back to his mommy and she checked his temperature again. This time it was very high and Timmy had to go to the hospital.

The moral of the story is that when we are sick, we need to rest and listen to our parents. We shouldn't ignore our health or we might end up getting even more sick.

When in the chronicle of wasted time I see descriptions of the fairest wights, And beauty making beautiful old rhyme In praise of ladies dead and lovely knights, Then, in the blazon of sweet beauty's best, Of hand, of foot, of lip, of eye, of brow, I see their antique pen would have express'd Even such a beauty as you master now. So all their praises are but prophecies Of this our time, all you prefiguring; And, for they look'd but with divining eyes, They had not skill enough your worth to sing: For we, which now behold these present days, Have eyes to wonder, but lack tongues to praise.

The whole shed smelt of dead iron: the dented teeth of a harrow, the feminine pathos of donkey's shoes A labourer backed in a Clydesdale Hugely fretful, its nostrils dilated while the smith viced a hoof in his apron, wrestling it to calmness, as he sheared the pith like wood-chips, to a rough circle. Then the bellows sang in the tall chimney waking the sleeping metal, to leap on the anvil. As I was slowly beaten to a matching curve the walls echoed the stress of the verb to forge.

Once there was a family who lived by a warm landscape. Every day they would go outside and explore the wonderful world. One day, the mom and dad decided to allow the family to take a road trip. 

The family was so excited! They packed their bags and traveled for days until they reached the beautiful spot. Every day they would look out of the car window and see wonderful things - big mountains, tall trees and lush fields.

When they arrived, the family was in awe! Everywhere they looked, there were green trees and warm sunshine. They opened the car doors and ran through the grass and splashed in the cool stream. 

Mom and dad allowed the family lots of time and freedom to explore. They hiked through the forests, watched the sunsets and even camped under the stars. It was a magical time that they never wanted to end. 

The days went by quickly, but the family will always remember the wonderful landscape they explored and the many happy memories they made.

Tom and Jen like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads and bridges with blocks and books. They have fun zooming and crashing their cars.

One day, they find a new car in the toy box. It is shiny and silver, and has a button on the roof. Tom wants to play with it, but Jen grabs it first. She says it is her car, and she pushes the button. The car makes a loud noise and starts to move by itself. It goes forward and backward, and turns left and right. Jen laughs and says it is a magic car.

Tom is angry. He wants to play with the magic car too. He tries to take it from Jen, but she holds it tight. They pull and tug, and the car falls to the floor. It hits a block and breaks. The button pops off, and a small rock falls out. It is a mineral that makes the car move. Jen and Tom look at the broken car and the mineral. They feel sad and stupid. They broke the magic car.

They say sorry to each other, and hug. They decide to share their toys, and not fight. They put the mineral in a jar, and hope to find another magic car someday. They play with their other cars, and have fun again.

Once upon a time, there was a big field. It was empty. In the field, there was a little house. In the house, there was a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue.

One day, Tim and Sue saw a big truck coming. The truck was going to deliver something. "What will the truck bring?" asked Sue. "I don't know," said Tim, "but I hope it is something fun to play with."

The truck came closer and closer. Tim and Sue were very excited. The truck stopped in front of their little house. The driver got out and opened the back of the truck. He took out a big box. "Here you go, kids," said the driver, "have fun!"

Tim and Sue opened the box. Inside the box, there was a big, bouncy castle! They were so happy. They set up the bouncy castle in the empty field and played all day long. The truck had delivered the best surprise ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a new shirt to wear. It was red and had a picture of a dog on it. Timmy loved his new shirt and couldn't wait to show it to his friends.

When Timmy went outside, he saw his friends playing with a sharp stick. Timmy knew that the stick was dangerous and he didn't want anyone to get hurt. "Hey guys, let's play a different game," Timmy said. "This stick is too sharp and someone could get hurt."

Timmy's friends listened to him and they found a normal ball to play with instead. "Thanks for keeping us safe, Timmy," his friend said. Timmy felt happy that he could help his friends and he felt proud of his new shirt too.

Once upon a time, there was a car named Red. Red needed gas to go vroom vroom. His driver, Tim, would take him to the gas station to supply him with gas. Red was always proud when he had a full tank of gas. One day, Red and Tim went on a long drive to the beach. They had so much fun playing in the sand and swimming in the waves. But when it was time to go home, Red was out of gas! Tim quickly took Red to the gas station to supply him with more gas. Red was proud again with his full tank and they made it safely back home. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily saw a comet in the sky. She pointed and said, "Look! A comet!" Her mom said, "Yes, it's beautiful." 

Later that night, Lily couldn't sleep. She saw her closet door was open and it scared her. She said, "Mommy, can you shut my closet door?" Her mom said, "Sure, sweetie." 

After her mom shut the door, Lily felt better. She looked up at the sky and saw the empty space where the comet used to be. She said, "Mommy, where did the comet go?" Her mom said, "It's gone now, but maybe we'll see another one someday." 

Lily smiled and went to sleep, dreaming of comets and closed closet doors.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. They like to act like animals. Anna likes to act like a cat. Ben likes to act like a dog.

One day, the weather is bad. It is cold and wet. Anna and Ben cannot go outside. They are sad.

"Can we play inside?" Anna asks.

"Yes, we can," Ben says. "But what can we play?"

"Let's play act," Anna says. "We can act like different animals."

"OK," Ben says. "You start."

Anna thinks. She decides to act like a bird. She flaps her arms and makes a chirping sound. Ben watches her and laughs.

"Good job, Anna," Ben says. "You are a bird."

"Thank you, Ben," Anna says. "Now it is your turn."

Ben thinks. He decides to act like a fish. He wiggles his body and makes a bubbling sound. Anna watches him and claps.

"Good job, Ben," Anna says. "You are a fish."

"Thank you, Anna," Anna says. "This is fun."

They take turns acting like different animals. They act like a lion, a monkey, a snake, a cow, and a rabbit. They forget about the bad weather. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a doll that she loved to play with every day. One day, Lily's brother came into her room and saw the doll. He wanted to play with it too.

Lily said, "No, my doll!" Her brother replied, "Please, can I play with it too?" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but be careful with her."

Her brother took the doll and started to play. He made the doll open and close her eyes, and then he made her roar like a lion. Lily laughed and said, "That's silly!" They played together for a while, and then Lily's brother gave the doll back to her. They both had fun and were happy. The end.

Look, my love, on the wall, and here, at this Eastern picture. How still its scene, and neither of sleep nor waking: No shadow falls from the tree or the golden mountain, The boats on the glassy lake have no reflection, No echo would come if you blew a horn in those valleys. And look away, and move. Or speak, or sing: And voices of the past murmur among your words, Under your glance my dead selves quicken and stir, And a thousand shadows attend where you go. That is your movement. There is a golden stillness, Soundless and fathomless, and far beyond it; When brow on brow, or mouth to mouth assembled, We lie in the calm of morning. And there, outside us, The sun moves on, the boat jogs on the lake, The huntsman calls. And we lie here, our orient peace awakening, No echo, and no shadow, and no reflection.

name_of_work: A Lost Tradition by John Montague
content: All around, shards of a lost tradition: From the Rough Field I went to school In the Glen of the Hazels. Close by Was the bishopric of the Golden Stone; The cairn of Carleton's homesick poem. Scattered over the hills, tribal- And placenames, uncultivated pearls. No rock or ruin, dun or dolmen But showed memory defying cruelty Through an image-encrusted name. The heathery gap where the Rapparee, Shane Barnagh, saw his brother die - On a summer's day the dying sun Stained its colours to crimson: So breaks the heart, Brish-mo-Cree. The whole landscape a manuscript We had lost the skill to read, A part of our past disinherited; But fumbled, like a blind man, Along the fingertips of instinct. The last Gaelic speaker in the parish When I stammered my school Irish One Sunday after mass, crinkled A rusty litany of praise: Ta an Ghaeilge againn aris . . .* Tir Eoghain:Land of Owen, Province of the O'Niall; The ghostly tread of O'Hagan's Barefoot gallowglasses marching To merge forces in Dun Geanainn Push southward to Kinsale! Loudly the war-cry is swallowed In swirls of black rain and fog As Ulster's pride, Elizabeth's foemen, Founder in a Munster bog. *We have the Irish again.

Let them be as flowers, Always watered, fed, guarded, admired, But harnessed to a pot of dirt. I'd rather be a tall, ugly weed, Clinging on cliffs, like an eagle Wind-wavering above high, jagged rocks. To have broken through the surface of stone, To live, to feel exposed to the madness Of the vast, eternal sky. To be swayed by the breezes of an ancient sea, Carrying my soul, my seed, Beyond the mountains of time or into the abyss of the bizarre. I'd rather be unseen, and if Then shunned by everyone, Than to be a pleasant-smelling flower, Growing in clusters in the fertile valley, Where they're praised, handled, and plucked By greedy, human hands. I'd rather smell of musty, green stench Than of sweet, fragrant lilac. If I could stand alone, strong and free, I'd rather be a tall, ugly weed.

The robot was walking through the garden on a sunny day when he saw something shiny in a bush. He ran up to take a closer look and saw a laser. The robot was so excited, he had heard about lasers before, but he had never seen one in real life. He picked up the laser and looked around. He knew he had to complete a task with it. 

So, the robot ran back to his home, a small metal shack nearby. He put the laser on the table and started thinking. After a while, an idea came to him. The robot started to make something. He used his laser to put together a machine. After a few hours, the robot had completed the machine. He was very pleased with himself; it was a great success. 

The robot proudly stepped back and looked at what he had created. He held up the laser and smiled, knowing he had achieved something great.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Millie who was very sad. She loved spaghetti but it was all gone! One day, her grandad sent her some in the mail. 

Millie was so excited when she got the mail - a big package! Inside were two big packets of spaghetti. Millie thanked her grandad and hugged it tight. She knew that spaghetti was the best way to make her feel better. 

The next day, Millie cooked some of the spaghetti for breakfast. It was so tasty and she enjoyed every bite. She and her family had a happy meal together and soon enough she was not feeling so sad any more. 

Millie and her family were so thankful for the special mail with the spaghetti and appreciated the thought that her grandad had given them.  They had a yummy meal and from then on, millie felt happy again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a family with two children who loved to go to the playground. The children had lots of fun playing on the swings and running around. One day, the older brother and sister decided to go on the slide. They asked their dad if they could go, and he said yes but reminded them to be generous and take turns.

So they went to the slide, and climbed up the ladder. The brother kept going up and down the slide. He wouldn't let his sister have a turn and she started to get mad. The dad saw what was happening and he came over. He told the older brother that it wasn't nice to keep the slide all to himself and that he needed to be generous. The brother apologised to his sister and let her have a turn.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be generous and share things with others. When you take turns you can ensure that everyone is happy and that no one feels left out.

There were not many fields In which you had hopes for me But sport was one of them. On my twenty-first birthday I was selected to play For Grangegorman Mental Hospital In an away game Against Mullingar Mental Hospital. I was a patient In B Wing. You drove all the way down, Fifty miles, To Mullingar to stand On the sidelines and observe me. I was fearful I would let down Not only my team but you. It was Gaelic football. I was selected as goalkeeper. There were big country men On the Mullingar Mental Hospital team, Men with gapped teeth, red faces, Oily, frizzy hair, bushy eyebrows. Their full forward line Were over six foot tall Fifteen stone in weight. All three of them, I was informed, Cases of schizophrenia. There was a rumour That their centre-half forward Was an alcoholic solicitor Who, in a lounge bar misunderstanding, Had castrated his best friend But that he had no memory of it. He had meant well - it was said. His best friend had to emigrate To Nigeria. To my surprise, I did not flinch in the goals. I made three or four spectacular saves, Diving full stretch to turn A certain goal around the corner, Leaping high to tip another certain goal Over the bar for a point. It was my knowing That you were standing on the sideline That gave me the necessary motivation - That will to die That is as essential to sportsmen as to artists. Once there was a little girl who wanted to make a cake all by herself. She had never made a cake before so she was a bit scared. But with courage she got to work. She put sugar in the bowl and mixed it together. Then she stirred and poured the mixture into a baking tin.

The little girl placed the baking tin in the oven and waited. When the timer rang she carefully took it out. The cake looked beautiful and perfect. She was very proud of herself and happy that she had succeeded.

The little girl invited her parents over to enjoy her independent success. They all cut the cake together and it tasted delicious. Everyone was very proud of the little girl. She was happy she had succeeded!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his guitar, which was his favorite toy. One day, Timmy was curious about what would happen if he played his guitar backwards. 

So, Timmy decided to reverse the guitar and play it in a different way. He strummed the strings and listened carefully to the sound. It was different than before, but it still made him happy. 

Timmy continued to play his guitar in reverse, experimenting with different sounds and melodies. His mom watched him with a smile on her face, happy to see her son exploring his curiosity and having fun. 

From that day on, Timmy played his guitar in reverse whenever he felt like it. He learned that sometimes it's good to try something new and different, even if it seems a little strange at first.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a loud dog named Max. Max loved to bark and play all day. One day, Max found a club where other dogs played together. He wanted to join the club and make new friends.

When Max went to the club, he barked very loud. The other dogs did not like it. They told Max he could not play with them if he was so loud. Max felt sad and did not know what to do. He wanted to be a part of the club, but he also liked to bark loud.

Max's mom told him to surrender his loud barking and try to be quiet. Max listened to his mom and went back to the club. He tried to bark softly and play nicely with the other dogs. The other dogs were happy with Max's change and let him join the club.

Max learned that sometimes you have to give up something to make others happy. He made many new friends in the club and they all played happily together. The moral of the story is to be kind and think about how your actions can affect others.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big jar of jelly on a bench. They are happy.

"Look, jelly!" Lily says. "We can eat it!"

"Wait, Lily," Tom says. "Maybe it is not for us. Maybe someone left it here."

Lily does not listen. She opens the jar and takes a big spoon of jelly. She puts it in her mouth. It is sweet and sticky.

"Mmm, yummy!" Lily says. "You try, Tom!"

Tom is not sure. He looks at the jar. He sees a label. It says: "Strong jelly. Do not eat. For science."

Tom is scared. He tries to tell Lily.

"Lily, stop!" Tom says. "This is not good jelly. This is strong jelly. It is for science. It can make you sick."

But Lily does not hear him. She eats more jelly. She feels funny. She feels her arms and legs grow bigger and stronger. She feels her teeth grow sharper and longer. She feels her hair grow longer and spikier.

Lily is not Lily anymore. She is a jelly monster.

She roars and jumps. She scares the birds and the dogs. She scares the people and the cars. She scares Tom.

Tom runs away. He looks for help. He sees a police officer. He tells him what happened.

"Help, help!" Tom says. "My friend ate strong jelly. She turned into a jelly monster. She is in the park. She is scary. Please help!"

The police officer is surprised. He does not believe Tom. He thinks Tom is joking.

"Ha, ha, ha," the police officer says. "That is a funny story. But it is not true. There is no such thing as strong jelly. There is no such thing as a jelly monster. Go home, kid. And stop lying."

Tom is sad. He is not lying. He is telling the truth. He does not know what to do. He misses Lily. He hopes she will be okay. He hopes she will be Lily again.

Once upon a time, in a cold land, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy lived in an igloo with her furry pet dog, Max. They were very happy together.

One day, Amy and Max went for a walk in the snow. Amy saw a big hill and she had a fun idea. She asked Max, "Do you want to slide down the hill?" Max wagged his tail and barked, which meant "Yes!"

Amy and Max ran up the hill and slid down on their bottoms. They laughed and played all day. As the sun began to set, Amy remembered the igloo they left behind. "Max, we must go back to our igloo," she said. Max barked and followed Amy as they walked back home.

When they got to the igloo, they found a surprise! Inside, there was a big, warm blanket waiting for them. Amy knew her mom had left it for them. They snuggled up in the blanket and felt warm and cozy. Amy and Max were happy they had a fun day and a warm place to sleep.

Sebastian was a happy 3 year old boy. He loved music and he was always singing and humming different songs. One day, he decided to make his own music. He ran to the kitchen and grabbed his parent's wooden spoons. He started banging them together and then began to record his own jam. He twirled around while he was playing, feeling dizzy with the excitement of creating his own song.

Suddenly, his grandma Tanya walked in. She put her hands on her hips and said, "Oh my! What is that sound?"

Sebastian stopped tapping the spoons and said proudly, "I'm recording a new jam!" His granny smiled and said, "Wow! You are such a creative boy. That's amazing!"

Sebastian ran back to his bedroom with a skip in his step. He kept a record of all of his songs and was so proud of himself. From then on, he played and recorded jams all the time. Grandma Tanya was always so proud of him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was called Susie. Every day, Susie complained about doing her job. She had to do things that she didn't like, like picking up her toys and making her bed. 

One day, Susie had a crazy idea. She decided to quit her job. She told her mom and dad the news, but they were not happy. They said that everyone needs to do their job and they asked Susie to take it back. But Susie refused. She kept complaining and saying that she would never do her job again.

Finally, her parents said that she could stop, if she wanted to. So Susie was finally able to quit her job. She was happy and she didn't have to complain anymore. The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a bright red slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Let's hurry!" Tom says. "The slide looks fun!"

They run to the slide. They take turns to slide down. They laugh and shout. They have a good time.

But then they see a big squirrel. The squirrel has a peanut in its mouth. The squirrel looks angry. It runs to the slide. It wants to chase Tom and Mia.

"Uh-oh!" Mia says. "The squirrel is mad!"

They are scared of the squirrel. They do not want to be bitten. They hurry to get off the slide. They run to their moms.

"Mama, mama!" Tom says. "There is a bad squirrel on the slide!"

"Mama, mama!" Mia says. "The squirrel has a peanut!"

Their moms hug them. They are safe. They look at the squirrel. The squirrel is still on the slide. It eats the peanut. It does not care about Tom and Mia.

"Maybe the squirrel was hungry," Tom's mom says.

"Maybe the peanut was its snack," Mia's mom says.

Tom and Mia nod. They understand. They are not mad at the squirrel. They are happy to be with their moms. They decide to play somewhere else. They leave the slide to the squirrel.

name_of_work: A Brave and Startling Truth by Maya Angelou
content: We, this people, on a small and lonely planet Traveling through casual space Past aloof stars, across the way of indifferent suns To a destination where all signs tell us It is possible and imperative that we learn A brave and startling truth And when we come to it To the day of peacemaking When we release our fingers From fists of hostility And allow the pure air to cool our palms When we come to it When the curtain falls on the minstrel show of hate And faces sooted with scorn are scrubbed clean When battlefields and coliseum No longer rake our unique and particular sons and daughters Up with the bruised and bloody grass To lie in identical plots in foreign soil When the rapacious storming of the churches The screaming racket in the temples have ceased When the pennants are waving gaily When the banners of the world tremble Stoutly in the good, clean breeze When we come to it When we let the rifles fall from our shoulders And children dress their dolls in flags of truce When land mines of death have been removed And the aged can walk into evenings of peace When religious ritual is not perfumed By the incense of burning flesh And childhood dreams are not kicked awake By nightmares of abuse When we come to it Then we will confess that not the Pyramids With their stones set in mysterious perfection Nor the Gardens of Babylon Hanging as eternal beauty In our collective memory Not the Grand Canyon Kindled into delicious color By Western sunsets Nor the Danube, flowing its blue soul into Europe Not the sacred peak of Mount Fuji Stretching to the Rising Sun Neither Father Amazon nor Mother Mississippi who, without favor, Nurture all creatures in the depths and on the shores These are not the only wonders of the world When we come to it We, this people, on this minuscule and kithless globe Who reach daily for the bomb, the blade and the dagger Yet who petition in the dark for tokens of peace We, this people on this mote of matter In whose mouths abide cankerous words Which challenge our very existence Yet out of those same mouths Come songs of such exquisite sweetness That the heart falters in its labor And the body is quieted into awe We, this people, on this small and drifting planet Whose hands can strike with such abandon That in a twinkling, life is sapped from the living Yet those same hands can touch with such healing, irresistible tenderness That the haughty neck is happy to bow And the proud back is glad to bend Out of such chaos, of such contradiction We learn that we are neither devils nor divines When we come to it We, this people, on this wayward, floating body Created on this earth, of this earth Have the power to fashion for this earth A climate where every man and every woman Can live freely without sanctimonious piety Without crippling fear When we come to it We must confess that we are the possible We are the miraculous, the true wonder of this world That is when, and only when We come to it.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and generous monkey. His name was Bongo. Bongo loved to gather bananas from the jungle. He would climb up the trees and pick the yellow bananas. One day, Bongo saw a shiny telephone on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. He had never seen a telephone before. Suddenly, the telephone rang! Bongo was surprised and didn't know what to do. He listened carefully and heard a voice say, "Hello, can you help me?" Bongo was happy to help and listened to the voice on the telephone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Luna. She was three years old and lived in a big city.

One day Luna went on an adventure. She wanted to learn a new language. She went to the park to find someone to talk to.

When she got there, she noticed a nice lady sitting on the park bench. Luna walked up to her and said, "Hello. What language do you speak?".

The lady smiled warmly and said, "I'm from Italy. I speak Italian". Luna was so excited. She took out a notebook and started to ask the lady for some words to learn.

The lady taught Luna some basic words in Italian and even showed her how to make some sentences. They talked for a long time, until it was time for Luna to go home.

Before she left, the lady gave her a warm hug and said, "Have fun learning!" Luna smiled, thanked the lady, and took the language back to her home.

Once upon a time there was an egg. It was round and cool. One day, the egg decided to turn. So it did and started rolling around. It rolled here and there, near and far. Everywhere it went, it felt so cool. 

Wherever the egg went, it looked for a nice and comfortable spot to rest. But it couldn't find the perfect place. But then, suddenly, the egg saw a very special place. It was a sunny patch of grass and the egg immediately decided it was the perfect spot.

So the egg rolled into the sunny spot and turned on its side. It was so comfy and cool that the egg decided to stay there, forever. The egg was so happy and started singing a happy song. The end.

One day, there was an old lady who had a tray of cookies. The lady left the tray on a nearby table. 

Suddenly, the tray started to escape! It wobbled off the table and hurried to the door. 

The lady saw the tray and yelled, "Wait! Where are you going?" 

The tray said nothing. It just kept going.

The lady followed the tray and asked, "Where are you going?" 

Finally, the tray stopped in front of a 3 year old boy. The tray said "I want to give this boy a cookie". 

The boy was so excited to get a cookie! He thanked the tray and the old lady. 

The tray and the old lady were both happy. They had helped the 3 year old boy find a cookie.

Once there was a nosy little bird. She loved to look for junk in the park. Every day she would fly around to find all the fun things she could use to build her nest. 

But one day, she couldn't find anything! Everywhere she looked, the park was empty.

The little bird started to worry that she would not be able to build her nest, but then she saw the most amazing thing in the corner: a pile of old junk! The little bird was so excited. 

She worked all day long and finally, her nest was complete. She was so proud of her new home.

At the end of the day, the nosy little bird was very happy to have found all the junk she needed to make her new home. She flew away with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a dad and a mom. The dad and mom loved to raise their little boy. Every day, the dad and mom would play with their little boy and make him very happy. The dad and mom would take their little boy for walks in the park. The little boy liked to run and play. He loved to explore the grass and gather pretty flowers. The dad and mom would laugh and raise their little boy up in the air. The little boy would giggle as he flew to the sky. Soon the dad and mom had to go back home and the little boy was sad. But, he knew that they would play with him again the next day, and that made him very happy.

That was the week it didn't stop snowing. That was the week five-fingered trees fell on houses & power lines broke like somebody waiting for payday in a snowstorm.
