Boom, boom, boom, boom! Alice the camel has one hump. Alice the camel has one hump. Alice the camel has one hump. So go, Alice, go! Boom, boom, boom, boom! Alice the camel has no humps. Alice the camel has no humps. Alice the camel has no humps. 'Cause Alice is a horse, of course!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, she hid inside her mommy's wardrobe. She giggled as she closed the door, thinking she was the best hider.

But then, she heard her mommy coming. "Lily, where are you?" her mommy called out. Lily tried to stay quiet, but she accidentally knocked over some clothes. Her mommy heard the noise and opened the wardrobe door.

"Lily, you shouldn't hide in here. It's not safe," her mommy said. "You could get hurt if the wardrobe falls over."

Lily felt careless for not thinking about that. She promised her mommy she wouldn't hide in the wardrobe again. From then on, she always made sure to find a safe hiding spot when she played with her friends.

Say! You've struck a heap of trouble - Bust in business, lost your wife; No one cares a cent about you, You don't care a cent for life; Hard luck has of hope bereft you, Health is failing, wish you die - Why, you've still the sunshine left you And the big, blue sky. Sky so blue it makes you wonder If it's heaven shining through, Earth is smiling 'way out yonder, Sun so bright it dazzles you; Birds a-singing, flowers a-flinging All their fragrance on the breeze; Dancing shadows, green, still meadows - Don't you mope, you've still got these. These, and none can take this from you; These, and none can weigh their worth. What! You're tired and broke and beaten? - Why, you're rich - you're got the earth! Yes, if you're a tramp in tatters, While the blue sky bends above You've got nearly all that matters - You've got God, and God is love.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Amber and Jasmine. One day, Amber offered Jasmine an adventure. "Let's go to the train station!" said Amber. 

"Ok!" said Jasmine. So, Amber and Jasmine walked to the station. 

At the station, the two friends saw a train. It was so big and the colors were so bright! They were so excited.

The conductor saw Amber and Jasmine and he smiled. He offered them a ride on the train. "Would you like to take a ride?" the conductor asked.

"Yes please!" said Amber and Jasmine in unison.

The conductor smiled. "Hop aboard, then," he said.
The ride was mild and the two friends enjoyed it so much. 

At the end of their trip, the conductor thanked them. "Thank you for the wonderful journey," the conductor said. 

Amber and Jasmine thanked him and said goodbye. Then, they went on their way, still dreaming of their journey in the train.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big hill with many trees. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was there.

"Let's go to the hill!" Lila said.

"OK, but we have to be careful. Mom said we have to follow the law and not go too far." Ben said.

They walked to the hill and started to climb. They saw many birds, flowers and bugs. They also saw a hidden cave. It was dark and scary.

"Look, a cave!" Lila said.

"Wow, let's go inside!" Ben said.

They went inside the cave. It was cold and wet. They heard a loud roar. It was a bear. The bear was angry and hungry. It wanted to eat them.

"Run!" Lila said.

They ran out of the cave. The bear followed them. It was fast and big. They were scared and cried.

"Help!" Ben said.

Mom heard them and came to the hill. She saw the bear and the kids. She was brave and smart. She picked up a stick and threw it at the bear. The bear was hurt and ran away.

"Mom, you saved us!" Lila said.

"Are you OK, my loves?" Mom said.

"Yes, we are OK. But we are sorry. We broke the law and went to the hidden cave. We were curious and silly." Ben said.

Mom hugged them and kissed them. She was happy and relieved.

"It's OK, I forgive you. But you have to learn from this. The law is there to protect you. The hidden cave is dangerous. You have to listen to me and stay safe. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom, we understand. We love you. Thank you for saving us." Lila and Ben said.

They went back to the park. They played some more. They did not go to the hill again. They followed the law and stayed away from the hidden cave. They learned their lesson. They increased their love and respect for Mom. They were happy and grateful. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brown boat. Every day the boat sailed across the blue water. One day as the boat sailed, it started to rain. It was a heavy shower and it lasted for a very long time. The boat got very wet and the crew was cold.

The boat sailed to a safe place called a harbour. It was a great place for the boat to stay dry. The crew got out of the boat and ran to shelter. They stayed there until the rain stopped. Everyone was happy when the rain was gone. 

The boat sailed around the harbour for a little while. After a bit of exploring, the crew decided it was time to go back out to sea. Everyone was excited as the boat sailed out of the harbour and back into the blue water. 

The crew waved goodbye to the harbour and sailed away into the sunny sky. They all agreed that they had a wonderful time and they wanted to come back soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Midnight. One day, Lily wanted to play with her toys, but she couldn't open the toy box. It was heavy and she wasn't strong enough to lift it. She asked Midnight for help.

"Can you help me, Midnight?" Lily asked.

Midnight replied, "Sure, I can help you unlock the toy box."

Midnight jumped onto the toy box and unlocked it with his paw. Lily was so happy that she hugged Midnight. She learned that it's okay to ask for help when something is too heavy or difficult to do alone. The moral of the story is that friends can help each other and make things easier.

Jimmy was a brave 3 year old boy who loved to play with his toy car. He loved to zoom it around the house and make motor engine sounds. One day, he decided to take the car outside, but it was so windy, he was a little bit scared. 

But Jimmy was brave, so he decided to keep going. As soon as he rolled his car down the pathway, a huge gust of wind made it blow away! 

Jimmy was scared. He ran after the car, and all the way down to his neighbor's house, where it had gone. Fortunately, the neighbor was very kind and gave it back to Jimmy. 

Jimmy thanked her with a big smile, took his car and ran back home. He was so happy to have the car back. He took a deep breath and said "Thank you!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her dolls and her favorite doll was named Molly. One day, Lily decided to take Molly on an adventure to the park.

As they were walking, Lily saw a beautiful purple flower and she wanted to pick it. "Molly, look at this beautiful flower! Let's pick it and bring it home," said Lily excitedly.

But then, a bee flew out of the flower and Lily got scared. "Oh no, Molly! Let's go to the playground instead," said Lily. They entered the playground and had so much fun going down the slide and swinging on the swings.

After playing for a while, Lily and Molly went back home. Lily put the purple flower in a vase and it looked so beautiful in her room. "Molly, we had so much fun today! Let's go on another adventure tomorrow," said Lily before going to bed.

name_of_work: At the Parrot House, Taronga Park by Vivian Smith
content: What images could yet suggest their range of tender colours, thick as old brocade, or shot silk or flowers on a dress where black and rose and lime seem to caress the red that starts to shimmer as they fade? Like something half-remembered from a dream they come from places we have never seen. They chatter and they squawk and sometimes scream. Here the macaw clings at the rings to show the young galahs talking as they feed with feathers soft and pink as dawn on snow that it too has a dry and dusky tongue. Their murmuring embraces every need from languid vanity to wildest greed. In the far corner sit two smoky crones their heads together in a kind of love. One cleans the other's feathers while it moans. The others seem to whisper behind fans while noble dandies gamble in a room asserting values everyone rejects. A lidded eye observes, and it reflects. The peacocks still pretend they own the yard. For all the softness, how the beaks are hard.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Mittens. Mittens liked to sleep all day long and never wanted to play. One day, Mittens' owner asked her to shut the door. Mittens didn't want to move, but she finally got up and shut the door with her paw.

Later, Mittens' owner gave her some food to taste. Mittens didn't like the taste of the food and walked away. Mittens' owner tried different foods until she found one that Mittens liked.

From that day on, Mittens started to play more and became less lazy. She also tried new foods and found some that she really enjoyed. Mittens' owner was happy to see her cat becoming more active and adventurous.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient igloo in a very cold place. In the igloo lived a man who was very sad. He wanted warmth, but he did not have any. He suffered in the cold igloo.

One day, a kind man came walking by the igloo. He smiled and offered the cold man a fuzzy blanket. He wrapped the blanket around the man and the man felt so happy and warm. He thanked the kind man and the kind man smiled and continued on his way.

From that day forward, the cold man was never cold again. He was so happy that he had found the kind man to bring him warmth. He was no longer suffering in the ancient igloo.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and go on adventures with her friends. One day, she went on an adventurous hike in the woods with her best friend, Max.

As they were walking, they heard a strange noise. "What's that sound?" asked Lily. "I don't know," replied Max. "Let's go check it out!" So they followed the sound until they came to a peaceful stream.

Lily wanted to play in the water, but she was afraid of getting wet. "I don't want to get wet," she said. "That's okay," said Max. "We can sit on these rocks and watch the water. It's so peaceful here."

After a while, Lily's clothes got wet from the mist of the stream. "Oh no, my clothes are wet!" she exclaimed. "Don't worry," said Max. "We'll dry them in the sun." They sat in the sun and watched the water, feeling happy and peaceful.

name_of_work: Hope holds to Christ by Gerard Manley Hopkins
content: Hope holds to Christ the mind's own mirror out To take His lovely likeness more and more. It will not well, so she would bring about An ever brighter burnish than before And turns to wash it from her welling eyes And breathes the blots off all with sighs on sighs. Her glass is blest but she as good as blind Holds till hand aches and wonders what is there; Her glass drinks light, she darkles down behind, All of her glorious gainings unaware. I told you that she turned her mirror dim Betweenwhiles, but she sees herself not Him.

Once there was a girl named Alice. She was very young and only 3 years old. One day she looked around her bedroom and noticed it was not very tidy. So she went to her mom and requested some paint.

Alice's mom said yes, and gave her some paint and a brush. She then helped Alice start to paint her room. Alice worked very hard, and painted all the walls with different colors. After that her room looked much more tidy.

Alice was very happy and excited that her room was all tidy. She showed her mom and they both smiled. They even hung some pretty pictures and changed the curtains. Now Alice felt really proud of her tidy room!

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went outside to play. He saw a small insect on the ground and thought it looked funny. Timmy picked up the insect and looked at it closely. He wondered what the insect was thinking.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a wise old owl in a nearby tree. The owl said, "Insects are very important for our world. They help plants grow and keep our environment healthy." Timmy was amazed at how wise the owl was and thanked him for the information.

Timmy decided to put the insect back on the ground so it could continue to help the world. He felt happy knowing that he had learned something new and that he had helped the insect. From that day on, Timmy always looked at insects with respect and thought about how they help our world.

name_of_work: Recuerdo by Edna St. Vincent Millay
content: We were very tired, we were very merry-- We had gone back and forth all night on the ferry. It was bare and bright, and smelled like a stable-- But we looked into a fire, we leaned across a table, We lay on a hill-top underneath the moon; And the whistles kept blowing, and the dawn came soon. We were very tired, we were very merry-- We had gone back and forth all night on the ferry; And you ate an apple, and I ate a pear, From a dozen of each we had bought somewhere; And the sky went wan, and the wind came cold, And the sun rose dripping, a bucketful of gold. We were very tired, we were very merry, We had gone back and forth all night on the ferry. We hailed, "Good morrow, mother!" to a shawl-covered head, And bought a morning paper, which neither of us read; And she wept, "God bless you!" for the apples and pears, And we gave her all our money but our subway fares.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big spider on a flower. The spider was yellow and black. It had eight legs and many eyes.

"Wow, look at the spider!" Tom said. "It is so pretty and shiny!"

"Can we keep it?" Lily asked. "We can make a home for it in a jar."

Tom nodded. He found a jar and a lid. He put the spider in the jar and poked some holes in the lid. He gave the jar to Lily.

"Let's show it to Mom and Dad!" Lily said. She ran to the house with the jar.

Tom followed her. He had an idea. He wanted to sell the spider to someone. He thought the spider was very special and worth a lot of money.

They met Mom and Dad in the kitchen. Mom and Dad looked at the jar.

"What do you have there?" Mom asked.

"A spider!" Lily said. "We found it in the garden. It is our pet now."

"A spider?" Dad said. "Are you sure it is safe? Some spiders can bite and make you sick."

Tom said, "Don't worry, Dad. This spider is friendly. And it is very rare. It is a yellow spider. Do you want to buy it?"

"Buy it?" Mom and Dad said. "No, thank you. We don't want a spider in the house. You should let it go back to the garden. It belongs there."

Tom was sad. He thought he could sell the spider and get some money. He wanted to buy a new toy. He looked at Lily. She was happy. She liked the spider. She hugged the jar.

"Please, Mom and Dad, can we keep it?" Lily said. "We will take good care of it. We will feed it and play with it. It is our friend."

Mom and Dad looked at each other. They smiled.

"Okay, okay," Mom said. "You can keep the spider. But you have to keep it outside. And you have to be careful. Don't touch it or let it out of the jar. And don't sell it to anyone. It is not a toy. It is a living thing."

Tom and Lily agreed. They thanked Mom and Dad. They took the jar outside. They put it on a table. They watched the spider move and spin a web. They were happy. They had a yellow spider.

name_of_work: Snowshoe to Otter Creek by Stacie Cassarino
content: love lasts by not lasting --Jack Gilbert I'm mapping this new year's vanishings: lover, yellow house, the knowledge of surfaces. This is not a story of return. There are times I wish I could erase the mind's lucidity, the difficulty of Sundays, my fervor to be touched by a woman two Februarys gone. What brings the body back, grieved and cloven, tromping these woods with nothing to confide in? New snow reassumes the circleting trees, the bridge above the creek where I stand like a stranger to my life. There is no single moment of loss, there is an amassing. The disbeliever sleeps at an angle in the bed. The orchard is a graveyard. Is this the real end? Someone shoveling her way out with cold intention? Someone naming her missing?

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and make mud pies. They had a big bucket of water to wet the dirt and make it sticky.

"Look at my mud pie!" Lily said. "It has a cherry on top!" She pointed to a red pebble she had found.

"That's a nice mud pie!" Ben said. "But mine is bigger!" He showed her his mud pie. It was very big and round.

They were having fun, but then they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Rex. Rex was running towards them, barking and wagging his tail. He was very happy to see them.

But Rex did not see the bucket of water. He bumped into it and made it fall over. The water spilled everywhere. It soaked Lily and Ben and their mud pies.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben cried. "Our mud pies are ruined!"

They looked at their mud pies. They were not pies anymore. They were just wet dust. They felt very sad.

"Bad dog!" Lily said. "You spoiled our game!"

Rex did not understand. He thought they were playing with him. He licked their faces and tried to cheer them up.

But Lily and Ben did not want to play with Rex. They were too sad. They went inside the house to change their clothes and dry off.

Rex stayed in the garden. He looked at the wet dust. He thought it was fun. He rolled in it and made himself dirty. He was very happy. He did not know why Lily and Ben were sad. He hoped they would come back and play with him soon.

name_of_work: The Day is Done by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
content: The day is done, and the darkness Falls from the wings of Night, As a feather is wafted downward From an eagle in his flight. I see the lights of the village Gleam through the rain and the mist, And a feeling of sadness comes o'er me That my soul cannot resist: A feeling of sadness and longing, That is not akin to pain, And resembles sorrow only As the mist resembles the rain. Come, read to me some poem, Some simple and heartfelt lay, That shall soothe this restless feeling, And banish the thoughts of day. Not from the grand old masters, Not from the bards sublime, Whose distant footsteps echo Through the corridors of Time. For, like strains of martial music, Their mighty thoughts suggest Life's endless toil and endeavor; And to-night I long for rest. Read from some humbler poet, Whose songs gushed from his heart, As showers from the clouds of summer, Or tears from the eyelids start; Who, through long days of labor, And nights devoid of ease, Still heard in his soul the music Of wonderful melodies. Such songs have power to quiet The restless pulse of care, And come like the benediction That follows after prayer. Then read from the treasured volume The poem of thy choice, And lend to the rhyme of the poet The beauty of thy voice. And the night shall be filled with music, And the cares, that infest the day, Shall fold their tents, like the Arabs, And as silently steal away.

Once there was a little boy called Sam. He was 3 years old and he loved playing with his toy guns. Every day he would get out his guns and pretend to shoot. He would make 'pew, pew' noises and make believe he was an army soldier, shooting millions of enemies.

One day his dad said, "Sam, help me clean the shelves in the room." So, Sam got to work. He wiped all the shelves with a cloth, until they were very clean. Then he went back to playing with his toy guns. He was shooting at the shelves, making 'pew, pew' noises and pretending he was an army soldier. 

After playing for some time, his dad called him again, "Sam, can you help me put the books and toys back on the shelves?" So, Sam got to work again. He put all the books and toys back on the shelves and made sure they were nice and tidy. 

When he was finished, he looked around and was very happy. The shelves were now clean and looked nice and tidy. And he was very excited to go back to playing with his toy guns and shooting at the shelves.

name_of_work: Since there's no help, come let us kiss and part by Michael Drayton
content: Since there's no help, come let us kiss and part. Nay, I have done, you get no more of me; And I am glad, yea glad with all my heart, That thus so cleanly I myself can free. Shake hands for ever, cancel all our vows, And when we meet at any time again, Be it not seen in either of our brows That we one jot of former love retain. Now at the last gasp of Love's latest breath, When, his pulse failing, Passion speechless lies; When Faith is kneeling by his bed of death, And Innocence is closing up his eyes-- Now, if thou wouldst, when all have given him over, From death to life thou might'st him yet recover!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had beautiful long hair. One day, while she was playing outside, a naughty bird flew over and snatched a strand of her hair. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. 

Her mommy tried to comfort her and told her that she was grateful that the bird didn't take all of her hair. Lily tried to be brave and wiped her tears away. 

The next day, Lily went outside again and saw the same bird. She was scared that it would try to take more of her hair. But this time, she stood up tall and shouted at the bird to go away. The bird flew away and Lily was happy that she had tried to be brave. 

From that day on, Lily was grateful for her beautiful hair and made sure to keep it safe from any naughty birds.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy who loved to eat jam. Every morning, she would spread jam on her toast and eat it happily. She loved it so much that one day she decided to take a spoon and eat it straight from the jar. As Lucy opened the jar, she was surprised to find that the jam was bitter tasting! She was disappointed, and started to cry. "Why is the jam so bitter?" she asked.

Her mom came into the kitchen, and told her a story. She said that years ago, her grandmother was making a batch of jam, but accidentally made it too bitter! She was so sad, but decided to just stay with the bitter jam, rather than make a new batch.

As Lucy heard this story, her tears stopped. She realized that her grandmother had stayed with the bitter jam, so she decided to stay with it too. In the end, Lucy finished the jar of jam, even with its bitter taste. She was reminded of her grandmother each time she ate it, showing her that sometimes it's okay to stay with something even if it's a little bitter.

Mattie was a brave girl who loved to explore and one day she decided to visit the barn. She walked along the bright path of sunshine and when she arrived, she looked around with wonder.

Inside the barn, Mattie noticed a strange figure in the corner and said, "Who are you?"

The figure slowly stepped forward and replied, "I'm Gertie! Would you like to take a look at my secret?"

Mattie eagerly said, "Yes!" and Gertie told her to follow her. Gertie then took Mattie to a large box. She opened it, revealing something shiny and she said, "Take it if you dare!"

Mattie wanted to be brave so she reached in and took the shiny object. Suddenly, the box released an evil laugh and Mattie screamed in terror! Gertie explained, "You should not have taken this - it belongs to me." Gertie quickly locked Mattie in the box and she never saw the light of day again.

Even though Mattie had been warned, she was too curious and ended up paying the ultimate price.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy and his sister. The boy was happy, but the sister was gloomy. She did not like to play with the boy. The boy wanted to make his sister happy.

One day, the boy had an idea. He said to his sister, "Let's order a big toy for us to play with. It will make you happy!" The sister thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, let's do it."

They picked a toy together and ordered it. When the toy came, the sister was still gloomy. But when they started to play with the toy, she began to smile. The boy was happy to see his sister happy. They played together all day and the gloomy sister was gloomy no more.

Sara liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they made funny shapes with their bodies and breathed slowly. Sara liked to stretch her legs and arms and feel strong and calm.

One day, Sara and her mom were doing yoga in the living room. They had a big mat on the floor and some music playing softly. Sara was trying to do a pose like a bridge, but she lost her balance and fell on the table. The table broke and the lamp fell down and made a loud noise.

"Oh no, Sara, are you okay?" mom asked, running to her.

"I'm okay, mom, but the table and the lamp are not okay," Sara said, looking at the mess.

"Don't worry, honey, we can repair them. Repair means to fix something that is broken. We just need some tools and some glue and some tape. Can you help me find them?" mom said, smiling.

"Yes, mom, I can help you. I'm sorry I broke the table and the lamp," Sara said, feeling bad.

"It's okay, Sara, accidents happen. You didn't mean to break them. And look, the living room is empty now. Empty means there is nothing in it. We can move the mat and do some more yoga. Maybe we can find a pose that is easier for you. How about a cat or a dog?" mom said, hugging her.

"I like cats and dogs. Let's do that, mom. And then we can repair the table and the lamp together. I love you, mom," Sara said, feeling happy.

"I love you too, Sara. You are my best yoga partner," mom said, kissing her.

When did my childhood go? Was it the day I ceased to be eleven, Was it the time I realised that Hell and Heaven, Could not be found in Geography, And therefore could not be, Was that the day! When did my childhood go? Was it the time I realised that adults were not all they seemed to be, They talked of love and preached of love, But did not act so lovingly, Was that the day! When did my childhood go? Was it when I found my mind was really mine, To use whichever way I choose, Producing thoughts that were not those of other people But my own, and mine alone Was that the day! Where did my childhood go? It went to some forgotten place, That's hidden in an infant's face, That's all I know.

Once upon a time there was an adorable bunny. Her name was Binky and she had big floppy ears, a soft white tummy and a long tail. One day, while skipping in her garden, Binky suddenly heard a voice calling to her. 

"Come to me little one," the voice said. 

Curious, Binky hopped closer. She noticed a garden gnome with a bright blue hat and sparkly eyes holding his arm outstretched towards her. 

"I want to spoil you, little Binky," he said. 

Binky tilted her head and asked, "Why?" 

The gnome smiled at her and gently patted his arm. "Because, I think you're very special and I want to show you. Hop onto my arm and I'll show you something special."

Binky thought for a moment and then hopped onto the gnome's arm, snuggling in close against his soft blue hat. The gnome smiled and flew away, carrying Binky with him high into the sky. Binky looked down and could see her garden below, small and beautiful. 

The gnome laughed and said, "Now, little one, that's what it means to be spoiled!" 

Binky smiled, snuggling closer, enjoying her special ride through the sky.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and make noise. They did not like to clean their toys or their clothes. They thought cleaning was boring and hard.

One day, they saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a monster with long arms and sharp teeth. They were scared and ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, there is a monster in the garden!" they cried.

Mom looked at the wall and smiled. She said, "That is not a monster, that is your shadow. It is made by the sun and your body. It changes when you move or when the sun moves. It is not scary, it is fun. Do you want to play with your shadow?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They followed mom to the wall and tried to make different shapes with their shadow. They made a bird, a cat, a star, and a flower. They laughed and had fun.

But then, they saw something disgusting on the wall. It was brown and sticky and smelled bad. It was their mud and chocolate and juice that they had spilled on their toys and clothes. They had not cleaned them and they had stuck to the wall.

"Yuck, what is that?" they asked.

Mom said, "That is your mess. It is not fun, it is dirty. It can make you sick and it can ruin the wall. You need to clean it up. Do you want to help me?"

Tim and Lily shook their heads. They did not want to clean. They wanted to play.

Mom said, "If you do not clean, you cannot play. Cleaning is part of playing. It is good for you and for the garden. It can also be fun if you do it together. Do you want to try?"

Tim and Lily thought for a moment. They did not like the disgusting mess. They did not want to be sick or ruin the wall. They wanted to play with their shadow and their mom. They decided to try.

They said, "Okay, mom, we will help you. How do we clean?"

Mom smiled and gave them a bucket, a sponge, and some soap. She said, "You use the water and the soap and the sponge to wipe the mess off the wall. Then you rinse it with more water. Then you dry it with a towel. Then you put your toys and clothes in the basket. Then you are done. Do you want to start?"

Tim and Lily said, "Yes, mom, we want to start." They took the bucket, the sponge, and the soap and went to the wall. They started to clean the mess. They saw their shadow on the wall. It looked like they were dancing and singing. They had fun.

They cleaned the wall until it was shiny and clean. They put their toys and clothes in the basket. They dried the wall with a towel. They were done.

They said, "Mom, mom, we cleaned the wall. It looks nice. We had fun. Can we play some more?"

Mom hugged them and said, "Yes, you can play some more. You did a great job. I am proud of you. You learned how to clean and how to have fun. You are not scared of your shadow. You are brave and smart and kind. I love you."

Tim and Lily said, "We love you too, mom. Thank you for teaching us. Can we play with our shadow again?"

Mom said, "Of course, you can. Let's go and see what shapes we can make. Maybe we can make a monster and scare it away."

They laughed and ran to the wall. They played with their shadow and their mom. They were happy.

name_of_work: To India - My Native Land by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio
content: My country! In thy days of glory past A beauteous halo circled round thy brow and worshipped as a deity thou wast-- Where is thy glory, where the reverence now? Thy eagle pinion is chained down at last, And grovelling in the lowly dust art thou, Thy minstrel hath no wreath to weave for thee Save the sad story of thy misery! Well--let me dive into the depths of time And bring from out the ages, that have rolled A few small fragments of these wrecks sublime Which human eye may never more behold And let the guerdon of my labour be, My fallen country! One kind wish for thee!

Once there was Bob who lived in a small house near the beach. He saw a giant reef above the water, and he decided to go explore it.

Bob got into his boat and started rowing. The waves were big and the wind was howling, but he kept going.

Suddenly, the boat broke and started to sink. Bob shouted for help, but no one came. He was scared, until he saw a safe beach nearby. 

Bob began to swim towards the beach. He was so happy when he reached the shore. He had made it safely!

Bob realized he was still far away from home. He sat down on the sand and looked at the giant reef above the water. He was glad he had come to explore, even if it was to break his boat.

Ben likes to play with his car. He has a red car that can go fast and make loud noises. He likes to drive his car on the floor and pretend he is a racer.

One day, Ben wants to measure his car. He wants to know how big his car is. He looks for something to measure with. He sees a ruler on the table. He does not know what a ruler is, but he thinks it looks like a stick. He takes the ruler and puts it next to his car.

He tries to count the numbers on the ruler, but he does not know them all. He only knows one, two, three, four, and five. He sees that his car is longer than five. He is happy. He thinks his car is very big.

He wants to show his mom how big his car is. He runs to the kitchen with his car and his ruler. He sees his mom making a cake. He says, "Mom, look! My car is big! It is longer than five!"

His mom smiles and says, "Wow, Ben, that is a big car! You are very smart to measure it. How did you do that?"

Ben shows his mom his ruler. He says, "I used this stick. It has numbers on it. I counted them. My car is longer than five."

His mom says, "That is not a stick, Ben. That is a ruler. It is a tool to measure things. You can measure many things with a ruler. Do you want to measure something else?"

Ben thinks for a moment. He looks around the kitchen. He sees his cat sleeping on the couch. He says, "I want to measure my cat. He is lazy. He does not play with me. Maybe he is too big to play."

His mom says, "Okay, Ben, you can measure your cat. But be gentle. He might not like it."

Ben nods and runs to the couch with his car and his ruler. He tries to measure his cat, but his cat does not like it. He hisses and scratches Ben. Ben drops his car and his ruler and cries.

His mom hears him and comes to the couch. She hugs Ben and says, "Oh, Ben, I'm sorry. Your cat did not want to be measured. He was scared. He did not mean to hurt you. Are you okay?"

Ben sniffles and says, "I'm okay, Mom. But my cat is mean. He does not like me. He does not like my car. He does not like my ruler."

His mom says, "Your cat is not mean, Ben. He is just different. He likes to sleep and be quiet. He does not like loud noises and fast things. He likes you, but he does not like to play the same way as you. You have to respect his feelings and his space. Do you understand?"

Ben nods and says, "I understand, Mom. I'm sorry, cat. I will not measure you again. I will let you sleep. Can I still play with my car?"

His mom says, "Of course, Ben. You can play with your car. But be careful with your ruler. It is not a toy. It is a tool. You can use it to measure things, but you have to ask first. And you have to be gentle and respectful. Do you promise?"

Ben promises and says, "I promise, Mom. Thank you for the ruler. It is cool. I like to measure things. Can I measure the cake?"

His mom laughs and says, "No, Ben. You cannot measure the cake. The cake is for eating, not for measuring. But you can help me decorate it. Do you want to do that?"

Ben says, "Yes, Mom. I want to do that. That sounds fun. Can I put sprinkles on it?"

His mom says, "Sure, Ben. You can put sprinkles on it. But not too many. We don't want to make the cake too sweet."

Ben says, "Okay, Mom. I will not put too many. Just enough to make it pretty. Like my car."

His mom says, "Yes, Ben. Like your car. Your car is very pretty. And very big. And very fast. And very loud. And I love you very much."

Ben says, "I love you too, Mom. You are the best mom ever. And you make the best cake ever. And you are very smart. And very kind. And very gentle. And very respectful."

His mom says, "Thank you, Ben. You are the best son ever. And you are very smart. And very kind. And very gentle. And very respectful. And very curious. And very creative. And very brave."

Anna and her mom went to the store. Anna liked the store. She saw many things. She saw toys and books and clothes. She saw a big cake. The cake was sweet. Anna wanted the cake.

"Mom, can I have the cake?" Anna asked.

"No, Anna, we have to go home. We have no money for the cake," mom said.

"But I want the cake. It is sweet. Please, mom, please," Anna said.

"Anna, stop. You have to stay with me. Do not run away. The store is big. You can get lost," mom said.

Anna did not listen. She ran away from mom. She ran to the cake. She tried to grab the cake. But the cake was too high. Anna fell down. She hurt her knee. She cried.

"Anna, where are you?" mom called.

Anna heard mom. She was scared. She wanted mom. She said, "Mom, I am here. I am sorry. I fell down. I hurt my knee. I want you."

Mom found Anna. She hugged Anna. She said, "Anna, I am here. I am sorry. You are hurt. I love you."

Mom took Anna to the car. She gave Anna a band-aid. She gave Anna a kiss. She said, "Anna, next time, you have to stay with me. Do not run away. The store is not for cake. The store is for shopping. We can make a cake at home. It will be sweet. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will stay with you. I love you. Can we make a cake at home?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Yes, Anna. We can make a cake at home. It will be fun. It will be sweet. You are my sweet girl."

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little girl. One day, while playing in her bedroom, she noticed a package on the floor. She was so curious that she grabbed it and opened it. Inside, there was a big doll. The little girl was so excited that she started jumping.

When her mother came in, she said "What are you doing?!" 

The little girl said, "Mommy I found a package with a doll inside!" 

Her mother said, "That's great! I realize that you're so excited about it."

The little girl thanked her mother with a big hug and played happily with her new toy. 

The nosy little girl was so happy she realized that sometimes being nosy can make you very lucky!

Mum and Dad were having a party. All the family were there and they were having a great time. Mum and Dad had a quarrel. Dad was embarrassed and Mum was not happy. Everyone watched them quarrel. Everyone was quiet and they felt sad.

After the quarrel, Mum and Dad made up. Mum hugged Dad and Dad smiled. All the family were happy. They went back to the party and it was more fun. Everyone laughed and danced. They forgot all about the quarrel. 

The party was the best ever. Mum and Dad were happy and everyone laughed and talked. The party was a great success!

Once upon a time there was a farmer. He lived on a farm and grew lots of vegetables. He had so many vegetables, he didn't know what to do with them all!

One day he was walking across the farm when he heard a noise. It sounded like something was broken. He looked around, but he couldn't see anything. He decided to stay and watch and see if he could figure out what was broken.

After a few long minutes, he saw a baby deer. The deer had a broken leg and was lying on the ground. The farmer knew he couldn't fix the deer's leg by himself, so he stayed with the deer and kept it safe.

A few days later, a vet came to the farm and fixed the deer's broken leg. The happy deer thanked the farmer for staying with him and protecting him until help arrived. The farmer smiled and said goodbye to the deer as it ran off into the forest. 

The farmer knew that he had done the right thing by staying and protecting the deer. He went back to his farm and continued to grow plenty of healthy vegetables.

Once there was a cricket. He was fair and very playful. He loved to kick and play. Every day he would look for something to kick. One day he found a ball and was so excited. He picked it up and from the top of a hill he kicked the ball. It rolled and rolled until it stopped at the bottom. The cricket raced down the hill so that he could kick it again. He had so much fun kicking the ball up and down the hill. He kicked it until it was time to go home. The cricket was very happy, he had a fair day of fun playing with his new ball.

Once upon a time, there was a fast rabbit named Bob. Bob loved to run and play with his friends in the big green park. One day, Bob and his friends were playing a fun game of catch. They were all laughing and having a great time.

Bob's mom called him for lunch. She knew he was very hungry after playing with his friends. She made a big plate of food for him. On the plate, there was a carrot. Bob looked at the carrot and said, "I hate carrots!" His mom smiled and said, "Just try it, you might like it."

Bob took a small bite of the carrot. To his surprise, he liked it! He ate the whole carrot very fast. From that day on, Bob loved carrots and ate them every day. He learned that trying new things can be fun and tasty. And he kept playing with his friends, running very fast, and eating his favorite food, carrots.

At home, in my flannel gown, like a bear to its floe, I clambered to bed; up the globe's impossible sides I sailed all night--till at last, with my black beard, My furs and my dogs, I stood at the northern pole. There in the childish night my companions lay frozen, The stiff furs knocked at my starveling throat, And I gave my great sigh: the flakes came huddling, Were they really my end? In the darkness I turned to my rest. --Here, the flag snaps in the glare and silence Of the unbroken ice. I stand here, The dogs bark, my beard is black, and I stare At the North Pole . . . And now what? Why, go back. Turn as I please, my step is to the south. The world--my world spins on this final point Of cold and wretchedness: all lines, all winds End in this whirlpool I at last discover. And it is meaningless. In the child's bed After the night's voyage, in that warm world Where people work and suffer for the end That crowns the pain--in that Cloud-Cuckoo-Land I reached my North and it had meaning. Here at the actual pole of my existence, Where all that I have done is meaningless, Where I die or live by accident alone-- Where, living or dying, I am still alone; Here where North, the night, the berg of death Crowd me out of the ignorant darkness, I see at last that all the knowledge I wrung from the darkness--that the darkness flung me-- Is worthless as ignorance: nothing comes from nothing, The darkness from the darkness. Pain comes from the darkness And we call it wisdom. It is pain.

name_of_work: Rock Me to Sleep by Elizabeth Akers Allen
content: Backward, turn backward, O Time, in your flight, Make me a child again just for tonight! Mother, come back from the echoless shore, Take me again to your heart as of yore; Kiss from my forehead the furrows of care, Smooth the few silver threads out of my hair; Over my slumbers your loving watch keep;-- Rock me to sleep, mother, - rock me to sleep! Backward, flow backward, O tide of the years! I am so weary of toil and of tears,-- Toil without recompense, tears all in vain,-- Take them, and give me my childhood again! I have grown weary of dust and decay,-- Weary of flinging my soul-wealth away; Weary of sowing for others to reap;-- Rock me to sleep, mother - rock me to sleep! Tired of the hollow, the base, the untrue, Mother, O mother, my heart calls for you! Many a summer the grass has grown green, Blossomed and faded, our faces between: Yet, with strong yearning and passionate pain, Long I to-night for your presence again. Come from the silence so long and so deep;-- Rock me to sleep, mother, - rock me to sleep! Over my heart, in the days that are flown, No love like mother-love ever has shone; No other worship abides and endures,-- Faithful, unselfish, and patient like yours: None like a mother can charm away pain From the sick soul and the world-weary brain. Slumber's soft calms o'er my heavy lids creep;-- Rock me to sleep, mother, - rock me to sleep! Come, let your brown hair, just lighted with gold, Fall on your shoulders again as of old; Let it drop over my forehead to-night, Shading my faint eyes away from the light; For with its sunny-edged shadows once more Haply will throng the sweet visions of yore; Lovingly, softly, its bright billows sweep;-- Rock me to sleep, mother, - rock me to sleep! Mother, dear mother, the years have been long Since I last listened your lullaby song: Sing, then, and unto my soul it shall seem Womanhood's years have been only a dream. Clasped to your heart in a loving embrace, With your light lashes just sweeping my face, Never hereafter to wake or to weep;-- Rock me to sleep, mother, - rock me to sleep!

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom who lived with his mummy and daddy. He was playing in the garden when he came across a screw on the ground. Tom asked his mummy what it was and she said it was a screw. He had never seen one before, so he picked it up and started to ask lots of questions.

"Can I keep it mummy?" asked Tom.
Mummy replied, "No Tom, you can't keep it. Put it back outside please."

Tom was sad and he wanted to keep the screw. He asked his mummy if he could keep it, but she said no again. Tom started to get cross and he shouted "I want to keep the screw".

Mummy was getting sleepy, but she was still determined that Tom couldn't keep it. She said, "Tom, you can't keep the screw. Now put it back outside and let's go inside for dinner".

Tom was unhappy but he slowly put the screw back on the ground. As he walked inside, he was very sad that he couldn't keep it.

Once upon a time, there was an old mailbox on the street. It was very rusty and had lots of scratches. One day, a nice person came and put a new shiny mailbox next to the old one. The new mailbox was very pretty and had a lock to prevent anyone from taking the letters inside. 

The old mailbox felt sad and lonely because nobody used it anymore. But then, a little bird came and made a nest inside the old mailbox. The bird was very happy and felt safe because nobody could take its eggs. The old mailbox was happy again because it had a new friend. 

Now, every day the bird would come and sit on the old mailbox and sing a beautiful song. The old mailbox was very proud to have such a lovely friend. And even though the new mailbox was very nice, the old mailbox was still loved and important because it prevented the bird's eggs from being taken.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, her mom gave her a jug of lemonade. The jug was big and heavy, but Lily was strong and carried it carefully.

Lily poured the lemonade into a cup and took a sip. It was smooth and sweet. She drank some more and then paused to look at the clouds in the sky. They were fluffy and white.

After a while, Lily went back to playing. She ran around and laughed with her friends. When she got thirsty again, she took another sip of lemonade from her jug. It was still smooth and tasty. She was happy to have such a yummy drink on a hot day.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toy cars. One day, he was playing with his cars in the living room. Tim made the cars go fast and slow, and he made them seat on the floor.

As Tim played, he made a big wreck with his cars. The cars were all over the floor, and Tim was very happy. He laughed and clapped his hands. Tim's mom saw the wreck and smiled.

Tim's mom said, "Let's clean up the wreck together." Tim and his mom put the cars away. After they finished, Tim gave his mom a big hug. They were both very jolly and happy.

name_of_work: And When My Sorrow was Born by Kahlil Gibran
content: When my Sorrow was born I nursed it with care, and watched over it with loving tenderness. And my Sorrow grew like all living things, strong and beautiful and full of wondrous delights. And we loved one another, my Sorrow and I, and we loved the world about us; for Sorrow had a kindly heart and mine was kindly with Sorrow. And when we conversed, my Sorrow and I, our days were winged and our nights were girdled with dreams; for Sorrow had an eloquent tongue, and mine was eloquent with Sorrow. And when we sang together, my Sorrow and I, our neighbors sat at their windows and listened; for our songs were deep as the sea and our melodies were full of strange memories. And when we walked together, my Sorrow and I, people gazed at us with gentle eyes and whispered in words of exceeding sweetness. And there were those who looked with envy upon us, for Sorrow was a noble thing and I was proud with Sorrow. But my Sorrow died, like all living things, and alone I am left to muse and ponder. And now when I speak my words fall heavily upon my ears. And when I sing my songs my neighbours come not to listen. And when I walk the streets no one looks at me. Only in my sleep I hear voices saying in pity, "See, there lies the man whose Sorrow is dead."

One day there was a baby who needed to find a special bed. He had to choose the best one of all. He looked around and saw a crib that was very sweet. It was painted with beautiful colors and decorated with lots of animals. 

He hopped into the crib to try it out and it was just the right size for him. He liked how comfortable and cozy it felt, so he decided to choose it. He smiled as he drifted off to sleep.

As the days went by, the baby learned how to roll over and start to stand up in his crib. He played lots of games and had lots of fun in it. He loved his new crib and it became the perfect home for him.

He was so happy to choose the sweet crib. It was the best choice he ever made!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sit on her porch and watch the birds fly by. One day, a bright blue bird landed on her porch. Lily was so happy to see the bird up close. 

"Hello, little birdie!" Lily said. 

The bird looked at Lily and chirped. Suddenly, the bird pinched Lily's finger. 

"Ouch! That hurt!" Lily said. 

The bird flew away, leaving Lily with a sore finger. But she still loved to sit on her porch and watch the birds fly by, even if they pinched her sometimes.

name_of_work: Anecdote of the Jar by Wallace Stevens
content: I placed a jar in Tennessee, And round it was, upon a hill. It made the slovenly wilderness Surround that hill. The wilderness rose up to it, And sprawled around, no longer wild. The jar was round upon the ground And tall and of a port in air. It took dominion everywhere. The jar was gray and bare. It did not give of bird or bush, Like nothing else in Tennessee.

Tom and Lily liked to play with the old round ball in the park. The ball was red and blue and had many patches. It was a gift from their grandpa, who said it was his favorite toy when he was a kid.

One day, a big dog came to the park and saw the ball. He ran to it and bit it hard. The ball made a loud pop and went flat. Tom and Lily were very sad and angry. They shouted at the dog and tried to get the ball back, but the dog ran away with it.

They ran after the dog, but he was too fast. They lost sight of him and the ball. They looked everywhere, but they could not find them. They asked some people and other kids, but no one had seen the dog or the ball.

They went back to the park and sat on a bench. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they could restore the ball and make it round and bouncy again. They missed their grandpa and his stories. They felt very lonely and hopeless.

They did not know that the dog had dropped the ball in a trash can, where it was buried under some garbage. They did not know that the next day, the trash truck would come and take the ball away forever. They did not know that they would never see their old round ball again.

Most men use their eyes like metronomes clicking off the beats of a woman's walk; how her lips press against the cloth, as figs before they split their purple skins on the tree, measuring how much of her walk goes into bed at night, the jar of the sky being filled with the Milky Way glittering for every time she moves her lips but of course the secrets are not the obvious beats in the song that even a bad drummer can play hearing the speed of the motor - it too made up of beats - so fast, subtle, I suppose, they register as continuous sound or the heart which of course beats without any fan belt to keep it cool. it is a test, a rhythm, they could not see with those measuring eyes though perhaps there are some whose fingers and ears are so close to the motors with clean oil passing through their ears and draining properly into the brain pan, perhaps a few... who can tell what the secret bleeding of a woman is all about As a woman with oily stars sticking on all the tip points of my skin I could never trust a man who wasn't a mechanic, a man who uses his eyes, his hands, listens to the heart.

One day, Joe and his mom decided to go for a walk outside. Joe saw a branch hanging from a nearby tree. He ran towards it and started to swing on it. Joe laughed and enjoyed it so much that mom decided to sack the branch. 

Joe was so excited that he could take the branch with him. To show it to his friends. He thought the branch was so popular! He couldn't wait to show it to them.

Joe was feeling so happy. He ran back to the house carrying the branch. His little sister, Sally, saw him and asked if she could have a go too. Joe said yes and they both started to swing on the branch.

They were having so much fun that they lost track of time. By the time they were done playing, it was almost dark. Joe and Sally put the branch back where they'd found it and went back home. 

Joe was still so happy that he'd gotten the chance to show his branch to everyone. He really loved that branch!

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Ms. Velvet. She was a regular girl who liked to have fun. One day, Ms. Velvet decided to go for a walk in the park. As she was walking, she heard something. It was a loud scream! Ms. Velvet was scared. She jumped back and looked around to figure out where the sound came from. It was coming from a big tree nearby. Ms. Velvet was very curious so she decided to take a closer look. When she got closer, she was shocked. It was a baby bird! The little bird had gotten stuck in a tree hole and couldn't escape! Ms. Velvet was so sad and she wanted to help the bird. She ran and got help from a grown-up. Together they were able to help the baby bird escape and it flew away. Ms. Velvet felt so happy and she smiled. Everyone was safe and regular again!

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very intelligent, so she wanted to go on a journey to learn more. She asked her parents if she could, but they said no. So she decided to go anyway.

Lucy's journey was long, but she didn't mind because she wanted to learn lots of things. She travelled for days and met new people. Everyone was so friendly and she learnt lots of things from them. 

Eventually, Lucy came to the end of her journey. She was very tired but happy. She had learnt a lot and felt very proud of herself. She knew that she was intelligent and all the new things she had learnt made her even smarter. She had had a wonderful journey and didn't regret a thing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing hide and seek. Lily was hiding behind a tree when she saw a bird lay an egg in a nest. Lily wondered how the egg got there.

Lily went to her friends and told them about the egg. Her friend Tommy said, "Let's go see the egg!" They ran to the tree and saw the egg in the nest. It was a messy nest with twigs and leaves everywhere. 

Lily said, "I wonder what kind of bird laid this egg?" Tommy said, "Maybe it's a robin or a blue jay." They sat there for a while, watching the egg and wondering what would happen next. Suddenly, they heard a chirping sound and saw a baby bird hatch from the egg. They were so happy to see the baby bird and couldn't wait to tell their parents about their adventure.

name_of_work: Verses upon the Burning of our House, July 10th, 1666 by Anne Bradstreet
content: In silent night when rest I took, For sorrow near I did not look, I wakened was with thund'ring noise And piteous shrieks of dreadful voice. That fearful sound of "fire" and "fire," Let no man know is my Desire. I, starting up, the light did spy, And to my God my heart did cry To straighten me in my Distress And not to leave me succourless. Then, coming out, behold a space The flame consume my dwelling place. And when I could no longer look, I blest His name that gave and took, That laid my goods now in the dust. Yea, so it was, and so 'twas just. It was his own, it was not mine, Far be it that I should repine; He might of all justly bereft But yet sufficient for us left. When by the ruins oft I past My sorrowing eyes aside did cast And here and there the places spy Where oft I sate and long did lie. Here stood that trunk, and there that chest, There lay that store I counted best. My pleasant things in ashes lie And them behold no more shall I. Under thy roof no guest shall sit, Nor at thy Table eat a bit. No pleasant talk shall 'ere be told Nor things recounted done of old. No Candle e'er shall shine in Thee, Nor bridegroom's voice e'er heard shall be. In silence ever shalt thou lie, Adieu, Adieu, all's vanity. Then straight I 'gin my heart to chide, And did thy wealth on earth abide? Didst fix thy hope on mould'ring dust? The arm of flesh didst make thy trust? Raise up thy thoughts above the sky That dunghill mists away may fly. Thou hast a house on high erect Frameed by that mighty Architect, With glory richly furnished, Stands permanent though this be fled. It's purchased and paid for too By Him who hath enough to do. A price so vast as is unknown, Yet by His gift is made thine own; There's wealth enough, I need no more, Farewell, my pelf, farewell, my store. The world no longer let me love, My hope and treasure lies above.

Pat spotted a big gray pit in the middle of the park. He decided to sit in it to read. Suddenly, the pit started to get deeper. Pat was stuck! 

Pat started meowing for help. Then he saw a dog. The dog said, â€œWhat are you doing down there, Pat?â€ Pat said, â€œI wanted to read in the sun. Can you help me get out?â€

David was a thoughtful painter. Every day he went to the park to paint the trees, birds and flowers. One day, he was so busy painting that he didn't notice the little boy slowly walking up to his canvas.

The little boy wanted to play and he took the brush in his hands. He started to paint with a reckless gesture and broke the brush on the canvas!

David saw the brush on the ground and was very sad. He looked at the little boy and said "Why did you break the brush?"

The little boy was so scared that he wanted to run away. But he stopped and said "I'm sorry. It was an accident. I didn't mean to break it."

David could see the sadness in the little boy's eyes. He thoughtfully put his hand on the little boy's shoulder and said "It's alright. Accidents happen." 

The little boy smiled and thanked David. They both went to the store to get a new brush and David showed him how to paint with it. They had a great time together.

name_of_work: We Wear the Mask by Paul Laurence Dunbar
content: We wear the mask that grins and lies, It hides our cheeks and shades our eyes,-- This debt we pay to human guile; With torn and bleeding hearts we smile, And mouth with myriad subtleties. Why should the world be over-wise, In counting all our tears and sighs? Nay, let them only see us, while We wear the mask. We smile, but, O great Christ, our cries To thee from tortured souls arise. We sing, but oh the clay is vile Beneath our feet, and long the mile; But let the world dream otherwise, We wear the mask!

My age fallen away like white swaddling Floats in the middle distance, becomes An inhabited cloud. I bend closer, discern A lighted tenement scuttling with voices. O you tall game I tired myself with joining! Now I wade through you like knee-level weeds, And they attend me, dear translucent bergs: Silence and space. By now so much has flown From the nest here of my head that I needs must turn To know what prints I leave, whether of feet, Or spoor of pads, or a bird's adept splay.

Once there was a very cheerful fox who liked to speed around the woods. He was so fast that no creature in the forest could match his pace.

One day he was running faster than ever. So fast that he bumped into a big tree and hurt himself.

The fox was in so much pain that he had to have an operation. He was so scared that he cried and cried. 

After the operation, the fox learnt a valuable lesson. He decided to slow down and be more careful when running around the forest. 

His friends and family were pleased that he was more careful when running from then on. They were careful and cautious but could still have fun and enjoy life.

name_of_work: Oh, the Places You'll Go! by Dr. Seuss
content: Congratulations! Today is your day. You're off to Great Places! You're off and away! You have brains in your head. You have feet in your shoes. You can steer yourself any direction you choose. You're on your own. And you know what you know. And YOU are the guy who'll decide where to go. You'll look up and down streets. Look 'em over with care. About some you will say, "I don't choose to go there." With your head full of brains and your shoes full of feet, you're too smart to go down any not-so-good street. And you may not find any you'll want to go down. In that case, of course, you'll head straight out of town. It's opener there in the wide open air. Out there things can happen and frequently do to people as brainy and footsy as you. And then things start to happen, don't worry. Don't stew. Just go right along. You'll start happening too. OH! THE PLACES YOU'LL GO! You'll be on y our way up! You'll be seeing great sights! You'll join the high fliers who soar to high heights. You won't lag behind, because you'll have the speed. You'll pass the whole gang and you'll soon take the lead. Wherever you fly, you'll be best of the best. Wherever you go, you will top all the rest. Except when you don't. Because, sometimes, you won't. I'm sorry to say so but, sadly, it's true that Bang-ups and Hang-ups can happen to you. You can get all hung up in a prickle-ly perch. And your gang will fly on. You'll be left in a Lurch. You'll come down from the Lurch with an unpleasant bump. And the chances are, then, that you'll be in a Slump. And when you're in a Slump, you're not in for much fun. Un-slumping yourself is not easily done. You will come to a place where the streets are not marked. Some windows are lighted. But mostly they're darked. A place you could sprain both your elbow and chin! Do you dare to stay out? Do you dare to go in? How much can you lose? How much can you win? And IF you go in, should you turn left or right... or right-and-three-quarters? Or, maybe, not quite? Or go around back and sneak in from behind? Simple it's not, I'm afraid you will find, for a mind-maker-upper to make up his mind. You can get so confused that you'll start in to race down long wiggled roads at a break-necking pace and grind on for miles cross weirdish wild space, headed, I fear, toward a most useless place. The Waiting Place... ...for people just waiting. Waiting for a train to go or a bus to come, or a plane to go or the mail to come, or the rain to go or the phone to ring, or the snow to snow or the waiting around for a Yes or No or waiting for their hair to grow. Everyone is just waiting. Waiting for the fish to bite or waiting for the wind to fly a kite or waiting around for Friday night or waiting, perhaps, for their Uncle Jake or a pot to boil, or a Better Break or a string of pearls, or a pair of pants or a wig with curls, or Another Chance. Everyone is just waiting. NO! That's not for you! Somehow you'll escape all that waiting and staying You'll find the bright places where Boom Bands are playing. With banner flip-flapping, once more you'll ride high! Ready for anything under the sky. Ready because you're that kind of a guy! Oh, the places you'll go! There is fun to be done! There are points to be scored. There are games to be won. And the magical things you can do with that ball will make you the winning-est winner of all. Fame! You'll be as famous as famous can be, with the whole wide world watching you win on TV. Except when they don't Because, sometimes they won't. I'm afraid that some times you'll play lonely games too. Games you can't win 'cause you'll play against you. All Alone! Whether you like it or not, Alone will be something you'll be quite a lot. And when you're alone, there's a very good chance you'll meet things that scare you right out of your pants. There are some, down the road between hither and yon, that can scare you so much you won't want to go on. But on you will go though the weather be foul. On you will go though your enemies prowl. On you will go though the Hakken-Kraks howl. Onward up many a frightening creek, though your arms may get sore and your sneakers may leak. On and on you will hike, And I know you'll hike far and face up to your problems whatever they are. You'll get mixed up, of course, as you already know. You'll get mixed up with many strange birds as you go. So be sure when you step. Step with care and great tact and remember that Life's a Great Balancing Act. Just never foget to be dexterous and deft. And never mix up your right foot with your left. And will you succeed? Yes! You will, indeed! (98 and 3/4 percent guaranteed.) KID, YOU'LL MOVE MOUNTAINS! So... be your name Buxbaum or Bixby or Bray or Mordecai Ali Van Allen O'Shea, You're off the Great Places! Today is your day! Your mountain is waiting. So...get on your way!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy yacht in the bathtub. One day, Timmy's sister came in and accidentally broke the toy yacht. Timmy was sad and cried.

"Why are you crying?" asked his sister.

"You broke my yacht," Timmy replied.

"I'm sorry. It was just an ordinary toy. I'll buy you a new one," said his sister.

Timmy smiled and hugged his sister. "Thank you," he said.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, John and Susan. Every day they would go for a walk, searching for new things to explore.

One day, they went to the park. As they were walking around, Susan stopped and said: "John, let's search for something!"

John was curious, so he said: "Let's do it!"

Together they started exploring and searching for interesting things. After a while, they finally found a point. It was a fair point, with stones and small river flowing over it.

Suddenly, Susan said: "Let's play a game here. Whoever finds the most fair things wins!" 

John thought it was a great idea, so they started their search. After 15 minutes, they both realized they had found enough things to make the winner. 

John said: "Susan, you have found the most fair things, so you are the winner!"

Susan was very happy and said: "Thank you, John, for a fun day of searching and exploring together!"

name_of_work: Only a Dad by Edgar Albert Guest
content: Only a dad, with a tired face, Coming home from the daily race, Bringing little of gold or fame, To show how well he has played the game, But glad in his heart that his own rejoice To see him come, and to hear his voice. Only a dad, with a brood of four, One of ten million men or more. Plodding along in the daily strife, Bearing the whips and the scorns of life, With never a whimper of pain or hate, For the sake of those who at home await. Only a dad, neither rich nor proud, Merely one of the surging crowd Toiling, striving from day to day, Facing whatever may come his way, Silent, whenever the harsh condemn, And bearing it all for the love of them. Only a dad, but he gives his all To smooth the way for his children small, Doing, with courage stern and grim, The deeds that his father did for him. This is the line that for him I pen, Only a dad, but the best of men.

name_of_work: Life is Fine by Langston Hughes
content: I went down to the river, I set down on the bank. I tried to think but couldn't, So I jumped in and sank. I came up once and hollered! I came up twice and cried! If that water hadn't a-been so cold I might've sunk and died. But it was Cold in that water! It was cold! I took the elevator Sixteen floors above the ground. I thought about my baby And thought I would jump down. I stood there and I hollered! I stood there and I cried! If it hadn't a-been so high I might've jumped and died. But it was High up there! It was high! So since I'm still here livin', I guess I will live on. I could've died for love-- But for livin' I was born Though you may hear me holler, And you may see me cry-- I'll be dogged, sweet baby, If you gonna see me die. Life is fine! Fine as wine! Life is fine!

Once upon a time, there was a fat bear. He lived in a forest with a lot of trees and animals. One day the bear was feeling very hungry. He looked around for something to eat and saw a long rope. He grabbed it with his big claws and took a big bite. The rope tasted bad and the bear's mouth started to hurt. He quickly let go and knew that he should have stayed away from it. 

The bear decided to look for something else to eat. He found a fat apple tree just a few steps away and started to eat the apples. He ate and ate until he was full. The bear was happy and content. He decided to take a rope for himself the next time he went on an adventure. 

The end.

name_of_work: Confusion of the Senses by Kenneth Rexroth
content: Moonlight fills the laurels Like music. The moonlit Air does not move. Your white Face moves towards my face. Voluptuous sorrow Holds us like a cobweb Like a song, a perfume, the moonlight. Your hair falls and holds our faces. Your lips curl into mine. Your tongue enters my mouth. A bat flies through the moonlight. The moonlight fills your eyes They have neither iris nor pupil They are only globes of cold fire Like the deers' eyes that go by us Through the empty forest. Your slender body quivers And smells of seaweed. We lie together listening To each other breathing in the moonlight. Do you hear? We are breathing. We are alive.

Once on a dark night, Tom was walking in the woods by himself. He was feeling fearless until he heard a mysterious sound coming from behind the trees. He stopped and listened. The sound was like a rail reverberating in the distance. Tom, feeling scared, started walking faster. Suddenly, he heard the sound of the rail coming closer. Tom was so scared he ran, making his way back home. 

When he finally stopped running, Tom looked behind and he saw a mysterious figure standing there. Tom was so scared he froze. The figure was so tall and with a very strange look he could barely move. The figure started walking closer, and Tom tried to run away but he could not. Just at that moment, the figure spoke, and he said: "I will be back soon." 

Tom was paralyzed with fear, but he still ran as fast as he could. He ran for a long time, until he arrived back home. Unfortunately, Tom never forgot that mysterious figure. The figure still scared him, even after all this time. He was often worried that one day the figure would return, just as the figure had promised. Sadly, Tom was right and the figure eventually returned, making Tom's story have a bad ending.

name_of_work: As I Grew Older by Langston Hughes
content: It was a long time ago. I have almost forgotten my dream. But it was there then, In front of me, Bright like a sun,-- My dream. And then the wall rose, Rose slowly, Slowly, Between me and my dream. Rose slowly, slowly, Dimming, Hiding, The light of my dream. Rose until it touched the sky,-- The wall. Shadow. I am black. I lie down in the shadow. No longer the light of my dream before me, Above me. Only the thick wall. Only the shadow. My hands! My dark hands! Break through the wall! Find my dream! Help me to shatter this darkness, To smash this night, To break this shadow Into a thousand lights of sun, Into a thousand whirling dreams Of sun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to laugh and play. She loved to laugh so much that she could laugh for hours.

One day, she was so tired and sleepy, she decided to take a nap. She yawned a big, big yawn. She snuggled into her bed, which was a big, purple bed made out of soft, yummy fabric.

"What a nice bed," she said to herself. But then, she noticed something strange. She could hear something coming from the bed.

She listened carefully and heard a loud, deep yawn. She quickly realized that there was a giant, purple bear hidden inside her bed. She was so surprised that she couldn't help but laugh.

The bear laughed too, and they both yawned together. They shared lots of stories and laughed and played until the sun went down.

At the end of the day, they hugged each other goodbye. From that day forward, they would always be the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the park. The sun was shining bright and the sky was blue. Lily saw a big puddle on the ground. It was wet and brown.
