Lily was so happy to have discovered the little frog. She picked it up gently and brought it home. She put the frog in a jar with some water and watched it jump around. From that day on, Lily loved going on adventures and discovering new things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a long cane that she liked to play with. One day, her mother told her they were going on a trip and she needed to pack her things. Lily was excited and quickly packed her favorite toys and clothes.

As they were walking to the car, Lily noticed she had forgotten her long cane. She asked her mother if she could go back and get it but her mother said they didn't have time. Lily was sad but she didn't want to be late for their trip.

When they arrived at their destination, Lily realized she had left something important behind. She asked her mother if they could go back and get it but her mother said it was too late. Lily started to cry and wished she had packed her long cane.

The announcement Swung blunt as an axe-blow: All students were to leave Campus as soon as possible. We think we cried, Our brains bleached blank. We were already trying to forget What we would live. What we would give. * * * Beware the ides of March. We recognized that something ran Rampant as a rumor Among our ranks. Cases bleeding closer, Like spillage in a napkin. There is nothing more worrisome Than a titan who believes itself Separate from the world. * * * Graduation day. We don't need a gown. We don't need a stage. We are walking beside our ancestors, Their drums roar for us, Their feet stomp at our life. There is power in being robbed & still choosing to dance.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide and wanted to play on it. Tom ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. Lily followed him, but she was slower.

"Me first, me first!" Tom shouted. He sat on the slide and pushed himself down. He went very fast and felt happy.

"Wait for me, Tom!" Lily cried. She reached the top of the ladder and looked for a place to sit. But there was a big boy on the other side of the slide. He had a mean face and an ugly hat. He looked at Lily and said, "This is my slide. Go away, you little baby!"

Lily felt scared and sad. She did not want to go away. She wanted to slide with Tom. She said, "No, this is not your slide. This is for everyone. Please let me slide."

The big boy did not listen. He pushed Lily off the ladder and made her fall. Lily hurt her knee and started to cry.

Tom heard Lily cry and saw what happened. He was angry and brave. He rushed to the big boy and said, "You are very bad and mean. You should not push my sister. You should say sorry and go away."

The big boy was surprised and scared. He did not expect Tom to stand up for Lily. He said, "Sorry, sorry, I was just joking. I will go away now."

Tom helped Lily up and hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. You are not a baby. You are my sister and I love you. Let's slide together."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom. You are my brother and I love you too. Let's slide together."

They slid down the slide and had fun. Their mom saw them and was proud of them. She said, "You are very good and kind, Tom and Lily. You know how to share and care. I love you both very much."

name_of_work: Song for Lonely Roads by Sherwood Anderson
content: Now let us understand each other, love, Long time ago I crept off home, To my own gods I went. The tale is old, It has been told By many men in many lands. The lands belong to those who tell. Now surely that is clear. After the plow had westward swept, The gods bestowed the corn to stand. Long, long it stood, Strong, strong it grew, To make a forest for new song. Deep in the corn the bargain hard Youth with the gods drove home. The gods remember, Youth forgets. Doubt not the soul of song that waits. The singer dies, The singer lives, The gods wait in the corn, The soul of song is in the land. Lift up your lips to that.

Once upon a time, there was a large lake. In the middle of the lake was a beautiful palm tree. Every morning, a little duck would swim in the lake and go up to the palm tree. Every afternoon, the duck's friends would come to the lake, and they would all swim around the large palm tree. They played games in the lake and had lots of fun. The days were so sunny and the lake was so blueâ€”it was a perfect place to swim. 

One day, the duck's friends found a large shell. They showed it to the duck and said, "Let's make a game with this shell!" And so, the duck, its friends and the large shell made their own game. They would swim around the palm tree and when they found the shell, they had to go back to the beginning. It was the best game they'd ever seen!

The happy duck, its friends and the large shell continued to play the game every day. Sometimes they even invited baby ducks so they could learn how to swim. Life was good in the beautiful lake with the large palm tree, and everyone was so happy.

One day, Laura was playing outside. She looked up at the sky and saw so many clouds. Suddenly, one of the clouds spoke to her!

"Hello Laura!" said the cloud.

"Hi!" said Laura, surprised. 

"I'm a special cloud. Do you want to come to my cloud party?" asked the cloud.

"Yes!" said Laura.

The cloud smiled and said, "Let's go!"

Laura and the cloud flew up to the sky. When they arrived at the party, Laura saw lots of other clouds having fun. Suddenly she noticed something.

"Those clouds look fake," whispered Laura. 

The cloud laughed and said, "They are! We invited them because we wanted to make the party better. Now let's have some fun!"

And they did. Laura and the cloud played games, laughed and had an amazing time. 

Before Laura knew it, it was time to go home. The cloud hugged her and said goodbye. Laura flew back home with a smile on her face.

name_of_work: The River by Ralph Waldo Emerson
content: And I behold once more My old familiar haunts; here the blue river, The same blue wonder that my infant eye Admired, sage doubting whence the traveller came,-- Whence brought his sunny bubbles ere he washed The fragrant flag-roots in my father's fields, And where thereafter in the world he went. Look, here he is, unaltered, save that now He hath broke his banks and flooded all the vales With his redundant waves. Here is the rock where, yet a simple child, I caught with bended pin my earliest fish, Much triumphing, --and these the fields Over whose flowers I chased the butterfly, A blooming hunter of a fairy fine. And hark! where overhead the ancient crows Hold their sour conversation in the sky:-- These are the same, but I am not the same, But wiser than I was, and wise enough Not to regret the changes, tho' they cost Me many a sigh. Oh, call not Nature dumb; These trees and stones are audible to me, These idle flowers, that tremble in the wind, I understand their faery syllables, And all their sad significance. The wind, That rustles down the well-known forest road-- It hath a sound more eloquent than speech. The stream, the trees, the grass, the sighing wind, All of them utter sounds of 'monishment And grave parental love. They are not of our race, they seem to say, And yet have knowledge of our moral race, And somewhat of majestic sympathy, Something of pity for the puny clay, That holds and boasts the immeasurable mind. I feel as I were welcome to these trees After long months of weary wandering, Acknowledged by their hospitable boughs; They know me as their son, for side by side, They were coeval with my ancestors, Adorned with them my country's primitive times, And soon may give my dust their funeral shade.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big smile and loved to play outside. One day, she went to her backyard and saw that the lawn was very long. It was not pretty, it was poor.

But Lily didn't mind. She started to skip around the lawn, and she felt happy. She loved to skip and feel the wind in her hair. As she skipped, she saw a butterfly flying around. It was so pretty! Lily wanted to catch it, but it flew away.

Even though the lawn was poor, Lily had fun skipping around. She knew that she didn't need fancy things to be happy. She just needed to play and have fun.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. Tom loved to play outside. He had a special suit he always wore when outside.

One day, Tom was out playing when he met an old man. The old man looked at Tom and said: "Where are you going little one? Why are you wearing that suit?" 
Tom answered: "I'm playing outside. I like my special suit!" 

The old man smiled and said: "That's nice. Can you tell me a secret?" Tom thought for a minute and then said: "I like to keep it quiet." 

The old man laughed and said: "I like that! Keep it quiet, but don't forget to have fun!" Tom smiled and said: "I will!" and he went happily on his way.

Once there was a little boy who did something very naughty. He was feeling so sad and bad about what he had done, but he knew he had to tell his mum. After taking a deep breath, he told her about it and waited for her to be angry. Instead, his mum told him she was disappointed but that he should forgive himself. He looked up at her, surprised by her kind words.

They went together to the station and sat there. The little boy was feeling uncomfortable and didn't want to move. But his mum's loving arms were warm and comforting, so he started to feel better.

When they got back home, Mum hugged the little boy tightly and said "I forgive you" and suddenly everything felt right again. The little boy knew that it would be hard for him to forgive himself, but he was so happy that his mum had done it for him.

One day, a little dog hurt his leg while playing. He felt very sad and cried. His friend, a big cat, saw him and wanted to help. The cat knew she could support the dog and make him feel better.

The cat found a bandage to put on the dog's leg. She carefully wrapped it around his leg. The dog felt better and was grateful for the cat's help. They both smiled and were happy.

But then, a naughty bird came and tried to take the bandage off the dog's leg. The cat and the dog worked together to stop the bird. They chased the bird away and saved the bandage. The dog and the cat were proud of their teamwork and stayed best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who loved to eat yummy treats. She had one special treat, sweet jam filled cookie, that she loved the most.

One day, Sarah was playing in the park when she saw a giant cookie almost as big as her knee. She said "Wow, that cookie looks yummy!"

A voice from behind her said "Do you think you can fit that cookie in your mouth?" 

Sarah wasn't sure. She said, "I'm not sure. Can I try?"

The voice said "Yes, of course you can try. Go ahead!"

Sarah was so excited. She opened wide and took a big bite. Sure enough, it fit perfectly! She said "Yummy! This is my favorite treat ever!" and she ate up the whole cookie.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with toys and eat snacks. One day, Tom has a new toy. It is a big bear. It is soft and brown. Tom is happy.

"Look, Lily, this is my new toy. His name is Ben. He is very soft and nice. Do you want to play with him?" Tom says.

Lily looks at the bear. She wants the bear. She thinks it is better than her toys. She is not happy.

"Can I have him? He is so soft and cute. I want him more than you. Give him to me!" Lily says.

Tom is shocked. He loves his bear. He does not want to give him to Lily. He is angry.

"No, Lily, you cannot have him. He is mine. I got him from my mom. You have your own toys. Go away!" Tom says.

Lily is mad. She does not listen to Tom. She grabs the bear from his arms. She runs away with him. Tom cries. He chases after her.

"Give him back, Lily, give him back! He is my bear, not yours!" Tom shouts.

But Lily is faster. She runs to her house. She slams the door. She locks it. She hugs the bear. She smiles.

"I have him now. He is mine. I do not care about Tom. He is a bad friend. I do not need him. I only need Ben. He is my new friend." Lily says.

Tom is sad. He knocks on the door. He begs Lily to open it. He wants his bear back. He wants his friend back. But Lily does not answer. She does not care. She ignores him. She plays with the bear.

Tom goes home. He is alone. He has no bear. He has no friend. He is unhappy. He cries. He wishes he never introduced Lily to Ben. He wishes he never met Lily. He wishes he had a different friend. A friend who would share and care. A friend who would not take his bear. A friend who would not break his heart.

"Look, Mamma!" exclaimed three-year-old Sophie. She had just spotted a lovely castle with an even lovelier garden. "Let's go explore! Please, please, please can we go?" Sophie begged.

Mamma smiled. "Of course," she said.

As they neared the entrance, Sophie saw a group of cleaners bustling around and polishing the walls of the castle. She reached out to touch one of the stone walls, but Mamma stopped her. "No Sophie," she said. "The cleaners are working hard to make this castle look perfect, and we must not get in the way."

Sophie felt disappointed, but stood back and watched as the cleaners continued to clean. The cleaners worked for hours and finally, their victory was complete. The castle looked splendid, even more lovely than before.

Suddenly, a wave of excitement ran through the crowd. Mamma had an announcement to make. "Today, the castle is now open! All of you have worked so hard, and your work has achieved a great victory." Everyone cheered, and all the cleaners were handed a medal, as a symbol of their victory.

Sophie clapped and cheered, feeling joy and admiration for the hard-working cleaners. She was so glad to be a part of such a lovely victory.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world. One day, she went inside her house and saw her mommy hanging a pretty curtain in the living room. Lily thought it was incredible and wanted to touch it. 

But, her mommy told her not to touch the curtain because it could spoil the pretty design. Lily didn't want to spoil it, so she promised to be careful. 

Later, Lily's friend came over to play. They had so much fun together, but they accidentally knocked over a vase and water spilled everywhere. Lily was worried that the water would spoil the pretty curtain, so she quickly grabbed towels to clean it up. Her mommy was so proud of her for being responsible and taking care of the curtain. From that day on, Lily made sure to always be careful around the incredible curtain.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She loved playing with water and having lots of fun. One day, Anna went to the park with her mum.

Anna had a special toy - it was a big yellow duck. Anna decided to have a splash with her duck. She threw it into the big pond and it landed in the water with a big splash!

Anna laughed as the water splashed up around her. She watched as the duck swam around. Then she spotted something else in the pond - a fashion show. Lots of little ducks had gathered together and they were strutting around the pond.

Anna couldn't believe it - the ducks were so fashion-forward! They were wearing tiny hats, bow ties and polka dot scarves. It was so fun to watch the ducks competing against each other.

And that's how Anna spent her day - with her duck, having a splash in the big pond and watching the fashion show!

Sara likes to play with her computer. She can make pictures and sounds and games on it. But sometimes the computer is not nice. It makes noises and says things Sara does not understand. Sara gets sad and angry.

One day, Sara is playing with her computer when it stops working. It shows a blue screen with white words. Sara does not know what it means. She tries to make it go away, but it does not. She pushes the buttons and taps the screen, but nothing happens. She cries and calls for her mom.

Mom comes and sees the computer. She knows what the problem is. She says, "Sara, you have to be careful with your computer. You cannot push too many buttons at once. You can make it crash. That means it cannot work anymore. You need to help it restart. Do you know how to do that?"

Sara shakes her head. She does not know how to restart the computer. She feels foolish. She thinks she broke the computer. She says, "I'm sorry, mom. I did not mean to break it. I just wanted to play. Can you fix it?"

Mom smiles and hugs Sara. She says, "It's okay, Sara. You did not break it. You just made a mistake. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. I can help you fix it. Look, there is a button on the side of the computer. It is called the power button. If you press it and hold it for a few seconds, the computer will turn off. Then you can press it again and the computer will turn on. That is how you restart it. Do you want to try?"

Sara nods. She wants to try. She follows mom's instructions and presses the power button. The blue screen goes away. The computer turns off. She waits for a moment and presses the power button again. The computer turns on. It shows a picture of a cat and says, "Hello, Sara. Welcome back." Sara is happy. She says, "Thank you, mom. You helped me fix the computer. You are smart. I love you."

Mom says, "You're welcome, Sara. You helped too. You are brave. I love you too." They hug and kiss. Then they play with the computer together. They have fun. They are happy.

name_of_work: The Naming Of Cats by T. S. Eliot
content: The Naming of Cats is a difficult matter, It isn't just one of your holiday games; You may think at first I'm as mad as a hatter When I tell you, a cat must have THREE DIFFERENT NAMES. First of all, there's the name that the family use daily, Such as Peter, Augustus, Alonzo or James, Such as Victor or Jonathan, George or Bill Bailey-- All of them sensible everyday names. There are fancier names if you think they sound sweeter, Some for the gentlemen, some for the dames: Such as Plato, Admetus, Electra, Demeter-- But all of them sensible everyday names. But I tell you, a cat needs a name that's particular, A name that's peculiar, and more dignified, Else how can he keep up his tail perpendicular, Or spread out his whiskers, or cherish his pride? Of names of this kind, I can give you a quorum, Such as Munkustrap, Quaxo, or Coricopat, Such as Bombalurina, or else Jellylorum- Names that never belong to more than one cat. But above and beyond there's still one name left over, And that is the name that you never will guess; The name that no human research can discover-- But THE CAT HIMSELF KNOWS, and will never confess. When you notice a cat in profound meditation, The reason, I tell you, is always the same: His mind is engaged in a rapt contemplation Of the thought, of the thought, of the thought of his name: His ineffable effable Effanineffable Deep and inscrutable singular Name.

name_of_work: Loving you less than life, a little less by Edna St. Vincent Millay
content: Loving you less than life, a little less Than bitter-sweet upon a broken wall Or brush-wood smoke in autumn, I confess I cannot swear I love you not at all. For there is that about you in this light-- A yellow darkness, sinister of rain-- Which sturdily recalls my stubborn sight To dwell on you, and dwell on you again. And I am made aware of many a week I shall consume, remembering in what way Your brown hair grows about your brow and cheek And what divine absurdities you say: Till all the world, and I, and surely you, Will know I love you, whether or not I do.

name_of_work: The Hill Fort (Y Gaer) by Owen Sheers
content: On a clear day he'd bring him here, his young son, charging the hill as wild as the long-maned ponies who'd watch a moment before dropping their heads to graze again. When he finally got him still he'd crouch so their eyes were level, one hand on the small of his back the other tracing the horizon, pointing out all the places lived in by the fathers and sons before them: Tretower, Raglan, Bredwardine ... And what he meant by this but never said, was 'Look. Look over this land and see how long the line is before you - how in these generations were no more than scattered grains; that from here in this view 9, 19, 90 years are much the same ... that it isn't the number of steps that will matter but the depth of their impression; And that's why he's come back again to tip these ashes onto the tongues of the wind and watch them spindrift into the night. Not just to make the circle complete, to heal or mend, but because he knows these walls, sunk however low, still hold him in as well as out protect as much as they defend.

When I see a couple of kids And guess he's fucking her and she's Taking pills or wearing a diaphragm, I know this is paradise Everyone old has dreamed of all their lives-- Bonds and gestures pushed to one side Like an outdated combine harvester, And everyone young going down the long slide To happiness, endlessly. I wonder if Anyone looked at me, forty years back, And thought, That'll be the life; No God any more, or sweating in the dark About hell and that, or having to hide What you think of the priest. He And his lot will all go down the long slide Like free bloody birds. And immediately Rather than words comes the thought of high windows: The sun-comprehending glass, And beyond it, the deep blue air, that shows Nothing, and is nowhere, and is endless.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sara. She was three years old and loved to play on the playground. Every day, she went to the playground and played on the slide.

One day when she was playing, her mom called her. "Sara, time to go home!", her mom said. But Sara refused to go home. She wanted to keep playing on the slide.

"Mommy, please! I don't want to go home!", said Sara.

"OK, one more turn on the slide and then you have to go home," said her mom. Sara agreed and went down the slide one last time.

When she got to the bottom, she was sorry. She wished she had stayed and played a little bit longer. But her mom said it was time to go home.

Sara hugged her mom and said goodbye to the slide. She learned that it was sometimes important to listen to your mom.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy wanted some juice. He asked his mommy for some, and she gave him a cup of smooth juice. Timmy loved the juice and drank it all up. 

After he finished his juice, Timmy wanted to record a video of himself playing with his toys. He asked his mommy to help him, and she gave him her phone. Timmy was so happy and started to record himself playing. 

But then, Timmy accidentally dropped the phone and it broke. His mommy was very upset because she needed her phone for work. Timmy felt bad and started to cry. 

From that day on, Timmy learned to be more careful with other people's things. And his mommy learned to keep her phone away from Timmy's reach. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a fair mouse. Every day, the mouse had so much to do! She had to find food, build her house, and find a friend.

One day, the mouse was walking through the forest when she heard a sound coming from a nearby bush. "Who's there?" called the mouse.

"It's me!" answered a small voice. 

The mouse looked around and saw a little frog. "Hi there," said the mouse. "My name is Mouse. What's yours?"

"I'm Frog," said Frog. "I'm looking for something to wrap my presents in." 

"I have just the thing," said Mouse. She took a few pieces of soft leaves and some twigs and helped Frog create a beautiful wrap for his presents.

Afterward, Frog thanked Mouse for her help and the two said goodbye. They were content in knowing they had made a new fair friend.

Once there was a little girl and all she wanted to do was play with her new toy, a tank. Every day she would take it out, and she would make different silly noises and repeat them all. Her mum would always laugh and giggle at her while she played.

One day, the little girl was playing with her tank outside and she couldn't stop repeating the silly noises she was making. Soon, all the animals in the neighbourhood started joining in and making their own silly noises too.

The little girl was so excited, she laughed and waved her arms around with joy. She kept repeating her noises and all the animals kept copying her. Everyone was having so much fun.

Then, suddenly, it started to rain. The little girl ran inside with her tank, but she could still hear her friends outside repeating the silly noises. She smiled and knew she would be able to play with them again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a heavy backpack full of toys. He was walking in the park when he saw a squirrel. The squirrel was eating nuts and Timmy thought it was funny. 

"Hello, Mr. Squirrel!" said Timmy.

"Hello, Timmy. What are you doing today?" asked the squirrel.

"I'm walking in the park with my heavy backpack. What are you doing?"

"I'm eating nuts. They're yummy!" said the squirrel.

Suddenly, a loud noise scared the squirrel. It was a big dog that wanted to catch the squirrel. The squirrel tried to escape, but the dog was too fast. Timmy saw the dog and he wanted to help the squirrel. 

"Run, Mr. Squirrel, run!" shouted Timmy.

The squirrel ran away and the dog couldn't catch him. Timmy felt happy and proud. "My brain is so smart," he said to himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing football, it was his favourite thing to do. One day, Timmy's friends asked him to play football with them but Timmy said he couldn't because he had to clean his room. His friends said they would help him but Timmy said no, he wanted to do it himself.

So Timmy rushed to clean his room as fast as he could. He didn't want to waste any time because he wanted to play football with his friends. When he finished, he ran to the park to play with his friends. They had a lovely time playing together.

The moral of the story is that it's important to do your chores before you play. It might feel like a rush to skip them, but it's always better to do them first.

Once upon a time there was a knight galloping through the kingdom on his brave horse. He was on an important mission to protect the shy princess. As he galloped closer to the castle, he heard a cry for help coming from a small, scared voice.

The knight dismounted his horse and shouted, "I am here to help you!" When he reached the source of the voice he saw a small dragon, hunched and quaking against the wall.

The knight took out his shield and told the dragon not to worry. He promised that the princess was safe and he would help the dragon too. The dragon was so relieved and thanked the knight with a big hug.

But, before the knight left, he said something very important in a calm voice, "Always remember, when you feel scared, no matter who you are or what you're facing, you can always call for help."

The dragon nodded and waved goodbye to the knight as he rode away. The knight was happy knowing he had given the scared dragon some sound advice. He was sorry he hadn't arrived earlier but he had taught the dragon an important lesson - never be afraid to call for help.

name_of_work: A Time to Talk by Robert Frost
content: When a friend calls to me from the road And slows his horse to a meaning walk, I don't stand still and look around On all the hills I haven't hoed, And shout from where I am, What is it? No, not as there is a time to talk. I thrust my hoe in the mellow ground, Blade-end up and five feet tall, And plod: I go up to the stone wall For a friendly visit.

name_of_work: Part IV: The Rime of The Ancient Mariner by S.T. Coleridge
content: I fear thee, ancient Mariner! I fear thy skinny hand! And thou art long, and lank, and brown, As is the ribbed sea-sand. I fear thee and thy glittering eye, And thy skinny hand, so brown.'-- Fear not, fear not, thou Wedding-Guest! This body dropt not down. Alone, alone, all, all alone, Alone on a wide wide sea! And never a saint took pity on My soul in agony. The many men, so beautiful! And they all dead did lie: And a thousand thousand slimy things Lived on; and so did I. I looked upon the rotting sea, And drew my eyes away; I looked upon the rotting deck, And there the dead men lay. I looked to heaven, and tried to pray; But or ever a prayer had gusht, A wicked whisper came, and made My heart as dry as dust. I closed my lids, and kept them close, And the balls like pulses beat; For the sky and the sea, and the sea and the sky Lay dead like a load on my weary eye, And the dead were at my feet. The cold sweat melted from their limbs, Nor rot nor reek did they: The look with which they looked on me Had never passed away. An orphan's curse would drag to hell A spirit from on high; But oh! more horrible than that Is the curse in a dead man's eye! Seven days, seven nights, I saw that curse, And yet I could not die. The moving Moon went up the sky, And no where did abide: Softly she was going up, And a star or two beside-- Her beams bemocked the sultry main, Like April hoar-frost spread; But where the ship's huge shadow lay, The charmed water burnt alway A still and awful red. Beyond the shadow of the ship, I watched the water-snakes: They moved in tracks of shining white, And when they reared, the elfish light Fell off in hoary flakes. Within the shadow of the ship I watched their rich attire: Blue, glossy green, and velvet black, They coiled and swam; and every track Was a flash of golden fire. O happy living things! no tongue Their beauty might declare: A spring of love gushed from my heart, And I blessed them unaware: Sure my kind saint took pity on me, And I blessed them unaware. The self-same moment I could pray; And from my neck so free The Albatross fell off, and sank Like lead into the sea.

One day, Daisy was playing in her garden when she saw something very bright in the sky. It was a big, beautiful rainbow! Daisy was so excited that she wanted to reach out and hold it.

"Mummy, look!" Daisy shouted. "There's a rainbow!"

Mummy smiled and said, "Yes, let's go and hold it!"

So Daisy and Mummy walked towards the rainbow, but then a storm began to roll in. Daisy was scared, so Mummy held her tight.

The storm was loud, but Daisy was brave and held her mother's hand. They kept walking until the storm had passed and the rainbow was still there.

Daisy smiled and said, "Let's go and hold it now!"

Mummy smiled and said, "Ok, let's go!"

The two of them ran towards the rainbow and held it as tight as they could. Then, suddenly, the rainbow was gone and Daisy and Mummy were filled with wonder and joy.

The end!

SINGING. BUILDING. LAUGHING. LEARNING. LOVING. TEACHING. BEING. Hey. Brother/Brotha. Sister/Sista. Here is my hand. Catch the fire...and live. live. livelivelive. livelivelive. live. live.

name_of_work: Tonight I Can Write by Pablo Neruda
content: Tonight I can write the saddest lines. Write, for example, 'The night is starry and the stars are blue and shiver in the distance.' The night wind revolves in the sky and sings. Tonight I can write the saddest lines. I loved her, and sometimes she loved me too. Through nights like this one I held her in my arms. I kissed her again and again under the endless sky. She loved me, sometimes I loved her too. How could one not have loved her great still eyes. Tonight I can write the saddest lines. To think that I do not have her. To feel that I have lost her. To hear the immense night, still more immense without her. And the verse falls to the soul like dew to the pasture. What does it matter that my love could not keep her. The night is starry and she is not with me. This is all. In the distance someone is singing. In the distance. My soul is not satisfied that it has lost her. My sight tries to find her as though to bring her closer. My heart looks for her, and she is not with me. The same night whitening the same trees. We, of that time, are no longer the same. I no longer love her, that's certain, but how I loved her. My voice tried to find the wind to touch her hearing. Another's. She will be another's. As she was before my kisses. Her voice, her bright body. Her infinite eyes. I no longer love her, that's certain, but maybe I love her. Love is so short, forgetting is so long. Because through nights like this one I held her in my arms my soul is not satisfied that it has lost her. Though this be the last pain that she makes me suffer and these the last verses that I write for her.

Robbie was so excited to go for a walk outside with his Mom. His Mom said he could skip as much as he wanted! Robbie loved skipping and ran ahead.

Suddenly, he was stopped by a tall fence. He tried to peek over but it was way too tall. Robbie looked around and seen a small opening in the fence. On the other side Robbie could see the gardens and tall trees.

Robbie listened to his Mom and they skipped down the road until they found a safe place to enter the gardens. They had so much fun exploring and skipping through the gardens.

Sammy saw something cute across the room. He knew he had to get it so he started to slip but his mom saw him. He tried to find an exit but there wasn't one! His mom was getting closer and closer. name_of_work: My Mother at Sixty-Six by Kamala Das
content: Driving from my parent's home to Cochin last Friday morning, I saw my mother, beside me, doze, open mouthed, her face ashen like that of a corpse and realised with pain that she was as old as she looked but soon put that thought away, and looked out at Young Trees sprinting, the merry children spilling out of their homes, but after the airport's security check, standing a few yards away, I looked again at her, wan, pale as a late winter's moon and felt that old familiar ache, my childhood's fear, but all I said was, see you soon, Amma, all I did was smile and smile and smile......

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a baby. Mommy had a bucket. It was very heavy. When Mommy looked inside the bucket, it had lots of water. There was so much! Mommy stirred it with a spoon and then she brought it outside.

When Mommy put the bucket down, she saw a result. The water from the bucket made the ground wet. It was all around the bucket. Mommy was so happy!

Then, she asked the baby to help. The baby got a small bucket and scooped some of the wet ground into it. Then they both went back into the house. They put the water and wet ground in a small pot. They made some soup! 

That was the result of mommy and baby's hard work. They enjoyed the soup and made sure not to waste any of it. And that is the end of the story.

Mommy: "What are you doing, honey?"

Boy: "I want to quit."

name_of_work: How I Discovered Poetry by Marilyn Nelson
content: It was like soul-kissing, the way the words filled my mouth as Mrs. Purdy read from her desk. All the other kids zoned an hour ahead to 3:15, but Mrs. Purdy and I wandered lonely as clouds borne by a breeze off Mount Parnassus. She must have seen the darkest eyes in the room brim: The next day she gave me a poem she'd chosen especially for me to read to the all except for me white class. She smiled when she told me to read it, smiled harder, said oh yes I could. She smiled harder and harder until I stood and opened my mouth to banjo playing darkies, pickaninnies, disses and dats. When I finished my classmates stared at the floor. We walked silent to the buses, awed by the power of words.

One day, a boy named Jamie was restless and wanted to go outside and play. The sky was dark and it started to rain. Jamie's mom said he couldn't go out so he had to stay inside. Jamie didn't like this and he started to cry. He ran to the garage to hide from his mom.

Jamie went further into the garage, trying to find something to play with. Suddenly, he noticed a door with a large handle. He opened the door and peered inside. He saw a big hole with a ladder going down into it. He thought it would be fun to explore. So, he climbed down the ladder into the darkness.

Jamie kept going down further and further. After a while, he noticed that he was getting colder. He started to get scared and tried to climb back up the ladder. But he couldn't find it. He was stuck in the darkness and the rain was coming down harder.

Jamie stayed there until his mom and dad noticed that he was missing. After a frantic search, they found him in the garage, shaking and scared. Jamie's mom and dad were very sad and angry. Jamie learned his lesson and will never sneak off again.

name_of_work: A Valediction: of Weeping by John Donne
content: Let me pour forth My tears before thy face, whilst I stay here, For thy face coins them, and thy stamp they bear, And by this mintage they are something worth, For thus they be Pregnant of thee; Fruits of much grief they are, emblems of more, When a tear falls, that thou falls which it bore, So thou and I are nothing then, when on a diverse shore. On a round ball A workman that hath copies by, can lay An Europe, Afric, and an Asia, And quickly make that, which was nothing, all; So doth each tear Which thee doth wear, A globe, yea world, by that impression grow, Till thy tears mix'd with mine do overflow This world; by waters sent from thee, my heaven dissolved so. O more than moon, Draw not up seas to drown me in thy sphere, Weep me not dead, in thine arms, but forbear To teach the sea what it may do too soon; Let not the wind Example find, To do me more harm than it purposeth; Since thou and I sigh one another's breath, Whoe'er sighs most is cruellest, and hastes the other's death.
