Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. He liked to go on adventures and explore new places. One day, he met a little bird who wanted to go on an adventure too. The bear said, "Let's go on an adventure together!" and the bird said, "Yes, let's go!"

They walked and walked for many days and many nights. They saw lots of trees and flowers and animals. The bear and the bird talked and talked about all the things they saw. They talked about the big year they had ahead of them and all the fun they were going to have.

Finally, they came to a big mountain. The bear said, "Let's climb to the top!" The bird said, "That sounds adventurous!" So they climbed and climbed until they reached the top. They looked out over the whole forest and saw how beautiful it was. They were happy they went on an adventure together.

I keep my answers small and keep them near; Big questions bruised my mind but still I let Small answers be a bulwark to my fear. The huge abstractions I keep from the light; Small things I handled and caressed and loved. I let the stars assume the whole of night. But the big answers clamoured to be moved Into my life. Their great audacity Shouted to be acknowledged and believed. Even when all small answers build up to Protection of my spirit, I still hear Big answers striving for their overthrow And all the great conclusions coming near.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to pretend. Everywhere he went, he was always making up stories and using his big imagination. One day this little boy saw a piano and he walked over to it. He was so intrigued and he wanted to try it out. He tried pressing a few keys, but the little boy had no idea what he was doing. He just thought it was a lot of fun.

He kept playing the piano and thought he was doing a great job. But he actually kept making a lot of mistakes. His mother came over and saw how foolish he was being. She said to the little boy, â€œYou should never pretend that you know something if you donâ€™t. You should always try and learn about it first. That way you wonâ€™t make mistakes.â€

The little boy listened to his mother and the next time he saw a piano he watched the person playing it for a few minutes before he tried it out himself. Little by little,he began to learn how to play the piano.

The moral of the story is that it's important to never pretend you know something unless you are sure that you actually do. It's better to learn and practice before you try something new.

Passers-by, Out of your many faces Flash memories to me Now at the day end Away from the sidewalks Where your shoe soles traveled And your voices rose and blent To form the city's afternoon roar Hindering an old silence. Passers-by, I remember lean ones among you, Throats in the clutch of a hope, Lips written over with strivings, Mouths that kiss only for love, Records of great wishes slept with, Held long And prayed and toiled for: Yes, Written on Your mouths And your throats I read them When you passed by.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went for a walk in the forest. She saw a big black bear! The bear looked dangerous. Lily was scared and she wanted to go home.

Lily remembered that her mom gave her a phone. She called her mom and said, "Mommy, there's a big black bear in the forest and it looks dangerous. I want to come home now." Her mommy said, "Stay where you are, Lily. I will come and get you."

Lily waited for her mommy and the bear went away. Her mommy arrived and took her home safely. From that day on, Lily never went for a walk in the forest alone again.

name_of_work: The Stone Age by Kamala Das
content: Fond husband, ancient settler in the mind, Old fat spider, weaving webs of bewilderment, Be kind. You turn me into a bird of stone, a granite Dove, you build round me a shabby room, And stroke my pitted face absent-mindedly while You read. With loud talk you bruise my pre-morning sleep, You stick a finger into my dreaming eye. And Yet, on daydreams, strong men cast their shadows, they sink Like white suns in the swell of my Dravidian blood, Secretly flow the drains beneath sacred cities. When you leave, I drive my blue battered car Along the bluer sea. I run up the forty Noisy steps to knock at another's door. Though peep-holes, the neighbours watch, they watch me come And go like rain. Ask me, everybody, ask me What he sees in me, ask me why he is called a lion, A libertine, ask me why his hand sways like a hooded snake Before it clasps my pubis. Ask me why like A great tree, felled, he slumps against my breasts, And sleeps. Ask me why life is short and love is Shorter still, ask me what is bliss and what its price....

Once upon a time, there was a sick little girl. She was very sad and weak. Her mommy took her to the doctor to try to make her better. But when the doctor looked at her, he frowned. The little girl was very worried and started to weep. 

The doctor spoke to her mother and said it was an unusual sickness. He said he'd have to do a special test to see what was wrong. The mommy was very scared and gave her daughter a big hug. 

The doctor kindly gave the little girl some medicine and a special tea to drink. The girl was relieved, but still sad. She hoped she'd get better soon. 

The next day, her mommy took her back to the doctor again. This time, the doctor smiled and said she was feeling much better. 

The mommy and the little girl were overjoyed. From then on, she took the medicine every day and soon she was completely healed. The little girl was very happy and full of energy again.

One day, a boy named Ben went to the zoo with his mom. He saw many animals, but his favorite was the kangaroo. He wanted to give the kangaroo a hug, but his mom said no.

"Kangaroos are wild animals, Ben. They can kick and scratch. You have to stay behind the fence," his mom said.

But Ben did not listen. He waited until his mom was looking at the monkeys, and he climbed over the fence. He ran to the kangaroo and tried to hug it. But the kangaroo did not like that. It was an enormous kangaroo, and it felt scared. It kicked Ben hard in the chest, and he fell to the ground.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben cried. His mom heard him and ran to him. She saw the kangaroo and the fence, and she was very angry.

"Ben, what did you do? You could have been hurt very badly! Why did you not listen to me?" his mom said.

Ben was sorry. He had a big bruise on his chest, and he felt ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to give the kangaroo a hug. I thought it would be nice."

His mom hugged him and said, "I know, Ben. But you have to remember that not all animals like hugs. Some animals need space and respect. You have to be careful and follow the rules when you visit the zoo. Do you understand?"

Ben nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I will be more careful next time. Can we still see the other animals?"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can. But only from a safe distance. Come on, let's go see the elephants."

Ben learned his lesson. He enjoyed seeing the other animals, but he did not try to hug them. He realized that giving hugs is not always the best way to show love. Sometimes, giving space is better.

Why have you made life so intolerable And set me between four walls, where I am able Not to escape meals without prayer, for that is possible Only by annoying an attendant. And tonight a sensual Hell has been put on me, so that all has deserted me And I am merely crying and trembling in heart For Death, and cannot get it. And gone out is part Of sanity. And there is dreadful Hell within me, And nothing helps, forced meals there have been and electricity And weakening of sanity by influence Thats dreadful to endure, and there is orders And I am praying for death, death, death And dreadful is the indrawing or out-breathing of breath Because of the intolerable insults put on my whole soul Of the soul loathed, loathed, loathed of the soul. Gone out every bright thing from my mind. All lost that ever God himself designed. Not half can be written of cruelty of man, on man, Not often such evil guessed as between Man and Man.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and dress them up in pretty clothes. One day, she went to the beach with her family and saw a jellyfish in the water. It was big and round and had long tentacles. 

Lily's mom told her that jellyfish can sting, so they have to be careful. But Lily felt lucky because she got to see a real jellyfish up close. She watched it swim in the water and thought it looked like a floating umbrella. 

After a while, Lily and her family went back to their beach towels to have a snack. Lily's mom gave her a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, which was her favorite. She felt happy and content as she ate her sandwich and watched the waves. It was a perfect day at the beach for Lily.

Marrying left your maiden name disused. Its five light sounds no longer mean your face, Your voice, and all your variants of grace; For since you were so thankfully confused By law with someone else, you cannot be Semantically the same as that young beauty: It was of her that these two words were used. Now it's a phrase applicable to no one, Lying just where you left it,scattered through Old lists, old programmes, a school prize or two Packets of letters tied with tartan ribbon - Then is it scentless, weightless, strengthless, wholly Untruthful? Try whispering it slowly. No, it means you. Or, since you're past and gone, It means what we feel now about you then: How beautiful you were, and near, and young, So vivid, you might still be there among Those first few days, unfingermarked again. So your old name shelters our faithfulness, Instead of losing shape and meaning less With your depreciating luggage laden.

Once upon a time, there was a big, blue boat called a navy ship. The sailors on the ship liked to eat food that was spicy. One day, a little mouse snuck onto the ship to try some of the spicy food. The sailors didn't see the mouse, so it ate some of their food without them knowing.

When the sailors found out, they were very mad. They looked all around the ship, but they couldn't find the little mouse anywhere. Then, one of the sailors heard a tiny noise. He whispered to the other sailors, "I think I hear the mouse!" They all listened carefully and heard the little mouse squeaking. They found it hiding behind a box and took it off the ship. From then on, they made sure to keep their spicy food in a safe place where no mice could get to it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. She was very brave - but also very scared.

One day, Daisy's parents took her to the library. She opened the door and saw a huge walls of books. She was amazed!

Daisy's mum asked her, "Shall we look for a book, Daisy?" Daisy nodded, so they both went over to the bookshelf. 

Daisy looked for a bit, but then started to feel scared again. "I can't find one," she said.

Then Daisy's mum said, "Don't worry, Daisy! I have one I can recommend". She went and fetched a big book. Daisy wasn't scared any more - she was so excited to read it!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but one day, she heard a loud sound. It was the thunder! Lily was scared and ran inside her house. 

â€œMommy, whatâ€™s that loud noise?â€ Lily asked.

â€œItâ€™s just the thunder, honey. Donâ€™t worry, it will stop soon,â€ her mommy replied. 

Lily felt better, but then she heard a knock on the door. It was her neighbor, Mr. Smith. 

â€œHello, Lily. Can you come over and play with me?â€ Mr. Smith asked.

Lily didnâ€™t want to be rude, but she was still scared of the thunder. She thought for a moment and then said, â€œIâ€™m sorry, Mr. Smith. I canâ€™t come over right now. Iâ€™m scared of the thunder. Maybe we can play later when it stops?â€ 

Mr. Smith understood and said, â€œOf course, Lily. Stay safe inside.â€ 

After a while, the thunder stopped and Lily went outside to play with Mr. Smith. She was happy she didnâ€™t have to be rude and she was no longer scared of the thunder.

One day, Ben was walking in the park. He was feeling very tired and wishing that something exciting would happen. Suddenly, he saw a big blue balloon lying on the ground. He was amazed by its beauty and was excited to pick it up. But, when he tried to pick it up, a mean man came out of nowhere and shouted at him, "Don't steal my balloon!"

Ben was very scared and quickly ran away. He thought the mean man would come back in the future and get revenge on him, so he was scared to come back to the park.

A few years later, Ben was all grown up. One day, he was walking in the park again and he saw the same big blue balloon lying in the same spot as before. Ben already knew that the mean man was gone and he was not scared but very tired.

He picked up the balloon and was surprised when he heard a familiar voice in his ear, "Thank you for not stealing my balloon, Ben!" He realized that the mean man he was scared of years ago was the balloon's owner! He was happy and relieved, and had not expected a reward like this.

Tim and Mia liked to play in the yard. They had a ball, a bike, and a doll. They had fun with their toys, but they also liked to look at the fence. The fence was old and brown. It had holes and cracks. Sometimes they saw animals on the other side of the fence. They saw a cat, a bird, and a rabbit. They wanted to touch them, but they could not.

One day, Tim had an idea. He said to Mia, "Let's move the fence. Maybe we can make a hole and go to the other side. Maybe we can play with the animals." Mia nodded. She thought it was a good idea. They pushed and pulled the fence. It was hard, but they did not give up. They made a small hole in the fence. They were happy.

They put their toys down and went to the hole. They looked through the hole. They saw a big dog. The dog was black and white. It had sharp teeth and a loud bark. It saw them too. It ran to the hole. It was angry. It wanted to bite them. Tim and Mia were scared. They screamed and ran away. They left their toys behind.

The dog reached the hole. It tried to get through the hole. It was too big. It pushed and pulled the fence. It was not hard for the dog. It made the hole bigger and bigger. It broke the fence. It was fragile. The dog got through the fence. It saw the toys. It did not want to play with them. It wanted to destroy them. It bit the ball, the bike, and the doll. It made them flat, bent, and torn. It was not nice.

Tim and Mia ran to the house. They told their mom what happened. Their mom was mad. She said, "You should not have moved the fence. It was fragile. You should have left it alone. Now the dog is in our yard. Now your toys are ruined. You are in trouble." Tim and Mia were sad. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They did not move the fence again.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and honest girl. Her name was Candy and she was only three years old.

One day, she went to a special shop. When she opened the door, she saw many different kinds of ice cream cones. She wanted to try one, so she asked her mommy for a cone. 

Her mommy smiled and said, "Ok, sweetie! What kind of cone would you like?". Candy said, "I would like a chocolate cone with sprinkles".

Then her mommy ordered a cone for Candy. The shopkeeper looked at mommy happily and quickly gave her the cone. Candy thanked her mommy and took a big bite of the delicious cone.
 
It was the most yummy cone Candy had ever tasted! She smiled and told her mommy, "Thank you for the honest order!"

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around in the green grass and eat yummy carrots. One day, Benny found a big basket on the ground. It was so big that Benny could fit inside of it! Benny felt happy because he loved finding new things to play with. 

As Benny was playing in the basket, he saw a wise old owl perched on a nearby tree. The owl was very intelligent and knew a lot about the forest. Benny wanted to ask the owl some questions, but he was too shy. Finally, Benny gathered his courage and asked the owl what it was like to fly. 

The owl smiled and said, "Flying feels like magic. It's like you're floating on a cloud!" Benny felt amazed by the owl's words. He thanked the owl for his wisdom and went back to playing in the basket. From that day on, Benny felt smarter and more confident because he had learned something new from the intelligent owl.

Once upon a time there was a 3 year old boy named Bob. Bob was a very creative kid, and he loved to design things. One day, his dad decided to take him to the park. 

When they got there, Bob noticed a slide and was very excited. He started to design a plan to go down the slide, but his dad saw what he was doing and said - "No, no Bob! You can't go on the slide." 

Bob was embarrassed and started to cry. So, his dad said, "It's okay, Bob. It's the law - you can't go down the slide until you are 4". 

Bob was very sad. He couldn't design any more plans for the slide and was very upset. The bad ending of the story was that Bob had to wait one more year before he could have fun on the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very excited because her family was going on a holiday to the beach. Her mom said, "Lily, we need to pack our bags for the trip. Can you help me?"

Lily said, "Yes, mommy! I want to pack my toys and my swimsuit." Her mom smiled and said, "That's a good idea. We need to pack lots of things for our holiday."

The next day, they went to the beach and saw a big, rich hotel. Lily said, "Wow! That hotel is so big and fancy!" Her dad said, "Yes, it is. But we are happy with our little cottage by the beach. It's cozy and perfect for us."

Lily had a great time playing in the sand and swimming in the ocean. At night, she cuddled with her parents in their cozy cottage. She said, "I love our holiday. It's the best!"

One day, a little boy named Timmy went to the beach with his mommy. They played in the sand and chased the waves. Timmy loved the water, but his mommy warned him about the tide. She said, "Timmy, be careful. The tide can be dangerous."

But Timmy didn't listen. He ran towards the water and got wet. His mommy scolded him, "Timmy, you should have listened to me. Now your clothes are all wet."

Timmy felt sad and apologized. His mommy hugged him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. Let's lay in the sun and dry off." They laid on the beach and watched the waves. Timmy learned that it's important to listen to his mommy and be safe.

name_of_work: Animal Crackers by Richard de Zoysa
content: "Draw me a lion." So I set my pen to work. Produce a lazy, kindly beast . . . Colour it yellow. "Does it bite?" "Sometimes, but only when it's angry-- if you pull its tail or say that it is just another cat . . ." But for the most part, indolent, biddable, basking in the sun of ancient pride. (Outside, the sunlight seems a trifle dulled and there's a distant roaring, like a pride of lions, cross at being awakened from long, deep sleep). Then "Draw me a tiger." Vision of a beast compounded of Jim Corbett yarns and Blake stalks through my mind, blazing Nature's warning, black bars on gold. "DRAW!" You turn and draw the gun on me, as if to show that three-years-old understands force majeure and as you pull the silly plastic trigger all hell breaks loose; quite suddenly the sky is full of smoke and orange stripes of flame. BUT HERE THERE ARE NO TIGERS HERE THERE ARE ONLY LIONS. And their jackals run panting, rabid in the roaring's wake, infecting all with madness as they pass while My Lord the Elephant sways in his shaded arbour, wrinkles his ancient brows, and wonders-- if, did he venture out to quell this jungle-tide of rising flame, he'd burn his tender feet. "Put down that gun. If you do, and you're good, I'll draw a picture of an elephant. A curious beast that you must understand . . . ." DONT LOOK OUT THE WINDOW-- Just a party down the lane a bonfire, and some fireworks, and they're burning-- No, not a tiger--just some silly cat."

Once upon a time there was a small girl who really wanted to learn to dance. Every day she tried but no matter how much she tried, she just couldn't get the steps right.

The girl was very persistent. She touched her feet to the floor in the same way but she just couldn't do it correctly. She touched her knees and her hips, but the movements just weren't right. 

One day, she saw a dancer in the park. He was dancing with such grace and movement. The little girl just watched in amazement. 

The man saw the girl watching him and he stopped to see what she was doing. He touched her feet gently and said 'try these steps'. He touched her hands and her hips and showed her how to move them. She kept trying and trying, and eventually she was able to dance just like him! 

The little girl was so happy. She felt the happiness in her heart. From that day on she continued to practice and soon she was dancing like she had always dreamed!

Once upon a time there was a mighty hippo. He lived in a beautiful pond. Every day he liked to spend time playing with his friends.

One day, he and his friends decided to go for a swim. As they were in the middle of the pond, something awesome happened. A boat sailed by and all the animals cheered.

The hippo was so excited, he shouted, "Let's go and investigate!" So off they went.

They soon got to the boat and it had been filled with all kinds of delicious treats. The hippo was so excited, he shouted, "Let's spoil ourselves!"

The animals began to eat the treats and it was delicious. They even shared with the birds that flew by. They had the most wonderful time! 

The hippo felt so content and happy. They all returned to the pond, full of joy and good memories. 

The mighty hippo thanked his friends for such a wonderful adventure. They all agreed that spoiling themselves was the best way to spend their day!

name_of_work: Repression of War Experience by Siegfried Sassoon
content: Now light the candles; one; two; there's a moth; What silly beggars they are to blunder in And scorch their wings with glory, liquid flame-- No, no, not that,--it's bad to think of war, When thoughts you've gagged all day come back to scare you; And it's been proved that soldiers don't go mad Unless they lose control of ugly thoughts That drive them out to jabber among the trees. Now light your pipe; look, what a steady hand. Draw a deep breath; stop thinking; count fifteen, And you're as right as rain ... Why won't it rain? ... I wish there'd be a thunder-storm to-night, With bucketsful of water to sluice the dark, And make the roses hang their dripping heads. Books; what a jolly company they are, Standing so quiet and patient on their shelves, Dressed in dim brown, and black, and white, and green, And every kind of colour. Which will you read? Come on; O do read something; they're so wise. I tell you all the wisdom of the world Is waiting for you on those shelves; and yet You sit and gnaw your nails, and let your pipe out, And listen to the silence: on the ceiling There's one big, dizzy moth that bumps and flutters; And in the breathless air outside the house The garden waits for something that delays. There must be crowds of ghosts among the trees,-- Not people killed in battle,--they're in France,-- But horrible shapes in shrouds--old men who died Slow, natural deaths,--old men with ugly souls, Who wore their bodies out with nasty sins. You're quiet and peaceful, summering safe at home; You'd never think there was a bloody war on! ... O yes, you would ... why, you can hear the guns. Hark! Thud, thud, thud,--quite soft ... they never cease-- Those whispering guns--O Christ, I want to go out And screech at them to stop--I'm going crazy; I'm going stark, staring mad because of the guns.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she went to visit her grandma who lived in a big house. 

When she arrived, her grandma offered her some cookies and milk. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, grandma! You are so nice!"

While Lily was eating her cookies, she saw a shiny iron on the table. She asked her grandma, "What is that charming thing?" Her grandma smiled and said, "That's an iron, my dear. It's used to make clothes smooth and flat."

Lily was fascinated and said, "Can I help you iron your clothes, grandma?" Her grandma was delighted and said, "Of course, my dear. You are such a helpful and charming girl!" And so, Lily spent the afternoon helping her grandma iron her clothes while enjoying her cookies and milk.

Gold survives the fire that's hot enough to make you ashes in a standard urn. An envelope of course official buff contains your wedding ring that wouldn't burn. Dad told me I'd to tell them at St. James's the ring should go in the incinerator. That "eternity" inscribed with both their names is his surety that they'd be together, "later". I signed for the parcelled clothing as the son, the cardy, apron, pants, bra, dress- The clerk phoned down, 6- 8- 8- 3- 1? Has she still her ring on? (Slight pause) Yes! It's on my warm palm now, your burnished ring! I feel your ashes, head, arms, breasts, womb, legs, sift through its circle slowly, like that thing you used to let me watch to time the eggs.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Stephen. He was three years old and was always very glad. 

Stephen had an old cupboard in his bedroom that was filled with toys and games. Every day, Stephen would open the cupboard and play and have lots of fun. 

One day, Stephen's parents decided it was time to improve the cupboard. They took out all the toys, emptied the cupboard and replaced it with a new and shiny cupboard. 

Stephen was not glad about this. He said to his parents, "No! I don't like it. I want my old cupboard back." But his parents wouldn't listen and the new cupboard stayed. 

Stephen quickly learned he could no longer find any of his favourite toys and games. He was very sad and wished his old cupboard was back. Sadly, this never happened.

name_of_work: I Shall Paint My Nails Red by Carole Satyamurti
content: Because a bit of colour is a public service. Because I am proud of my hands. Because it will remind me I'm a woman. Because I will look like a survivor. Because I can admire them in traffic jams. Because my daughter will say ugh. Because my lover will be surprised. Because it is quicker than dyeing my hair. Because it is a ten-minute moratorium. Because it is reversible.

Ben and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Ben found a bottle of oil and poured some into a big pan. He said, "I will make a yummy cake with oil and flour and sugar."

Mia saw the oil and said, "No, Ben, oil is not for cakes. Oil is for cars and machines. It will make the cake taste bad and make us sick." She tried to take the bottle from Ben, but he held it tight.

They started to fight over the bottle. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The bottle slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. The oil spilled everywhere. It made the floor slippery and shiny.

Ben and Mia slipped and slid on the oil. They could not stand up or walk. They felt uncomfortable and scared. They cried for help.

Mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the mess and was angry. She said, "What have you done? You have wasted the oil and made the kitchen dirty. You are in big trouble." She slapped her hand on the table to show how mad she was.

Ben and Mia heard the slap and felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing and we did not mean to spill the oil. Please help us get up and clean the kitchen."

Mom sighed and said, "Okay, I will help you, but you have to promise me to never play with oil again. Oil is not a toy. It is dangerous and wasteful. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nodded and said, "We understand, Mom. We promise to never play with oil again. We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Ben and Mia. Now let's get you out of this oily mess." She took their hands and helped them stand up. She gave them a hug and a kiss and said, "Next time, if you want to make a cake, ask me first. I will show you how to use the right ingredients and tools."

Ben and Mia said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom. You are the best chef in the world."

So say Bazonka every day (That's what my grandma used to say) Don't say it if your socks are dry! Or when the sun is in your eye! Never say it in the dark (The word you see emits a spark) Only say it in the day (That's what my grandma used to say) Young Tiny Tim took her advice He said it once, he said it twice he said it till the day he died And even after that he tried To say Bazonka! every day Just like my grandma used to say. Now folks around declare it's true That every night at half past two If you'll stand upon your head And shout Bazonka! from your bed You'll hear the word as clear as day Just like my grandma used to say!

We stripped in the first warm spring night and ran down into the Detroit River to baptize ourselves in the brine of car parts, dead fish, stolen bicycles, melted snow. I remember going under hand in hand with a Polish highschool girl I'd never seen before, and the cries our breath made caught at the same time on the cold, and rising through the layers of darkness into the final moonless atmosphere that was this world, the girl breaking the surface after me and swimming out on the starless waters towards the lights of Jefferson Ave. and the stacks of the old stove factory unwinking. Turning at last to see no island at all but a perfect calm dark as far as there was sight, and then a light and another riding low out ahead to bring us home, ore boats maybe, or smokers walking alone. Back panting to the gray coarse beach we didn't dare fall on, the damp piles of clothes, and dressing side by side in silence to go back where we came from.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl named Daisy. She smiled all day long, no matter what happened. One day, she decided that she had a goal: she wanted to ride a bike.

Daisy asked her parents if she could ride a bike and they said no. She was so disappointed that she frowned and her face turned bitter.

A few days later, Daisy's parents said they had a special surprise for Daisy!

She was so excited that she smiled from ear to ear!

Daisy's parents had bought her a shiny new bike! 

Daisy took her bike outside and hopped on. She wobbled a little at first, but then she got the hang of peddling and before she knew it, she was off!

Daisy was so proud that she had achieved her goal that she couldnâ€™t stop smiling. And since that day, she has never stopped riding her bike and always smiled when she did.

name_of_work: The force that through the green fuse drives the flower by Dylan Thomas
content: The force that through the green fuse drives the flower Drives my green age; that blasts the roots of trees Is my destroyer. And I am dumb to tell the crooked rose My youth is bent by the same wintry fever. The force that drives the water through the rocks Drives my red blood; that dries the mouthing streams Turns mine to wax. And I am dumb to mouth unto my veins How at the mountain spring the same mouth sucks. The hand that whirls the water in the pool Stirs the quicksand; that ropes the blowing wind Hauls my shroud sail. And I am dumb to tell the hanging man How of my clay is made the hangman's lime. The lips of time leech to the fountain head; Love drips and gathers, but the fallen blood Shall calm her sores. And I am dumb to tell a weather's wind How time has ticked a heaven round the stars. And I am dumb to tell the lover's tomb How at my sheet goes the same crooked worm.

Sara and Ben wanted to make a snowman. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They went outside and saw a lot of snow on the ground. They were happy.

They rolled a big ball of snow for the body. They rolled a smaller ball of snow for the head. They put the head on top of the body. They found two sticks for the arms, a carrot for the nose, and some stones for the eyes and mouth. They gave their snowman a smile.

But then, a strong wind blew. The snowman's head fell off. Sara and Ben were frustrated. They tried to put the head back on, but it was too heavy. They needed support.

They saw their dad coming from the house. He had a shovel in his hand. He saw their snowman and their sad faces. He asked them what was wrong.

"Our snowman's head fell off. We can't put it back on. It's too heavy. We need support," Sara and Ben said.

"Don't worry, I can help you," their dad said. He used the shovel to make a pile of snow behind the snowman's body. He lifted the head and placed it on the pile. He pressed the snow around the head to make it stable. He gave their snowman a scarf.

"There, now your snowman has support. He won't fall off again," their dad said.

Sara and Ben thanked their dad. They hugged their snowman. They were happy.

One day, the mother decided it was time for her daughterâ€™s first adventure outside. She said â€œLetâ€™s go explore! Come and look outside the igloo.â€

Once there was a yellow worm. He liked to wriggle around and have fun. He loved to stir up the dirt and move his little feet.
One day he found a little hole. He peered inside and saw a big pile of dirt. He knew he had to find something to stir it up with.
He saw a big stick lying nearby. He used it to stir up the dirt, turning it over and over. He was soon covered in mud and having a great time.
When he was done, he had made a big mound of dirt. He smiled and wriggled his way back out of the hole. 
It was the best day ever for the little yellow worm. He knew he'd be back to make some more mud.

Lila and Tom are playing with shapes. They have a big box of shapes. They can make a house, a car, a boat, or anything they want. They like to make shapes.

But there is a bad cat in the room. The cat is black and furry. The cat likes to play too, but not with shapes. The cat likes to play with Lila and Tom. The cat likes to jump on them and scratch them and bite them. The cat is not nice.

One day, the cat sees Lila and Tom making a house with shapes. The cat thinks it is a game. The cat runs to the house and knocks it down. The shapes fall everywhere. Lila and Tom are sad and angry. They shout at the cat.

"Bad cat! Bad cat! Go away! You broke our house!" they say.

The cat does not care. The cat thinks it is fun. The cat sees Tom holding a star shape. The cat wants the star. The cat jumps on Tom and tries to take the star. Tom holds the star tight. The cat scratches Tom's hand. Tom cries.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! Help! Help! Help!" he says.

Lila hears Tom cry. She sees the cat hurting Tom. She wants to help Tom. She wants to rescue Tom. She looks around. She sees a big pillow. She picks up the pillow. She runs to Tom and the cat. She throws the pillow at the cat. The pillow hits the cat. The cat is surprised. The cat lets go of the star and the hand. The cat runs away. Lila hugs Tom.

"Are you okay, Tom? I rescued you from the bad cat. I'm sorry the cat hurt you," she says.

Tom smiles. He hugs Lila back.

"Thank you, Lila. You are a good friend. You are brave. I'm okay. The cat is gone. We can play with shapes again," he says.

Lila and Tom are happy. They forget about the bad cat. They pick up the shapes. They make a new house. They make a big sign that says "No cats allowed". They play with shapes. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his favorite toy, a red ball. One day, Tim was playing with his ball outside when he accidentally dropped it. The ball bounced and rolled away until it landed in a nearby bush.

Tim tried to reach for his ball, but it was too far away. He felt sad because he couldn't play with his favorite toy anymore. Luckily, Tim's mom saw what happened and went to help him. She found a stick and used it to reach the ball, which was now available again for Tim to play with.

Tim was happy and hugged his mom. He learned that even when things get dropped, they can still be found and made available again.

One sunny day, Jack was playing in his garden. He saw a cane bouncing on the ground. The cane looked broken. Jack wanted to take the cane and play. He ran over to get it. He was so happy to see the cane.

Jack held the cane in his hands and started bouncing it on the ground. He watched it carefully as it bounced up and down. Suddenly, the cane broke in two. Jack was sad. But then he saw something funny.

Jack noticed that the handle of the cane was still bouncing! He laughed as he watched it bounce around his garden. He kept playing with it until it finally came to a stop.

Jack was happy that he got to use the broken cane to have fun. He decided to put it in his toy box and save it for another sunny day.

Ben liked to swim in the pond with his big sister, Amy. They wore swimsuits and goggles and splashed in the water. Ben liked to pretend he was a fish and swim under the water. Amy liked to pretend she was a mermaid and swim on top of the water.

One day, they saw a big post in the pond. It was brown and hard and had a sign on it. Amy wanted to read the sign, but Ben did not. He wanted to swim around the post and see what was on the other side. He was stubborn and did not listen to Amy.

Amy swam to the post and looked at the sign. It said, "Danger! Do not swim past this post. There are sharp rocks and strong currents." Amy was scared and called for Ben. But Ben did not hear her. He swam past the post and felt the water pull him. He saw the sharp rocks and tried to swim back. But he could not. He was stuck.

Amy saw Ben in trouble and swam to help him. She grabbed his hand and pulled him away from the rocks. She swam with him to the shore and hugged him. She was angry and sad and said, "Ben, you were very stubborn and very silly. You could have been hurt. You should have read the sign and listened to me."

Ben was sorry and said, "Amy, you were very brave and very kind. You saved me. I should have read the sign and listened to you." He hugged her back and said, "I love you, big sister." Amy smiled and said, "I love you, little brother." They dried off and went home. They never swam past the post again.

name_of_work: The History Teacher by Billy Collins
content: Trying to protect his students' innocence he told them the Ice Age was really just the Chilly Age, a period of a million years when everyone had to wear sweaters. And the Stone Age became the Gravel Age, named after the long driveways of the time. The Spanish Inquisition was nothing more than an outbreak of questions such as "How far is it from here to Madrid?" "What do you call the matador's hat?" The War of the Roses took place in a garden, and the Enola Gay dropped one tiny atom on Japan. The children would leave his classroom for the playground to torment the weak and the smart, mussing up their hair and breaking their glasses, while he gathered up his notes and walked home past flower beds and white picket fences, wondering if they would believe that soldiers in the Boer War told long, rambling stories designed to make the enemy nod off.

Once upon a time, there was a cop named Jack. Jack was very nice and compassionate. He loved to help people and animals. One day, Jack saw a lost puppy on the street. He felt sad for the puppy and wanted to help him. 

Jack picked up the puppy and took him to the animal shelter. At the shelter, the puppy was very scared and lonely. Jack wanted to make the puppy feel better, so he decided to join him in his cage. 

The puppy was so happy to have a friend. Jack and the puppy played together and cuddled. Soon, a kind family came to the shelter and adopted both Jack and the puppy. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved muffins, especially the blueberry ones. One day, she saw a big muffin on the kitchen counter. She wanted to eat it, but it was too high for her to reach. So, she asked her daddy to help her.

Daddy tried to pull the muffin down, but he was too weak. He asked mommy to help him. Together, they pulled the muffin down and gave it to Lily. She was so happy and took a big bite. It was the best muffin she ever had.

From that day on, Lily always asked for help when she wanted something she couldn't reach. She learned that it's okay to ask for help when you need it. And she also learned that muffins taste even better when you share them with people you love.

name_of_work: Minerva Jones by Edgar Lee Masters
content: I am Minerva, the village poetess, Hooted at, jeered at by the Yahoos of the street For my heavy body, cock-eye, and rolling walk, And all the more when "Butch" Weldy Captured me after a brutal hunt. He left me to my fate with Doctor Meyers; And I sank into death, growing numb from the feet up, Like one stepping deeper and deeper into a stream of ice. Will some one go to the village newspaper, And gather into a book the verses I wrote?-- I thirsted so for love I hungered so for life!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She had a house that was big and fun.

Inside the house was a room with a big window. It was a black window.

The little girl was very curious. She wanted to know what was on the other side.

One day, her mommy and daddy provided her with a ladder. They helped her climb up and she looked through the window.

On the other side was a beautiful garden with lots of flowers, trees and animals. The little girl was so happy! She could look out her window and see the wonderful things outside.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big monster. He was enormous! He had a weapon that he liked to play with. One day, he accidentally dropped his weapon on the ground and it started to burn. The monster was scared and didn't know what to do. He ran away and asked his friend, a little bird, for help. The bird told him to pour water on the burning weapon, and so the monster did. The fire went out and the monster was happy. From that day on, he was more careful with his weapon and always made sure it was put away safely.

In your arms was still delight, Quiet as a street at night; And thoughts of you, I do remember, Were green leaves in a darkened chamber, Were dark clouds in a moonless sky. Love, in you, went passing by, Penetrative, remote, and rare, Like a bird in the wide air, And, as the bird, it left no trace In the heaven of your face. In your stupidity I found The sweet hush after a sweet sound. All about you was the light That dims the greying end of night; Desire was the unrisen sun, Joy the day not yet begun, With tree whispering to tree, Without wind, quietly. Wisdom slept within your hair, And Long-Suffering was there, And, in the flowing of your dress, Undiscerning Tenderness. And when you thought, it seemed to me, Infinitely, and like a sea, About the slight world you had known Your vast unsconsciousness was thrown . . . O haven without wave or tide! Silence, in which all songs have died! Holy book, where hearts are still! And home at length under the hill! O mother quiet, breasts of peace, Where love itself would faint and cease! O infinite deep I never knew, I would come back, come back to you, Find you, as a pool unstirred, Kneel down by you, and never a word, Lay my head, and nothing said, In your hands, ungarlanded; And a long watch you would keep; And I should sleep, and I should sleep!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ann. She was three years old and loved to paint. 

Ann's mummy bought her a beautiful pink bicycle. She was so happy, she ran outside and started to paint the bicycle. 

Ann's mummy noticed her and said, "Ann, don't paint the bike. It's not normal to paint bicycles." 

Ann stopped what she was doing and looked up. She said, "But mummy, I want to paint it. I like painting." 

Her mummy smiled and said, "Yes, you can paint, but just be careful not to get too much paint on the bike." 

So Ann continued to paint the bicycle, and when she was done, it looked very pretty. Ann's mummy was very proud of her and they both went for a normal bike ride.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They both lived in the same city. The town was very big and had lots of things to explore. 

One day, Jack and Jill decided to go explore the city together. As they explored, they noticed how gentle everyone was. Everyone smiled and waved at them when they passed.

Jack and Jill were having so much fun! Suddenly, Jack stumbled and was about to fall. Jill quickly ran over to him and gave him a big hug. 

"Thank you for the hug," Jack said to Jill. 

"You are welcome," Jill replied with a smile. 

Jack and Jill continued to explore the city, feeling so happy and proud of the friendship they shared. Their gentle hugs made their friendship even stronger!

name_of_work: Crossing the Bar by Alfred Lord Tennyson
content: Sunset and evening star, And one clear call for me! And may there be no moaning of the bar, When I put out to sea, But such a tide as moving seems asleep, Too full for sound and foam, When that which drew from out the boundless deep Turns again home. Twilight and evening bell, And after that the dark! And may there be no sadness of farewell, When I embark; For tho' from out our bourne of Time and Place The flood may bear me far, I hope to see my Pilot face to face When I have crost the bar.

Sandra was feeling worried. She had a guitar but she didn't know how to use it. She asked her Daddy for help.

"Daddy, can you show me how to use my guitar?" She asked.

Daddy smiled, "Yes of course, my little girl. I'll show you how to use it."

Sandra was so excited. She watched as Daddy showed her how to strum the strings and hold the guitar. Daddy finished showing her how to use the guitar.

Suddenly, there was a loud crash from the other room. Daddy ran away to investigate. As he left, Sandra heard him talking to somebody else.

Sandra waited and waited but Daddy never came back. She was so worried. She never got to learn how to use her guitar. After a few hours, Sandra fell asleep on the couch.

When morning came, Sandra woke up to find her Daddy had gone. He had left the house and never came back. Sandra never found out what happened to Daddy and her guitar stayed unused.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play near the river. One day, they found a big raft. It was dry and had many sticks. They wanted to ride on it.

"Let's go on the raft!" Tom said. "It will be fun!"

"OK!" Sam said. "But we have to be careful. The river is fast and deep."

They pushed the raft into the water. They climbed on it. They used sticks to move. They laughed and sang.

But soon, the raft hit a big rock. It broke into two pieces. Tom and Sam fell into the water. They were scared and cold.

"Help! Help!" Tom cried. "I can't swim!"

"Me neither!" Sam cried. "Grab my hand!"

They tried to hold each other. But the water was too strong. It pulled them apart. They screamed and cried. They quit trying to swim. They sank under the water.

No one heard them. No one saw them. No one helped them. They were gone. The raft was gone. The river was quiet.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Joe. Joe wanted to go on a vacation. Every morning he would get on the bus and go to the charming seaside village near his house.

One day on the bus, Joe met a nice man who was very kind. The man asked Joe what he wanted to do most in life. Joe told him he wanted to go on a vacation.
 
The man smiled and told Joe that if he worked hard, he could make it happen. He said that in life, it was important to deliver the best that you can.
 
The man was right. Joe worked hard every day to save money. After a few months, he had enough money to go on the vacation he had always dreamed of.

Joe's hard work paid off. He had a wonderful time on his vacation and he learnt a valuable lesson: no matter how small and young you are, you can always deliver if you work hard.

Bob was so excited. He had been looking forward to the big day for so long. It was finally here! He was about to go on a real adventure!

He was going to the jungle with his parents. He had been imagining it for weeks. The trees, the animals, and the great big scary caves!

He packed his bag, put on his hat and got in the car. His dad drove them all the way to the edge of the jungle, where there was a fake toilet that all the animals could use.

"Look Daddy! What's that?" Bob asked, pointing at the toilet.

"That's a toilet, Bob," his dad replied.

Bob couldn't believe it! A real fake toilet made especially for animals! He was so excited, he was ready to start exploring! He couldn't wait!

Once upon a time there was a very icy crocodile. He liked to ignore everyone around him. One day a brave 3 year old child came near the crocodile. But the crocodile ignored the child, no matter how much she yelled hello. 

The child felt sad and started to cry. But then she had an idea. She started to build an igloo from all of the icy snow around her. When she finished building it, she called out to the crocodile. This time the crocodile saw her and came over to see the igloo. The crocodile was impressed and decided to stay near the igloo. 

From then on the crocodile and the three year old were the best of friends. The crocodile would never ignore her again and they would often play together in the icy snow. The End.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a mysterious door. No one knew what was behind it. One day, a little girl named Lucy walked up to the door. She was brave and wanted to see what was inside.

Lucy knocked on the door and said, "Hello! Is anyone there?" She heard a voice from the other side of the door repeat, "Hello! Welcome! Who is there?" Lucy said, "It's me, Lucy!" The door slowly opened, and a friendly cat was standing there.

The cat said, "Hi Lucy! Welcome to my home!" Lucy was very happy to meet the cat. They played together all day and became best friends. From that day on, the mysterious door was not scary anymore.

One day, Tommy went to the train station to play with his toy train. He was very obedient and carefully followed his mom's instructions. But when he got to the station, he saw a boy his age playing with another train, one that was the same size and color as Tommy's. Suddenly, he remembered that his mom had said that matching toys were good friends so he ran up to the other boy and asked, "Is your train matching mine?"

The other boy looked confused and said, "No, this isn't your train. It's mine." Tommy was a bit hurt but he was still very obedient and asked his mom if he could play with the boy and his train.

She said no. Tommy started to get sad, but his mom explained that it was very important to be respectful to what others own and that playing with it without permission was not nice.

Tommy understood, and was very obedient. From then on, he only played with his own train and was always respectful of others' belongings.

Once upon a time there was a wild animal. He was a scary and brave creature but he had lost his family. This made him very sad and scared. He looked everywhere for his family, but couldn't find them. He was all alone and feeling very, very scared.

Suddenly he heard a noise. He wasn't sure what it was, but he knew it didn't sound good. He panicked and ran and ran as fast as he could. He ran until he found a safe place. It was a dark and quiet cave. He hid in the cave and felt safer.

To his surprise, he was not alone. There were other wild animals there too. They were scared and sad too. He made new friends.

One of his new friends told him that they had found a special place full of safety and food. The animal was so happy and was no longer scared.

He and his new friends went to this special place every day and they were safe. And the wild animal didn't have to panic anymore.

name_of_work: Easter Monday (In Memoriam E.T.) by Eleanor Farjeon
content: In the last letter that I had from France You thanked me for the silver Easter egg Which I had hidden in the box of apples You liked to munch beyond all other fruit. You found the egg the Monday before Easter, And said, 'I will praise Easter Monday now - It was such a lovely morning'. Then you spoke Of the coming battle and said, 'This is the eve. Good-bye. And may I have a letter soon.' That Easter Monday was a day for praise, It was such a lovely morning. In our garden We sowed our earliest seeds, and in the orchard The apple-bud was ripe. It was the eve. There are three letters that you will not get.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to travel. She looked for many ways to travel, but nothing seemed available. One day, she thought of a way to travel. She had to ask her mommy for help. Her mommy said she could go to a park nearby. The girl was so happy! She was excited to go to the park. She quickly put on her shoes and went along the way. On her way, she saw so many different things. She enjoyed looking at all the trees, birds and people around her. When she finally arrived at the park, she was amazed at how beautiful it was. She ran all around the park, exploring and spending time with her mom. She had a wonderful time, and can't wait to travel this way again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo lived in a beautiful reef with his friends. One day, Nemo's mommy told him they needed to buy some food. Nemo was excited to go with her.

As they swam to the store, Nemo saw a big, terrible shark. He was scared! But his mommy told him not to worry and they swam away quickly.

At the store, Nemo's mommy bought some yummy fish flakes. Nemo was happy they got what they needed and they swam back to their reef. From then on, Nemo always listened to his mommy and never went near the terrible shark again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy bricks. He would build tall towers and knock them down with a big push. Timmy's mom always told him to be gentle with his toys and to not push too hard.

One day, Timmy was playing with his bricks outside when he saw a sad little girl sitting alone on the sidewalk. Timmy felt compassionate and wanted to make her feel better. He went over to her and offered to build her a tower with his bricks.

The little girl smiled and Timmy started building. He carefully placed each brick on top of the other until the tower was as tall as he could reach. The little girl clapped her hands and Timmy felt happy that he could make her smile.

As they were playing, Timmy accidentally knocked over the tower with a big push. The little girl started to cry and Timmy felt bad. But then he remembered what his mom always told him about being gentle with his toys. He apologized to the little girl and promised to build an even bigger tower, but this time he would be more careful. And so, Timmy and the little girl spent the rest of the day building and playing together, with lots of compassion and gentle pushes. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Gizmo. He loved exploring the forest, but he was a bit clumsy. As he was wandering around, he began to feel the ground tremble beneath his feet. He looked around to see who else was shaking, but all the other animals were calmly standing still. Gizmo realized that he was feeling an earthquake and became very scared.

Gizmo ran quickly to find a safe place, but the shaking of the earth kept following him. Everywhere he looked, he could see the trees shaking. He was so scared that he didn't even notice when he stumbled and fell over. He lay there trembling until he heard a voice.

"Gizmo! Are you ok?" The voice belonged to Gizmo's friend, a rabbit named Hippo. He helped Gizmo up and explained that the trembling was part of an earthquake. Impressed by the power of this natural force, Gizmo thanked Hippo for helping him understand what was happening.

"There is great power in nature," Hippo said. "It's important to remember that even when something looks scary, it can still be a beautiful thing." Gizmo learned an important lesson that day: respect nature, and it will keep you safe.

name_of_work: Looking-Glass River by Robert Louis Stevenson
content: Smooth it glides upon its travel, Here a wimple, there a gleam-- O the clean gravel! O the smooth stream! Sailing blossoms, silver fishes, Pave pools as clear as air-- How a child wishes To live down there! We can see our colored faces Floating on the shaken pool Down in cool places, Dim and very cool; Till a wind or water wrinkle, Dipping marten, plumping trout, Spreads in a twinkle And blots all out. See the rings pursue each other; All below grows black as night, Just as if mother Had blown out the light! Patience, children, just a minute-- See the spreading circles die; The stream and all in it Will clear by-and-by.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with his friends. One day, Ducky's friend, Bunny, asked him if he wanted to play a game.

"Let's see who can dive the deepest!" Bunny said.

Ducky was excited to play the game. He put on his apron and took a deep breath. He dove into the pond and swam as deep as he could. When he came back up, Bunny was clapping.

"Wow, Ducky! You dove really deep!" Bunny said.

Ducky was happy that he won the game. He and Bunny continued to play in the pond until it was time to go home. Ducky went to bed that night feeling proud of himself for diving so deep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, she saw an old lady sitting on a bench looking sad. Lily went over to her and said, "Hi! Are you okay?"

The old lady replied, "No, I'm not feeling well. I'm a patient and I'm feeling weak."

Lily didn't know what to do, so she went to her mommy and asked, "Mommy, can we bring some cookies and water to the old lady in the park? She's a patient and she feels weak."

Her mommy said, "Of course! That's a great idea." So, they went to the store and bought some cookies and water. When they gave it to the old lady, she smiled and said, "Thank you so much! You didn't disturb me at all. You made my day."

From that day on, Lily and her mommy would bring cookies and water to the old lady every week. They became good friends and would talk for hours. And Lily learned that helping others can make them feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to paint. One day, he went to the park with his mom. The sky was clear and the sun was shining. Tim brought his paint and paper with him.

At the park, Tim saw a big tree. He wanted to paint the tree. So, he took out his paint and paper and started to paint. While he was painting, a little girl named Sue came over. She was eating a sandwich.

Sue said, "Hi! I like your painting!" Tim smiled and said, "Thank you! I like your sandwich!" Sue laughed and they became friends. They played in the park and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Paul. Paul was playing in his backyard when he found a tunnel. He was curious what was inside so he decided to see. He went in and suddenly everything got very dark. He was scared but kept walking. Suddenly at the end of the tunnel he heard voices coming from the other side. 

Paul got closer and heard the voices getting louder and louder. He peeked around the corner and saw two friends arguing about their game. He heard one of them say to the other, "You have to surrender now, cause I'm winning!" 

The other friend replied, "No way! I'm not guilty of surrendering just yet!" Paul was so scared he ran back down the tunnel as fast as he could. He was happy to be back in the safety of his own backyard! He never went back in the tunnel again.

name_of_work: I Don't Miss It by Tracy K. Smith
content: But sometimes I forget where I am, Imagine myself inside that life again. Recalcitrant mornings. Sun perhaps, Or more likely colorless light Filtering its way through shapeless cloud. And when I begin to believe I haven't left, The rest comes back. Our couch. My smoke Climbing the walls while the hours fall. Straining against the noise of traffic, music, Anything alive, to catch your key in the door. And that scamper of feeling in my chest, As if the day, the night, wherever it is I am by then, has been only a whir Of something other than waiting. We hear so much about what love feels like. Right now, today, with the rain outside, And leaves that want as much as I do to believe In May, in seasons that come when called, It's impossible not to want To walk into the next room and let you Run your hands down the sides of my legs, Knowing perfectly well what they know.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a pet mouse named Lucky. Lucky was very small and had soft, brown fur. 

One day, Lily was playing in her room when she saw Lucky run across the floor. She chased after him, but Lucky was too fast and ran under her bed. 

Lily got down on her hands and knees and looked under the bed. She saw Lucky hiding in a corner. Lucky was lucky because Lily loved him very much and took good care of him. 

Lily reached under the bed and gently picked up Lucky. She held him in her hands and gave him a little kiss on his head. Lucky was happy to be with Lily, his best friend in the whole world.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Max who lived in a jungle. Max loved to play and swing from tree to tree. One day, Max saw a little bird named Bella who was anxious because she couldn't find her nest. Max asked Bella, "What's wrong?"

Bella said, "I lost my nest and I don't know where to put my eggs."

Max felt sad for Bella and wanted to help her. He asked his friends in the jungle if they had seen Bella's nest. Finally, they found the nest and put it back in the tree. Bella was very happy and grateful. Max learned that helping others can make them happy and that's the right thing to do. From that day on, Max and Bella became good friends and played together in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys, but he couldn't decide which one to play with. He looked at his toy cars, his stuffed animals, and his building blocks, but he just couldn't make up his mind.

Suddenly, his friend Billy came over to play. "Hey Timmy, what's wrong?" Billy asked. "I can't decide which toy to play with," Timmy said. "Well, let's have a fight and see which toy wins!" Billy suggested.

Timmy wasn't sure about fighting, but he knew Billy was ready for it. So, they picked their favorite toys and had a pretend fight. In the end, Timmy's toy car won, and he was so happy. "Thanks for helping me decide, Billy," Timmy said. "No problem, Timmy! That was a fun fight," Billy replied.

Once upon a time, there was a scary monster who lived in a big, dark house. The monster loved to spread paint on the walls to make them even scarier. He had a big, blue ashtray that he used to hold all his paint.

One day, a little girl named Lucy came to the house. She saw the scary walls and the big, blue ashtray. Lucy was not scared of the monster. She said, "Mr. Monster, why do you spread paint on the walls? It makes your house look scary."

The monster looked at Lucy and said, "I like scary things, but I want to be friends with you." So Lucy and the monster spread new paint on the walls. They used happy colors like pink, yellow, and green. They made the house look fun and pretty.

Now, the monster and Lucy are best friends. They play in the big, dark house every day. The scary monster is not scary anymore, and the big, blue ashtray holds paint for their fun art projects. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie was very graceful and loved to fly around the forest. One day, Tweetie met a squirrel named Nutty. Nutty asked Tweetie if she could deliver a message to her friend who lived on the other side of the forest. Tweetie agreed and took the message.

As Tweetie was flying, she saw smoke and fire in the distance. She knew it was dangerous, but she wanted to deliver the message. When she arrived at her friend's house, she saw that it was on fire. She quickly delivered the message and told her friend to leave the house. Her friend was safe, but Tweetie realized she had flown too close to the fire and her wings were burned.

Tweetie tried to fly back home, but she couldn't. She had to walk back to her nest, and it took a long time. When she finally arrived, her family was sad to see her hurt. Tweetie's wings never healed, and she could no longer fly. She learned that even though she wanted to help, sometimes it's better to be safe than sorry.

Mia was so excited to get ready for the party. First, she had to take a bath. She put her foot in the warm water and it felt so nice. She grabbed her washcloth and her fluffy yellow duck and washed with them. After she was done, she stepped out and dried herself off with a towel.

Next, she got out her shoes. They were brand new and very clean. She loved the big purple bows on the top. She put them on and admired her outfit. She was ready for the party!

Finally, it was time for the party. Mia put on her shoes and grabbed a balloon. She couldnâ€™t wait to show off her new shoes and have fun with her friends.

As though no one has told him many times, what a nonlinear slapstick meets slasher flick meets psychological pit he is now co-starring in. Remind me, he says to our family.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He was only three years old and loved to play with his friends. One day, Tim decided to try something new - the violin! He was so excited so he asked his mom if he could try it. His mom said yes and found him a nice one.

Tim was a bit scared when he first tried to play the violin. He was afraid that he wouldn't be able to make a nice sound come out of it. But he trusted himself and tried anyway.

At first it was crazy! All the notes were all jumbled up and messy. But soon enough he was able to figure it out. Now he can play all kinds of songs on the violin and he loves it!

Whenever Tim plays the violin, he remembers that he can trust himself to try something new. He knows that he can do anything if he trusts himself and tries.

There was a gigantic forest, thick with trees and all kinds of creatures. To find a way through the forest was a difficult task.

One day, a little girl called Jane decided to explore the forest. She was so brave and full of curiosity.

As Jane ventured through the forest, she came across a crossroads. In front of her were two paths, one leading to the east and one leading to the west. Jane looked closely at both the paths and considered carefully for a moment.

Finally, she asked the trees, "which way do I choose?"

One tree responded with, â€œchoose the path to the west, for it is filled with wonderful images."

Jane smiled and said, â€œokay. I will choose the west path.â€ Without hesitation, she stepped onto the west path and immediately felt inspired by the images she saw around her- a tiny rainbow, a playful bird and a beautiful lake. 

Jane was so happy she had chosen the west path!

Once there was a little girl who wanted a puppy. Day after day, she would beg her parents to get one. But they wouldn't listen. The little girl was so sad and she would cry and cry.

One day, the little girl was outside when she saw a little puppy in the park. It was so cute that the little girl couldn't help herself. She ran over to the puppy and started petting it. Suddenly, the puppy let out a loud yelp and bit the little girl's toe. The little girl was so startled, she started to cry.

The puppy's owner came over and asked the little girl why she was crying. She said she wanted a puppy of her own. The owner told her that before she got a puppy she had to be alert. Puppies take a lot of work and she had to be prepared to look after it properly.

The little girl learned her lesson and from then on she was very alert whenever she was around animals. She knew that if she wanted to be a responsible pet owner, she had to pay attention.

The moral of the story is that if you want to look after something, you have to be alert and responsible.

Once upon a time there was an old vase. It lived on a shelf in a house. One day the vase bumped into the wall and it started to sneeze. 

The vase sneezed and sneezed. The homeowner heard the sneezing and came running. 

"Oh! What's the matter? What happened?" he asked the vase.

The vase replied, "I bumped into the wall and started to sneeze." 

"That's not good," said the homeowner. He grabbed the old vase and carried it outside. Then he dropped it on the ground and it broke into a million pieces. 

The vase was sad. It had wanted to stay inside the warm and cozy house, but now it was outside and alone. The homeowner felt bad, but it was too late. The old vase was gone forever.

Once there was a boy called Joe. He was always very polite. Every day Joe would leave for school, a big building with lots of pupils just like him. Joe would always greet the teachers and he would always be the first to put his hand up when he knew the answer. 

One day, Joe left school very late. The sun was almost setting and it was almost dark. Joe decided to take a shortcut home which was in the woods. As Joe was walking, he saw that a little pup was lost. The pup was very scared and he was crying. Joe saw the pup, and he decided to help.

Joe was very polite. He politely asked the pup what was wrong and if he needed help. The pup told him he had been separated from his family and didn't know how to get home. Joe saw what a difficult situation the pup was in and he decided to help.

Joe left the woods with the pup and made sure he was safe. When they reached the pup's family, one of the pup's siblings thanked Joe for being so polite and helping to reunite them. Joe was glad he was able to help.

This story teaches us that it is important to be polite and always help out whenever we can. Kindness always goes a long way!

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Tom. Tom was three years old.

One day, Tom wanted to see an animal. So he went to his dad and asked with a big smile, "Dad, can I have an animal?" 

His dad smiled and replied, "What kind of animal do you want?"

Tom thought for a while and then made a request. "I want a tough animal!" he said.

His dad nodded and said, "Ok, letâ€™s go look for one!" 

So Tom and his dad went on a journey and eventually found an elephant. It was a big and tough animal. Tom was so excited he wanted to touch it.

But his dad said, "It's too tough for you. So remember, don't touch it!" 

Tom nodded and watched the elephant with admiration. He was so happy that he had made a request and found such a tough animal.

Molly was a three year old little girl who lived in the countryside with her parents. They had a beautiful garden with many flowers, and a mule named Sam.

Every morning, Molly's dad would take Sam around the garden, and let him eat the grass and other plants. One morning, Molly asked her dad "Can I go with you?". Her dad said "yes, you can, but you must hold onto the mule's tail when I tell you to". Molly agreed, and got on the mule, with a big smile on her face.

As they were walking around the garden, Molly suddenly noticed a patch of pretty, pink flowers. She asked her dad "Can I pick one?". Her dad said, "Yes, you can, but remember to let the mule do his job". Molly nodded and let Sam go, and watched as he stopped near the flowers and started to yield.

Within a few minutes, the mule had yielded the flowers and Molly was so pleased. She picked a pretty pink flower and thanked Sam before putting it into her pocket.

It was a memorable morning for Molly and her dad, and afterwards, Molly thanked her dad for taking her with him, and for teaching her about the work that the mule did in the garden.
