Once upon a time, there was a bald man who lived alone in a small cell. Every day was a struggle for him as he tried to find something to do that made him happy. One day, he decided to restore the cell. He got some bright colours, cleaned the walls and bought some furniture. He even added a few plants and put up some decorations.

When he finished, he proudly admired his work. He opened the windows to let the sun shine in and it made everything look even brighter. He spent the day relaxing in his newly restored cell and feeling content.

The bald man was so happy with the results that he decided to restore some of the other cells in the building. He got together some friends, who also wanted to make the place more beautiful, and they worked together to restore all the other cells. They even convinced the owners of the building to provide fresh paint and decorations for the cells.

The bald man was so pleased with the results. It was so nice to see the building looking beautiful again! Everyone was happy and now the bald man had something to be proud of. He was thankful for being able to restore the cells and make the building a place of beauty.

One day, a three year old child came to visit the mill. They were very excited to see all the parts moving around. As they watched, the machines moved the pieces around. 

The child was so amazed. They wanted to help out so the workers let them part a few items. The child smiled proudly when the pieces fit together perfectly. 

When it was time to go home, the workers thanked the child for all their hard work. The child waved goodbye, feeling like the most popular person ever. 

The child couldn't wait to tell their friends all about the mill. They knew it was something special, a place that shouldn't be missed.

In the portrait of Jefferson that hangs at Monticello, he is rendered two-toned: his forehead white with illumination -- a lit bulb -- the rest of his face in shadow, darkened as if the artist meant to contrast his bright knowledge, its dark subtext. By 1805, when Jefferson sat for the portrait, he was already linked to an affair with his slave. Against a backdrop, blue and ethereal, a wash of paint that seems to hold him in relief, Jefferson gazes out across the centuries, his lips fixed as if he's just uttered some final word. The first time I saw the painting, I listened as my father explained the contradictions: how Jefferson hated slavery, though -- out of necessity, my father said -- had to own slaves; that his moral philosophy meant he could not have fathered those children: would have been impossible, my father said. For years we debated the distance between word and deed. I'd follow my father from book to book, gathering citations, listening as he named -- like a field guide to Virginia -- each flower and tree and bird as if to prove a man's pursuit of knowledge is greater than his shortcomings, the limits of his vision. I did not know then the subtext of our story, that my father could imagine Jefferson's words made flesh in my flesh -- the improvement of the blacks in body and mind, in the first instance of their mixture with the whites -- or that my father could believe he'd made me better. When I think of this now, I see how the past holds us captive, its beautiful ruin etched on the mind's eye: my young father, a rough outline of the old man he's become, needing to show me the better measure of his heart, an equation writ large at Monticello. That was years ago. Now, we take in how much has changed: talk of Sally Hemings, someone asking, How white was she? -- parsing the fractions as if to name what made her worthy of Jefferson's attentions: a near-white, quadroon mistress, not a plain black slave. Imagine stepping back into the past, our guide tells us then -- and I can't resist whispering to my father: This is where we split up. I'll head around to the back. When he laughs, I know he's grateful I've made a joke of it, this history that links us -- white father, black daughter -- even as it renders us other to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Jack. Jack had a big field where he grew wheat. He was very wise and knew how to take care of his crops.

One day, Jack's friend, Tom, came to visit him. Tom was a funny man and loved to joke around. He saw the wheat field and said, "Jack, let's play a joke on your scarecrow!"

Jack thought it was a bad idea, but Tom insisted. So they dressed up the scarecrow in funny clothes and put a hat on its head. They both laughed and went home.

The next day, Jack went to check on his wheat field and saw something strange. The scarecrow was gone! He looked around and saw it lying on the ground, torn apart. Jack realized that their joke had attracted some hungry animals who had destroyed his crops. From then on, Jack never let anyone play jokes on his scarecrow again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Sally. Joe was very bossy, but Sally didn't mind too much. One day Joe suggested to Sally that they both wear suits for their upcoming birthday party. Joe said he could buy Sally a new suit of her own, so she happily agreed.

At the shop Joe pointed out a blue suit to Sally and said it would look perfect on her. But Sally thought it was too dull, so she shook her head and pointed to a bright pink suit instead. Joe thought a pink suit looked silly, but he didn't want to be too bossy and so he recommended the pink one to Sally.

Sally was so happy with her new suit and wore it to the party. She received lots of compliments, and Joe was very proud of her. He was glad that he had recommended the pink suit and that it had made Sally so happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a furry rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop and skip around his home in the forest. One day, Benny decided he wanted to try something new. He wanted to jump over a big log that was in his way. 

Benny tried and tried, but he couldn't do it. He felt sad and thought he wasn't successful. But then, his friends came along and cheered him on. They told him to keep trying and not to give up. 

Benny took their advice and tried again. This time, he skipped and hopped and with a big jump, he made it over the log! He felt so happy and proud of himself. From that day on, Benny knew that success comes from trying and not giving up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, Sue's mom asked her to get a pan. Sue was very alert and knew where the pan was. She got the pan and gave it to her mom.

Sue and her mom tried to cook some eggs. At first, they did not succeed. The eggs broke and made a mess. But Sue did not give up. She tried again and again.

Here in a quiet and dusty room they lie, Faded as crumbled stone or shifting sand, Forlorn as ashes, shrivelled, scentless, dry -- Meadows and gardens running through my hand. Dead that shall quicken at the call of Spring, Sleepers to stir beneath June's magic kiss, Though birds pass over, unremembering, And no bee seek here roses that were his. In this brown husk a dale of hawthorn dreams, A cedar in this narrow cell is thrust That will drink deeply of a century's streams, These lilies shall make summer on my dust. Here in their safe and simple house of death, Sealed in their shells a million roses leap; Here I can blow a garden with my breath, And in my hand a forest lies asleep.

name_of_work: Wanting to Die by Anne Sexton
content: Since you ask, most days I cannot remember. I walk in my clothing, unmarked by that voyage. Then the almost unnameable lust returns. Even then I have nothing against life. I know well the grass blades you mention, the furniture you have placed under the sun. But suicides have a special language. Like carpenters they want to know which tools. They never ask why build. Twice I have so simply declared myself, have possessed the enemy, eaten the enemy, have taken on his craft, his magic. In this way, heavy and thoughtful, warmer than oil or water, I have rested, drooling at the mouth-hole. I did not think of my body at needle point. Even the cornea and the leftover urine were gone. Suicides have already betrayed the body. Still-born, they don't always die, but dazzled, they can't forget a drug so sweet that even children would look on and smile. To thrust all that life under your tongue!-- that, all by itself, becomes a passion. Death's a sad Bone; bruised, you'd say, and yet she waits for me, year after year, to so delicately undo an old wound, to empty my breath from its bad prison. Balanced there, suicides sometimes meet, raging at the fruit, a pumped-up moon, leaving the bread they mistook for a kiss, leaving the page of the book carelessly open, something unsaid, the phone off the hook and the love, whatever it was, an infection.

Once upon a time, a little elephant was marching through the jungle. He was very happy and he was singing as he marched.

The elephant was looking for food when he stopped at a big tree. The elephant heard a squeaking noise and he saw a trunk poking out of the tree. He was so excited and he reached out to touch it.

The elephant shook the trunk and the trunk opened. Inside the trunk were lots of yummy treats. The elephant munched the treats and he was so delighted that he started to march again.

He was so happy that he decided to take the trunk with him. The trunk was very clean, so the elephant was careful not to make it dirty. 

The elephant put the trunk on his back and marched on, singing and eating treats from his trunk as he went.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the doctor. The doctor was nice and had a clear smile. Tim was a bit scared, but he knew the doctor would help him feel better.

While the doctor looked at Tim, they heard a loud noise outside. They both paused and listened. It was a big dog and a small cat fighting. The doctor and Tim went out to see what was happening.

The doctor tried to stop the fight, but the big dog was very angry. The small cat ran away, but the big dog bit the doctor's hand. The doctor was hurt and sad. Tim was sad too, because the doctor could not help him anymore. They both went home with a bad day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. She was three years old and liked to touch things.

One day she went to the market with her mom. All the fruits were so colorful and bright. Mia saw a yellow lemon and wanted to touch it.

Mia's mom said, "No Mia! Lemons are sour." But Mia didn't listen and touched the lemon anyway. She was so surprised at how sour it was!

Mia then saw a deaf man sitting all alone in the corner. She felt sorry for him and went up to him. Mia touched his hand and he smiled at her.

Mia and her mom then went home, but Mia still remembered how she touched the lemon and the deaf man. She smiled and thought how nice it was to touch them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and his favorite toy was a soft teddy bear. One day, Timmy's teddy bear got stuck on a high shelf and he couldn't reach it. 

Timmy asked his mom for help. "Mommy, can you help me get my teddy bear?" he said. 

"Sure, Timmy. Let's stretch our arms up high and try to reach it together," his mom replied. 

They stretched their arms up high and finally, Timmy's mom was able to reach the teddy bear. Timmy was so happy to have his favorite toy back in his arms. As he hugged his teddy bear, he heard a soft whistle sound coming from inside the bear. 

"Mommy, listen! My teddy bear is whistling!" Timmy exclaimed. 

His mom smiled and said, "That's the sound of the wind going through the bear's soft fur. It's like a little secret whistle just for you." 

Timmy hugged his teddy bear even tighter, feeling grateful for his mom's help and the special secret whistle.

Tom and Lily were playing in the living room with their toys. Tom had a new car that was very expensive. His dad gave it to him for his birthday. Lily had a doll that she loved very much. She got it from her mom.

"Can I play with your car, Tom?" Lily asked.

"No, it's mine. You can't touch it. It's too expensive. You might break it," Tom said.

"Please, Tom. Just for a little bit. I'll be careful. You can play with my doll," Lily said.

"No, no, no. Your doll is boring. Go away," Tom said.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to play with the car. She thought Tom was mean. She waited until Tom was not looking. Then she grabbed the car and ran away. Tom saw her and shouted.

"Hey, give me back my car. That's not yours. That's stealing," Tom said.

He chased Lily around the house. Lily tried to hide, but Tom found her. He grabbed the car from her hands. He was very mad. He pushed Lily to the floor. Lily dropped her doll. The doll's head broke off.

Lily started to cry. She looked at her doll. She loved her doll. Now her doll was broken. She felt very bad.

"Look what you did. You broke my car. You scratched it. It's ruined. You're a bad sister. I hate you," Tom said.

He threw the car on the couch. He didn't care about it anymore. He went to his room and slammed the door.

Lily was still crying. She picked up her doll. She tried to put the head back on, but it didn't work. She hugged her doll. She wished Tom would say sorry. She wished he would forgive her. She wished they could play together again. But Tom didn't come out of his room. He didn't say anything. He didn't forgive her. He was still angry. Lily felt very lonely. She wished she had a nice brother. She wished she had a new doll. She wished she had never touched the car. But it was too late. She had made a big mistake. And she had to live with it. The end.

When the swift-rolling brook, swollen deep, Rushes on by the alders, full speed, And the wild-blowing winds lowly sweep O'er the quivering leaf and the weed, And the willow tree writhes in each limb, Over sedge-reeds that reel by the brim -- The man that is staggering by Holds his hat to his head by the brim; And the girl, as her hair-locks outfly, Puts a foot out, to keep herself trim, And the quivering wavelings o'erspread The small pool where the bird dips his head. But out at my house, in the lee Of the nook, where the winds die away, The light swimming airs, round the tree And the low-swinging ivy stem, play So soft that a mother that's nigh Her still cradle may hear her babe sigh.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play in the river. One day, he saw a mule walking by and asked if it wanted to play with him. The mule said yes and they began to splash in the river together. 

Suddenly, Timmy noticed something unusual about the mule. It had wings! Timmy was amazed and asked, "How did you get wings?" The mule replied, "I was born with them. I'm a special mule." 

Timmy was so happy to have made a new friend and they continued to splash and play together in the river. From that day on, Timmy and the unusual winged mule were the best of friends and would often be seen splashing in the river together.

Once upon a time, there was a healthy fox. The fox lived in a big forest. He had many friends like the birds, the bugs, and the rabbits. They all liked to play together.

One day, the fox saw a big rock. He wanted to lift the rock and see what was under it. He tried very hard to lift the rock, but it was too heavy. He asked his friends to help him lift the rock.

The birds, the bugs, and the rabbits all helped the fox to lift the big rock. Under the rock, they found a lot of yummy food. They all shared the food and had a big party. The healthy fox and his friends were very happy.

name_of_work: To Be in Love by Gwendolyn Brooks
content: To be in love Is to touch with a lighter hand. In yourself you stretch, you are well. You look at things Through his eyes. A cardinal is red. A sky is blue. Suddenly you know he knows too. He is not there but You know you are tasting together The winter, or a light spring weather. His hand to take your hand is overmuch. Too much to bear. You cannot look in his eyes Because your pulse must not say What must not be said. When he Shuts a door- Is not there_ Your arms are water. And you are free With a ghastly freedom. You are the beautiful half Of a golden hurt. You remember and covet his mouth To touch, to whisper on. Oh when to declare Is certain Death! Oh when to apprize Is to mesmerize, To see fall down, the Column of Gold, Into the commonest ash.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to go on a trip with her family. She wanted to bring her luggage with her. She was proud of her luggage because it was pink with sparkles.

Lily's family went on the trip and they had a lot of fun. But when they were on their way back home, they lost Lily's luggage. Lily was very sad because she wanted her luggage back. She cried and cried.

Lily's family tried to find her luggage, but they couldn't. They looked everywhere, but it was gone. Lily was very upset and her family felt bad for her. The end.

name_of_work: 1st Date She and 1st Date He by Wendy Cope
content: I said I liked classical music. It wasn't exactly a lie. I hoped he would get the impression That my brow was acceptably high. I said I liked classical music. I mentioned Vivaldi and Bach. And he asked me along to this concert. Here we are, sitting in the half-dark. I was thrilled to be asked to this concert. I couldn't care less what they play But I'm trying my hardest to listen So I'll have something clever to say. When I glance at his face it's a picture Of rapt concentration. I see He is totally into this music And quite undistracted by me. 1st Date - He She said she liked classical music. I implied I was keen on it too. Though I don't often go to a concert, It wasn't entirely untrue. I looked for a suitable concert And here we are, on our first date. The traffic was dreadful this evening And I arrived ten minutes late. So we haven't had much time for talking And I'm a bit nervous. I see She is totally lost in the music And quite undistracted by me. In that dress she is very attractive - The neckline can't fail to intrigue. I musn't appear too besotted. Perhaps she is out of my league. Where are we? I glance at the programme But I've put my glasses away. I'd better start paying attention Or else I'll have nothing to say.

Summer is late, my heart. Words plucked out of the air some forty years ago when I was wild with love and torn almost in two scatter like leaves this night of whistling wind and rain. It is my heart that's late, it is my song that's flown. Outdoors all afternoon under a gunmetal sky staking my garden down, I kneeled to the crickets trilling underfoot as if about to burst from their crusty shells; and like a child again marveled to hear so clear and brave a music pour from such a small machine. What makes the engine go? Desire, desire, desire. The longing for the dance stirs in the buried life. One season only, and it's done. So let the battered old willow thrash against the windowpanes and the house timbers creak. Darling, do you remember the man you married? Touch me, remind me who I am.

Anna and Ben wanted to give a gift to their baby brother, Sam. They had a soft toy horse that Sam liked to play with. They decided to wrap the toy horse with some paper and a ribbon. They looked for some paper and a ribbon in their room.

"Look, Anna, I found some paper with stars on it. Sam likes stars," Ben said.

"Good, Ben, you are clever. And I found a ribbon that is red. Sam likes red," Anna said.

They put the toy horse on the paper and folded the paper around it. Then they tied the ribbon in a bow. They were happy with their gift.

They ran to the living room, where Sam was sitting in his crib. They put the gift next to him and said, "Surprise, Sam! We have a gift for you. Open it and see what it is."

Sam smiled and reached for the gift. He tore the paper and saw the toy horse. He hugged the toy horse and said, "Horse, horse, I love horse. Thank you, Anna, thank you, Ben."

Anna and Ben hugged Sam and said, "You are welcome, Sam. We love you."

They played with the toy horse and pretended it was a real horse. They made it run and jump and neigh. They said it lived in a stable with other horses. They had a lot of fun.

Jenny loves to slide on the big slide at the park. She likes to go fast and feel the wind in her hair. She always wears her favorite jewelry, a pink necklace and a blue bracelet, that her mommy gave her for her birthday.

One day, she went to the park with her daddy and saw a new girl on the slide. The girl had long curly hair and shiny jewelry. She had earrings, rings, and a necklace that sparkled in the sun. Jenny wanted to slide, but the girl was taking too long. She was sliding slowly and stopping in the middle. Jenny was impatient. She wanted to slide now.

"Move, please!" Jenny said to the girl. "I want to slide!"

The girl looked at Jenny and frowned. "No, you move!" she said. "This is my slide! You can't slide here!"

Jenny was angry. She didn't like the girl. She thought she was mean and greedy. She wanted to slide and have fun, not fight. She looked at the girl's jewelry and had an idea.

"Your jewelry is pretty," Jenny said. "Can I see it?"

The girl smiled. She liked compliments. She thought Jenny was nice and wanted to be friends. She nodded and took off her earrings, rings, and necklace. She handed them to Jenny.

"Here, you can look at them," she said. "But be careful. They are very special."

Jenny took the jewelry and pretended to admire them. She said, "Wow, they are so shiny and pretty. Can I try them on?"

The girl hesitated. She didn't want to share her jewelry. But she wanted to be nice to Jenny. She said, "Okay, but only for a minute. Then you have to give them back."

Jenny nodded and put on the jewelry. She felt very fancy and happy. She said, "Thank you. You are very kind. Can I slide with them?"

The girl was surprised. She didn't expect Jenny to ask that. She said, "No, you can't slide with them. They might fall off or break. You have to take them off and give them back."

Jenny shook her head. She didn't want to give them back. She wanted to keep them. She said, "No, I like them. They are mine now. Bye!"

Jenny ran to the slide and slid down as fast as she could. She laughed and waved at the girl. She didn't care about the girl. She only cared about the jewelry.

The girl was shocked and angry. She screamed and cried. She wanted her jewelry back. She ran after Jenny and tried to catch her. But Jenny was too fast. She ran away with the jewelry.

Jenny was happy. She had the jewelry and the slide. She thought she was smart and clever. She didn't know that she was rude and selfish. She didn't know that she hurt the girl's feelings. She didn't know that she made a bad choice. She didn't know that she would get in trouble. She only knew that she liked to slide and wear jewelry.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. The sun was bright and the water was calm. Tim loved to play in the sand and watch the waves.

As Tim was playing, he saw a dolphin appear in the water. The dolphin was happy and jumped high in the air. Tim was excited and called his mom to see the dolphin.

"Mom, look! A dolphin!" Tim said. His mom came and they both watched the dolphin play in the water. They felt happy and calm as they enjoyed their day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who flew to an unknown land. The clouds were glowing and the sun was shining. As she looked down, she saw something in the distance - a giant cauliflower. She smiled and flew down to explore.

When she reached the cauliflower, she saw a small doorway at the base. She stepped through the door and found herself in a world full of strange, colourful creatures. 

The creatures spotted her and ran over. She smiled and asked, â€œWho are you?â€

The creatures smiled and said, â€œWe are the Glowy People! We live here and glow so brightly! We make our homes in the Cauliflower and like to explore unknown lands. Welcome!â€

The girl was amazed. She grinned and said, â€œThis is so cool! I can't wait to explore and learn more.â€

The Glowy People cheered and they all set off, glowing and exploring the unknown land.

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom and dad at home. One day, her mom asked her to spread a big sheet on the mattress. Lily was so excited to help her mom.

Lily went to her room and found the big sheet. She carefully spread it over the mattress. She made sure there were no bumps or wrinkles. She felt so proud of her work.

Later, Lily's mom came to see the room. She was so happy to see the mattress with the sheet spread on it. She gave Lily a big hug and said, "Thank you for being such a good helper!" Lily smiled and knew she had done a great job.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy robot that she loved very much. One day, the robot's eye started to blink very fast. Lily didn't know what to do, so she asked her dad for help. Her dad took a screwdriver and opened up the robot's eye. He found a loose screw inside and fixed it. 

The robot's eye stopped blinking and Lily was very happy. She played with her robot all day long. But later that night, Lily noticed that her dad was not responding when she talked to him. She called out to him louder and louder, but he didn't hear her. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. 

Then she remembered what her dad had said earlier that day when he fixed the robot's eye. He told her that sometimes things can't work right if they have a screw loose. Lily realized that her dad must have a screw loose too, but not in his eye, in his ear! She tapped her dad on the shoulder and he turned around. He had been wearing headphones and didn't hear her. Lily was relieved and hugged her dad tightly.

Once upon a time there lived Noreen, a brave little girl who lived all alone in a tiny house in the countryside. She was very lonely and wished she had someone to help her out, like a best friend. 

One day, Noreen heard a soft voice coming from outside. She looked out the window and saw a butterfly perched on a tree branch. 

"Who are you?" asked Noreen.

"I'm a special butterfly!" said the butterfly in a musical voice. "My name is Jenny and I'm here to help you find a special treasure!"

Noreen was so excited! She and Jenny set off into the forest, searching for the treasure all day. Finally, after a long journey, they reached the top of a hill with a small cave at its centre. 

"This is it!" said Jenny. "Let's say a prayer before we go in to find the treasure."

The two said a short prayer and then entered the cave. Inside, they found the treasure they'd been searching for all day. Noreen was so happy. She hugged Jenny and thanked her for helping her find her special treasure.

And that is how Noreen and Jenny became best friends - all thanks to a special treasure and a simple prayer.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden with their dog, Max. Max is a big and friendly dog, but sometimes he is too loud and messy. He likes to dig holes, chase birds and bark at cars.

One day, Anna and Ben's mom tells them to behave. She says she has to cook dinner and they have to be calm and quiet. She gives them a basket and tells them to pick some herbs from the garden. She says herbs are good for food and they smell nice.

Anna and Ben take the basket and go to the garden. They see some green plants with small leaves. They smell them and they like them. They pick some mint, basil and parsley and put them in the basket. They are careful not to step on the flowers or break the stems.

Max follows them and sniffs the herbs. He thinks they are funny and he wants to play with them. He jumps on the basket and tries to grab some herbs with his mouth. He makes a lot of noise and scatters the herbs on the ground.

Anna and Ben are not happy. They shout at Max and tell him to stop. They say he is a bad dog and he does not behave. They try to pick up the herbs and put them back in the basket.

Max does not understand. He thinks they are playing with him and he wants to join. He wags his tail and licks their faces. He does not mean to be naughty, he just wants to have fun.

Anna and Ben's mom hears the noise and comes to the garden. She sees the mess and the herbs. She is not angry, but she is not pleased. She tells Max to sit and stay. She tells Anna and Ben to finish picking the herbs and bring them to the kitchen. She says they have to be more careful and teach Max to behave. She says she loves them and Max, but they have to be calm and quiet.

Anna and Ben nod and say sorry. They hug Max and tell him to be a good dog. They finish picking the herbs and bring them to the kitchen. They help their mom wash and chop the herbs and add them to the food. They smell the food and they think it is yummy. They are proud of their work and they are calm and quiet. They wait for dinner and they hope Max will behave.

name_of_work: Canal Bank Walk by Patrick Kavanagh
content: Leafy-with-love banks and the green waters of the canal Pouring redemption for me, that I do The will of God, wallow in the habitual, the banal, Grow with nature again as before I grew. The bright stick trapped, the breeze adding a third Party to the couple kissing on an old seat, And a bird gathering materials for the nest for the Word Eloquently new and abandoned to its delirious beat. O unworn world enrapture me, encapture me in a web Of fabulous grass and eternal voices by a beech, Feed the gaping need of my senses, give me ad lib To pray unselfconsciously with overflowing speech For this soul needs to be honoured with a new dress woven From green and blue things and arguments that cannot be proven.

Once there was a girl who loved pretty things. She bought a colorful vase from the store and admired it every day. One day, the girl realized that the vase had changed! Inside was a colorful surprise - a brightly colored parrot. 

The parrot looked at the girl, and the girl looked at the parrot. It was very friendly, so the girl decided to keep it. She named him Alvin. 

Alvin soon recognized the girl as his friend, and started to follow her everywhere she went. Everywhere the girl went, Alvin would sit in the colorful vase, and watch with his bright eyes. The girl and Alvin were very happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who had a big, happy birthday. She put on a pretty dress and everyone was excited. 

The princess wanted to get married, so she looked for a prince. She found a prince who was rough and brave. He asked her to marry him and she said yes. 

The village people held a big party for the princess and the prince. They put up decorations, made food and shared stories. Everyone was very happy for the princess.

At the end of the day, the princess and the prince said 'I do'. They hugged each other and everyone applauded. 

The princess was so happy to be married to the prince. They were now together and that made her even more excited for her birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she was digging in her backyard when she found a small radio buried in the ground. 

"Mommy, look what I found!" Lily exclaimed, holding up the radio for her mom to see. 

Her mom was surprised and asked, "Where did you find that, Lily?" 

"I found it buried in the dirt," Lily replied. 

Her mom turned on the radio, but it was very boring music that played. "Let's bury it again," her mom suggested. 

So, Lily and her mom buried the radio back in the ground and continued to play outside, enjoying the beautiful day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl. She had a cozy sweater that she loved to wear. One day, she was playing in the park with all her toys. Suddenly, one of her toys disappeared! She looked all around, but the toy was nowhere to be seen. Feeling sad, the little girl asked her mom, "Where did it go?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "It must have gone away. Let's look together, and we might find it again."

So, the little girl and her mom searched all around the park, but the toy was nowhere to be found. After looking for a while, her mom said, "Let's go home; it's getting late. I'm sure the toy will come back soon."

The little girl smiled and put on her cozy sweater. She cheered up and waved goodbye to her toy! Then, they both went home together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her red cap everywhere she went. One day, while playing in the park, she met a boy named Max. Max had a blue cap on his head.

"Hi, I like your cap," said Lily.

"Thank you, I like your cap too," replied Max.

Lily looked at Max's cap and said, "Your cap is so flexible, it can bend in any direction. I believe my cap is not as flexible as yours."

Max smiled and said, "That's okay, we can still be friends even if our caps are different." And so, Lily and Max became good friends and played together in the park every day while wearing their favorite caps.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old cat. The cat did not like anyone and always hissed at people. One day, a little girl found a watch on the ground. She thought it was pretty and wanted to keep it safe, so she put it in her pocket. 

Later that day, the little girl saw the grumpy cat in the street. She wanted to be friends with the cat and show it the watch, but the cat did not want to be friends. The cat scratched the little girl and ran away. 

The little girl was sad and went to the store to buy a bandage for her scratch. While she was there, she saw the grumpy cat again. The cat knocked over a shelf and made a big mess. The store owner was very angry and yelled at the cat. The cat ran away again, but this time it got hit by a car and did not survive. 

The little girl was very sad that the cat had died. She wished she could have been friends with the cat and shown it the pretty watch. But now, she would never get the chance.

The sun was shining in the wide open fields. The bright yellow sun lit up the green grass, where two cows were grazing. One of the cows, named Tim, was obedient and did as he was told, unlike the other cow, Bess.

"Bess, don't you dare go close to the edge of the field," Tim said.

But Bess, the more adventurous cow, wasn't listening. She kept on walking closer and closer, until she was at the edge of the field.

Suddenly, Bess heard a loud voice. 

"Bess, I dare you to jump over the fence," said the voice.

Bess was scared at first, but then she felt brave.

"I can do it," she thought.

With a big jump, Bess cleared the fence and landed safely on the other side.

Tim saw the whole thing and was amazed.

"Wow, Bess, you were so obedient and brave!" said Tim. 

Bess smiled and neighed proudly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat yummy snacks like cookies and candy. One day, she went on a long walk in the hot sun with her family. They were very thirsty and tired.

Suddenly, they saw a small oasis with cool water and green trees. Lily's dad split the watermelon he brought and it was very tasty. They all felt happy and refreshed. They rested under the shade of the trees and played games together.

Lily felt grateful for the oasis and the tasty snack. She knew that even though the walk was long, it was worth it to find such a special place. From then on, she always remembered to bring snacks and water on their adventures.

Once upon a time, there lived a wise old man. He was so wise that everyone in the village asked him for help and advice.

The old man loved everyone in the village, and everyone loved him. He especially loved spending time on the floor, watching the children play.

One day, the old man saw a small child dancing on the floor. He smiled when he saw the child twirling around. The old man thought to himself, how can someone so young be so wise?

The old man stood up and asked the child to dance with him. The child smiled and held out his hand.

The two danced together for a long time, until the sun started to set. The old man said goodbye and thanked the child for dancing.

The old man walked away, feeling warm and happy. He knew that genuine love was the most important thing in life.

Mum was cooking dinner. It smelt so good. John said to Mum, â€œWhat are you making?â€ 

Mum replied, â€œI am making soup.â€

John asked, â€œCan I help?â€

But Mum said, â€œNo, you have to take your medicine.â€ 

So John grabbed the medicine and went outside. He looked up at the light blue sky. It was so pretty. 

John tried to work out a way to not take the medicine. But nothing worked. So John had to take the medicine. He was very sad. 

John was so unhappy that he lay down in the grass and cried. His tears were wet and he felt so alone. 

John finished his medicine and he said goodbye. He never felt so bad about taking medicine.

name_of_work: A Helpmeet For Him by Christina Rossetti
content: Woman was made for man's delight,-- Charm, O woman! Be not afraid! His shadow by day, his moon by night, Woman was made. Her strength with weakness is overlaid; Meek compliances veil her might; Him she stays, by whom she is stayed. World-wide champion of truth and right, Hope in gloom, and in danger aid, Tender and faithful, ruddy and white, Woman was made.

name_of_work: I Looked Up from My Writing by Thomas Hardy
content: I looked up from my writing, And gave a start to see, As if rapt in my inditing, The moon's full gaze on me. Her meditative misty head Was spectral in its air, And I involuntarily said, 'What are you doing there?' 'Oh, I've been scanning pond and hole And waterway hereabout For the body of one with a sunken soul Who has put his life-light out. 'Did you hear his frenzied tattle? It was sorrow for his son Who is slain in brutish battle, Though he has injured none. 'And now I am curious to look Into the blinkered mind Of one who wants to write a book In a world of such a kind.' Her temper overwrought me, And I edged to shun her view, For I felt assured she thought me One who should drown him too.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fierce lion. He was so scary that he roared all the time. All the animals in the forest ran away whenever they heard the lion's roar! 

One day, a little, shy rabbit heard the lion's roar and was scared. He looked around and saw a door. He thought it might be safe behind the door, so he hopped over, opened it, and hopped inside.

The lion heard the door open and close. He thought it was one of the other animals, so he ran over to the door and roared. He was so loud and so scary that the door shook and the rabbit shivered.

But the rabbit stayed really still and stayed really quiet. So the lion moved on and didn't notice the rabbit had been there.

The rabbit was so thankful for the door. He had been so shy, but the door kept him safe from the roaring lion.

All through that summer at ease we lay, And daily from the turret wall We watched the mowers in the hay And the enemy half a mile away They seemed no threat to us at all. For what, we thought, had we to fear With our arms and provender, load on load, Our towering battlements, tier on tier, And friendly allies drawing near On every leafy summer road. Our gates were strong, our walls were thick, So smooth and high, no man could win A foothold there, no clever trick Could take us, have us dead or quick. Only a bird could have got in. What could they offer us for bait? Our captain was brave and we were true.... There was a little private gate, A little wicked wicket gate. The wizened warder let them through. Oh then our maze of tunneled stone Grew thin and treacherous as air. The cause was lost without a groan, The famous citadel overthrown, And all its secret galleries bare. How can this shameful tale be told? I will maintain until my death We could do nothing, being sold; Our only enemy was gold, And we had no arms to fight it with.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sweet treats like candy and ice cream. One day, Lily's mommy took her to the store to buy some candy. Lily was so excited to pick out her favorite sweet treats.

At the store, Lily saw her friend Emma. Emma was also picking out candy. They decided to have a meeting outside the store to share their sweet treats. Lily was happy to share her candy with Emma.

When they got home, Lily's mommy told her that they were going to have a party the next day. Lily wanted to bring her candy to the party, but she also wanted to share it with Emma. She had to decide what to do.

The next day at the party, Lily brought her candy and shared it with all of her friends, including Emma. Everyone was happy and had a sweet time. Lily was glad she decided to share her candy with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big, happy dog named Spot. Spot was very obedient. He always did what his owner, a little girl named Sue, told him to do. They lived in a small house with a pretty garden.

One hot day, Spot and Sue went for a walk in the park. They were very thirsty. They managed to find a beautiful oasis in the park. The oasis had a small pond with clear water and green grass. They were so happy to find this special place.

Spot and Sue played near the oasis all day. They splashed in the water and rolled in the grass. Sue would tell Spot to sit, and he would sit. She would tell him to fetch, and he would fetch. They had lots of fun together. At the end of the day, they went back home, tired but happy from their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a man named John. John had a wife named Mary. John loved Mary very much and was always glad to see her. One day, John was walking in the park when he saw a little girl crying. He went up to her and asked her what was wrong. The little girl said she lost her teddy bear.

John felt sad for the little girl and offered to help her find her teddy bear. They looked all over the park, but they couldn't find it. John was about to give up when he saw something in the bushes. It was the little girl's teddy bear! John was glad he could help the little girl.

As John was walking home, he realized he had lost his wallet. He was worried because he needed his wallet to buy groceries for his wife. John searched everywhere but couldn't find it. He was about to give up when he remembered the little girl he helped. He went back to the park and found his wallet where he had been searching with the little girl. John was glad he could find his wallet and buy groceries for his wife.

name_of_work: Love in a Life by Robert Browning
content: I Room after room, I hunt the house through We inhabit together. Heart, fear nothing, for, heart, thou shalt find her-- Next time, herself!--not the trouble behind her Left in the curtain, the couch's perfume! As she brushed it, the cornice-wreath blossomed anew: Yon looking-glass gleamed at the wave of her feather. II Yet the day wears, And door succeeds door; I try the fresh fortune-- Range the wide house from the wing to the centre. Still the same chance! she goes out as I enter. Spend my whole day in the quest,--who cares? But 'tis twilight, you see,--with such suites to explore, Such closets to search, such alcoves to importune!

Once upon a time there were two people who were very happy. Their names were Mommy and Daddy. They really loved each other.

One day Mommy and Daddy decided to bring marriage to their lives. Marriage is when two people love each other forever.

They went to the church and said special words. Then they had a light party. Everyone was there and they were so happy!

At the end of the day they hugged and kissed and said they would always love each other. 

Mommy and Daddy's marriage was very special and full of light. And they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a friendly deer. He was so thoughtful, he always wanted to share his special mushrooms with everyone he met. 
One day, the deer met a sly fox. The fox said he wanted to share the mushrooms too, but he had a sneaky plan. 
The deer agreed to share the mushrooms and the fox grabbed them all. As soon as the fox had the mushrooms, he ran away.
The deer was so sad. He had been so kind and thoughtful but the fox tricked him. The deer was sad and never shared his mushrooms again.

Once upon a time there was a loyal animal named Pat. Pat was always very curious and loved to explore. One day Pat decided to take a test. She wanted to know if she was as smart as the other animals. She went to the exam room and was scared at first.

Pat saw the exam and was confused. She thought, "What kind of test is this?" She asked her friend, "What is this test about?"

Her friend explained, "This test will show how smart you are and if you are loyal". Pat was scared, but loyal. She took a deep breath and started the exam. After she finished the exam, Pat was very proud of herself. She knew she was loyal and smart and had passed the test.

name_of_work: A Dream by Edgar Allan Poe
content: In visions of the dark night I have dreamed of joy departed-- But a waking dream of life and light Hath left me broken-hearted. Ah! what is not a dream by day To him whose eyes are cast On things around him with a ray Turned back upon the past? That holy dream--that holy dream, While all the world were chiding, Hath cheered me as a lovely beam A lonely spirit guiding. What though that light, thro' storm and night, So trembled from afar-- What could there be more purely bright In Truth's day-star?

Once upon a time, there was a market. It was smelly, but very fun. Lilly and Jake loved to go there and explore all the colorful fruits and vegetables. 

One day, they sat down on a bench and watched the people in the market. They saw the fishmonger and the fruit stand. They saw the birds flying by and they waved to the old man walking around. 

They were having so much fun. Then, they saw the most beautiful thing. It was a smelly flower stand. Lilly loved flowers, so she went to take a closer look. She smiled as she saw all the different colors and sizes. 

Then they decided it was time to go home. As they left the market, Jake and Lilly waved goodbye, until they couldn't see the market anymore. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with puzzles, but she only had one puzzle, and it was very ugly. One day, she went to her friend Timmy's house to play. Timmy had many puzzles, and they were all very pretty.

Lily said, "Timmy, can I play with your puzzles?"

Timmy said, "Sure, which one do you want to play with?"

Lily said, "I want to play with the pretty one."

Timmy said, "Okay, but you have to return it when you're done."

Lily played with the pretty puzzle for a long time, but eventually, she got tired of it. She returned the pretty puzzle to Timmy and said, "Thank you for letting me play with your puzzle. My puzzle is ugly, but I still like it."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun, and her favorite place to go was the creek. She would spend hours there, splashing in the water and looking for rocks.

One day, Lily's friend Tommy came to play with her. He was a fat little boy with a big smile on his face. "Hi Lily!" he said. "Can I come play at the creek with you?"

"Sure!" said Lily. "We can spend the whole day there!"

So the two friends ran down to the creek and started playing. They found some sticks and pretended they were fishing poles. "I caught a big one!" said Tommy, holding up his stick.

Lily laughed. "That's not a fish, silly. It's just a stick." They played and laughed until the sun started to go down. "I had so much fun today," said Tommy. "Let's come back and spend the whole day here again soon!"

Once there was a special lemon tree, it was pink! Every day it showed off its beauty and spread happiness to all its friends.

One day some birds came to visit. They said, "What a beautiful tree, what can it do?" 

The pink lemon tree smiled and said, "I can bloom. When I bloom, my lemons cheer everyone up."

The birds were astonished. They asked, "How does it work?" The tree said, "When summer arrives, I blossom and big, juicy lemons come out of me. People can pick them and use them to make lemonade." 

The birds were very excited and clapped in joy. They thanked the pink lemon tree for being so kind and for showing them its special talent. From that day on, the birds spread the word about the special pink lemon tree and its ability to bloom.

name_of_work: Fiddler Jones by Edgar Lee Masters
content: The earth keeps some vibration going There in your heart, and that is you. And if the people find you can fiddle, Why, fiddle you must, for all your life. What do you see, a harvest of clover? Or a meadow to walk through to the river? The wind's in the corn; you rub your hands For beeves hereafter ready for market; Or else you hear the rustle of skirts Like the girls when dancing at Little Grove. To Cooney Potter a pillar of dust Or whirling leaves meant ruinous drouth; They looked to me like Red-Head Sammy Stepping it off, to "Toor-a-Loor." How could I till my forty acres Not to speak of getting more, With a medley of horns, bassoons and piccolos Stirred in my brain by crows and robins And the creak of a wind-mill--only these? And I never started to plow in my life That some one did not stop in the road And take me away to a dance or picnic. I ended up with forty acres; I ended up with a broken fiddle-- And a broken laugh, and a thousand memories, And not a single regret.

Tom and Mia like to play on the porch. The porch has a smooth floor and a big door. The door has a lock. Tom and Mia can open and close the door, but they cannot turn the lock.

One day, Tom and Mia are playing on the porch with their toys. They have a ball, a doll, a car and a book. They have fun throwing the ball, dressing the doll, driving the car and looking at the book.

"Let's play hide and seek!" Tom says. "I will count and you will hide."

"OK!" Mia says. She runs to find a hiding spot. She sees the door and thinks it is a good place to hide. She opens the door and goes inside. She closes the door behind her.

Tom counts to ten. "Ready or not, here I come!" he says. He looks for Mia on the porch. He does not see her. He looks under the chairs, behind the plants, in the box. He does not find her.

"Mia, where are you?" he calls. He hears a voice from inside the door.

"Tom, I'm here! I'm in the door!" Mia says.

Tom goes to the door and tries to open it. It does not open. He pushes and pulls. It does not move.

"Mia, the door is locked!" he says.

"What? How?" Mia says.

"I don't know. Maybe you turned the lock by mistake." Tom says.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to. Can you get the key?" Mia says.

"I don't know where the key is. Mom and Dad have the key. They are not here. They went to the store." Tom says.

"Oh no, what can we do?" Mia says.

Tom and Mia are scared and sad. They cry and yell for help. They hope Mom and Dad will come back soon and unlock the door. They miss each other and want to play together again.

There was a little girl named Sadie who liked to lift cubes. Sadie liked to lift all kinds of cubes - big ones, small ones, red ones and blue ones. One day, she found a special cube. It was small and easy to lift. 

Sadie carefully lifted the cube and discovered something inside. It was a toy train! Sadie was so excited. She lifted the cube over and over again to play with the toy train. 

Sadie played with the cube and the train all morning. But eventually, she had to stop to go to lunch. She carefully lifted the cube and put the train back inside, then put the cube back where she had found it.

The next day, Sadie went back to find the cube. She found it again, and with an easy lift, discovered that it held another surprise - a stuffed bear! Sadie smiled as she lifted the cube, ready to start playing with her new toy.

name_of_work: Have You Earned Your Tomorrow by Edgar Guest
content: Is anybody happier because you passed his way? Does anyone remember that you spoke to him today? This day is almost over, and its toiling time is through; Is there anyone to utter now a kindly word of you? Did you give a cheerful greeting to the friend who came along? Or a churlish sort of "Howdy" and then vanish in the throng? Were you selfish pure and simple as you rushed along the way, Or is someone mighty grateful for a deed you did today? Can you say tonight, in parting with the day that's slipping fast, That you helped a single brother of the many that you passed? Is a single heart rejoicing over what you did or said; Does a man whose hopes were fading now with courage look ahead? Did you waste the day, or lose it, was it well or sorely spent? Did you leave a trail of kindness or a scar of discontent? As you close your eyes in slumber do you think that God would say, You have earned one more tomorrow by the work you did today?

In Chicago, it is snowing softly and a man has just done his wash for the week. He steps into the twilight of early evening, carrying a wrinkled shopping bag full of neatly folded clothes, and, for a moment, enjoys the feel of warm laundry and crinkled paper, flannellike against his gloveless hands. There's a Rembrandt glow on his face, a triangle of orange in the hollow of his cheek as a last flash of sunset blazes the storefronts and lit windows of the street. He is Asian, Thai or Vietnamese, and very skinny, dressed as one of the poor in rumpled suit pants and a plaid mackinaw, dingy and too large. He negotiates the slick of ice on the sidewalk by his car, opens the Fairlane's back door, leans to place the laundry in, and turns, for an instant, toward the flurry of footsteps and cries of pedestrians as a boy--that's all he was-- backs from the corner package store shooting a pistol, firing it, once, at the dumbfounded man who falls forward, grabbing at his chest. A few sounds escape from his mouth, a babbling no one understands as people surround him bewildered at his speech. The noises he makes are nothing to them. The boy has gone, lost in the light array of foot traffic dappling the snow with fresh prints. Tonight, I read about Descartes' grand courage to doubt everything except his own miraculous existence and I feel so distinct from the wounded man lying on the concrete I am ashamed. Let the night sky cover him as he dies. Let the weaver girl cross the bridge of heaven and take up his cold hands.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat yogurt. One day, he found an old yogurt cup in his room. It looked ancient. He wanted to know what was inside.

Tim decided to examine the yogurt cup. He opened the lid and looked inside. He saw some yogurt, but it was a strange color. It was not like the yogurt he usually ate.

Tim showed the ancient yogurt cup to his mom. She told him it was too old to eat. Tim was sad, but his mom gave him a new yogurt cup. Tim was happy again. He ate the new yogurt and played with his toys.

Once there was a girl named Jane. She was only 3-years-old, and loved her parents very much.

One day, Jane heard her mom and dad talking in the living room. She couldn't understand what they were saying, so she stuck her head in the door. 

Dad saw her and spoke to her in a gentle voice. "Why don't you come in and join us?"

Jane was shy, but she walked over to where her parents were sitting. Then she looked up and said, "I want a reliable nose."

Mom and Dad looked at each other and smiled. Then Dad said, "That's a good idea. We'll get you a reliable nose!"

The next day, Mom and Dad took Jane to the store, where she saw lots of different noses. After looking around for a little while, she chose one she liked best. It was a small, pink nose that fit her just right.

Then Jane went back home with Mom and Dad and proudly showed them her new, reliable nose. 

From then on, Jane always had a reliable nose, and Mom and Dad were always there to support her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to search for treasure in her backyard. One day, she found a shiny rock and showed it to her mom.

"Mommy, look what I found! It's so pretty!" said Lily.

Her mom smiled and said, "That's nice, Lily. Do you know what language people speak in the country where that rock came from?"

Lily shook her head. "No, I don't know. Can you tell me?"

"Sure, it's called Spanish. Maybe we can learn some words in that language together," said her mom.

Lily's face lit up with excitement. "That sounds like fun! But first, we have to clean this rock so it shines even more!"

name_of_work: The Green Beret by Ho Thien
content: He was twelve years old And I do not know his name The mercenaries took him and his father, Whose name I do not know, One morning upon the High Plateau. Green Beret looked down on the frail boy With the eyes of a hurt animal and thought, A good fright will make him talk. He commanded, and the father was taken away Behind the forest's green wall. 'Right kid tell us where they are, Tell us where or your father - dead.' With eyes now bright and filled with horror The slight boy said nothing. 'you've got one minute kid,' said Green Beret, 'tell us where or we kill father,' And thrust his wrist-watch against a face all eyes, The second-hand turning, jerking on its way. 'O.K. boy ten seconds to tell us where they are.' In the last instant the silver hand shattered the Sky and the forest of trees. 'Kill the old guy,' roared Green Beret And shots hammered out Behind the forest's green wall And sky and trees and soldiers stood In silence, and the boy cried out. Green Beret stood In silence, as the boy crouched down And shook with tears, As children do when their father dies. 'Christ,' said one mercenary to Green Beret, 'he didn't know a damn thing We killed the old guy for nothing,' So they all went away, Green Beret and his mercenaries. And the boy knew everything. He knew everything about them, the caves, The trails, the hidden places and names, And in the moment that he cried out, In that same instant, Protected by frail tears Far stronger than any wall of steel, They passed everywhere Like tigers Across the High Plateau

Once upon a time there was a little boy who wanted to play in the garage. He ran fast to get there and said, "Yay!" When he opened the garage door, he saw lots of toys. He said, "Wow!" Then he heard a noise outside. He ran to the door and said, "What's that?"

It was his mom, who said, "Come out here and say hi!" The little boy ran out and said, "Hi!" His mom said, "Let's go for a drive!" The little boy said, "Yay!"

They got into the car and drove fast. The little boy said, "Whee!" They drove all around town and the little boy waved out the window at everyone they passed. Finally, they drove back to the garage and the little boy said, "Bye bye car, see you soon!"

Now I wish to tell apart from you-- the kindred of trees I wake from seeds within me.... ... I must set down in another land... the salt streams... Quite often in a boat I sought the spine, the homes of heroes where my manly lord sends me... across lofty halls-- I am now come here on the ship's deck, and now you ought to know how you ponder in your mind the pithy love of my master. I dare a command-- to locate there a tree glory-fast-- What he bids you request then, he who cut this wood so that you would remember yourself his promises treasure-laden in your wit's enclosure, that you two often spoke of in days of old, until you two were allowed in the mead-towns to keep homestead, to inhabit a single land, to make love to each other. Vendetta drove him from his triumphant tribe now he orders you yourself be instructed gladly, to trouble the waters-- afterwards you heard upon the coastal cliffs the mournful cuckoo singing in the boughs. Do not allow yourself to end this journey afterwards-- no living man can hinder your course. Seek already the sea, the homestead of gulls-- be seated in a seaward ship, so that you may find your husband-- to the south from here across the way of waters, where your lord dwells in your hopes and dreams. Nor can worldly desire suit him more in his mind, of this he said to me, when All-Wielding God should grant us two... together afterwards we are allowed to before men and friends... nailed rings--he holds enough decorous gold... strangers hold homewards the fair earth.... ... heroes, though here my friends... impelled by need rushing out on a ship youthful upon the waves must go forth upon the ship-ways, eager for the trip must blend sea-currents. Now the man has subdued his woes-- there is no want of desire in him, not horses nor treasures, nor the joys of mead any of them across the earth, an earl's treasures, prince's daughter if he possesses both of you over his ancient vow. Together I should choose S and R as one, EA, W and D, declaring my oath, so that he wishes to serve this compact, this conjugal pact, while he still lives, that you two often spoke about in days gone by

Lily liked to play with her toys, but she did not like to share them. She had a big dragon that she loved very much. She made the dragon roar and fly and breathe fire. She did not let anyone else touch the dragon.

One day, her friend Ben came over to play. He saw the dragon and wanted to play with it too. He asked Lily, "Can I play with your dragon? It looks so fun!"

Lily said, "No, you can't! It is my dragon! Go away!"

Ben felt sad and angry. He said, "That is not nice! You are very bossy! You should share your toys!"

Lily said, "No, I should not! I don't want to share! Go find your own toys!"

Ben looked around and saw a book on the shelf. He took the book and opened it. He saw pictures of different animals and words under them. He said, "Look, Lily, I found a book! It has a lot of animals in it! Do you want to see?"

Lily looked at the book and saw a picture of a lion. She liked lions. She said, "Maybe I want to see. What is that animal?"

Ben said, "That is a lion. It is big and yellow and has a mane. It can roar like your dragon."

Lily said, "Really? Can I hear it roar?"

Ben said, "Sure, you can. But first, you have to let me play with your dragon. That is fair."

Lily thought for a moment. She wanted to hear the lion roar, but she did not want to give up her dragon. She said, "How about we play with both? You can play with my dragon for a little bit, and I can play with your book for a little bit. Then we can switch."

Ben said, "That sounds good to me. I think that is a good idea. I recommend we do that."

Lily said, "OK, let's do that. But be careful with my dragon. He is very special to me."

Ben said, "Don't worry, I will be careful. And you be careful with my book. It is very special to me too."

They smiled at each other and started to play. They had fun with the dragon and the book. They learned new words and made new sounds. They shared their toys and became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue bird. It loved to fly high in the sky and sing sweet songs. One day, it saw a little bird who couldn't fly. The big blue bird felt sorry for the little bird and offered to help it learn how to fly.

But the little bird was scared and didn't want to try. The big blue bird tried to encourage it, but the little bird refused. So the big blue bird flew away, feeling sad that it couldn't help the little bird.

Later that day, the big blue bird saw the little bird trying to fly on its own. But it wasn't ready yet and fell to the ground, hurting itself badly. The big blue bird realized that sometimes, even with the best intentions, we can't always help others. It flew away, feeling sad but also knowing that it had tried its best.

Once upon a time there was a pony. His name was Max. Every day, Max made his way to the meadow. On sunny days, he liked to rest and eat the sweet grass until he was full.

One day, Max saw something special near the meadow; it was a perfect tree. He trotted over to investigate. When Max got closer, he wished he hadn't. The tree had lots of prickles on it, and Max knew he'd get a sore if he touched it. He regreted coming over to the tree.

Max decided to look for something else. He trotted on and came to a pond. He looked in and saw big fish swimming about, so he hopped in for a closer look. But the pond was deeper than Max thought, and soon he was in deep water. He was scared and regreted getting in to the pond.

Max was so happy when he noticed a boat nearby. He clambered onto it and lay down, feeling relieved. Max then closed his eyes and smelled a wonderful smell. When he looked up, he saw the perfect pony! She had a red saddle and a soft, brown mane. Max was very excited. He found his perfect pony!

On another occasion, we get sent out to tackle looters raiding a bank. And one of them legs it up the road, probably armed, possibly not. Well myself and somebody else and somebody else are all of the same mind, so all three of us open fire. Three of a kind all letting fly, and I swear I see every round as it rips through his life - I see broad daylight on the other side. So we've hit this looter a dozen times and he's there on the ground, sort of inside out, pain itself, the image of agony. One of my mates goes by and tosses his guts back into his body. Then he's carted off in the back of a lorry. End of story, except not really. His blood-shadow stays on the street, and out on patrol I walk right over it week after week. Then I'm home on leave. But I blink and he bursts again through the doors of the bank. Sleep, and he's probably armed, possibly not. Dream, and he's torn apart by a dozen rounds. And the drink and the drugs won't flush him out - he's here in my head when I close my eyes, dug in behind enemy lines, not left for dead in some distant, sun-stunned, sand-smothered land or six-feet-under in desert sand, but near to the knuckle, here and now, his bloody life in my bloody hands.

Tommy was in school with his friends. He loved learning to do new things.
His teacher asked him what his favourite thing was in the classroom.
Tommy said "I like drawing on the blackboard".
The teacher smiled and said, "That's very calm of you. I'm sure everyone will miss you when you go home."
Tommy nodded and said, "Yes, I'm going to miss everyone too." 
He said goodbye to his teacher, gave his friends big hugs, and then left the class. 
It was a calm day, and everyone missed Tommy when he was gone.

Once upon a time there was a chubby bunny. He was hopping around the garden and looking for something fun to do. He soon came to a huge structure.

Bunny said, "What's this?"

"It's a playhouse," replied a friendly frog.

Bunny hopped up to the door and knocked.

An old fox opened the door and said, "What do you want?"

"I want to play," said Bunny.

"No way," said Fox. "You don't belong here. Please hurry and go away!"

Bunny was very sad. He was mad that Fox wouldn't let him in.

Bunny tried to think of a way to get inside. He decided to use his chubby body to push against the walls of the structure. With a lot of pushing and shoving, Bunny eventually managed to make a big enough hole for himself to crawl in!

Once inside, he found lots of toys to play with. Bunny smiled and said, "This is great!"

The bunny and the frog played happily inside the structure all day. And they lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk by a stream. She saw some fish swimming in the water and she wanted to catch one. 

But her mommy told her to be careful and not fall in the stream. So, Lily found a big rock and sat down. She wanted to stay safe. She saw a lock on a gate nearby and wondered what was inside. 

Suddenly, her mommy called her back. It was time to go home. Lily waved goodbye to the fish and the lock on the gate. She was happy to be safe and sound with her mommy. The end.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy some cheap toys for Tom's little sister, Ann. Tom saw a toy gun and asked his mom, "Can I have this gun, please?" His mom said yes, and they bought the toy gun.

When they got home, Tom went outside to play with his new toy gun. He pretended to shoot at the trees and the birds. "Bang! Bang!" he said, as he played. Ann watched and laughed from the porch.

Suddenly, Tom saw some smoke coming from the neighbor's yard. He ran to his mom and said, "Mom, there's smoke next door!" His mom called the firemen, and they came to put out the small fire. Tom and Ann felt happy that they helped keep everyone safe.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They saw a big bug with many legs and a hard shell. It was dull and brown, not pretty like a butterfly or a ladybug.

"Look, a bug!" Lily said. "Let's catch it and put it in a jar."

Max nodded. He ran to get a jar and a lid. Lily followed him with the bug in her hand. They put the bug in the jar and closed the lid. They felt happy and proud.

They showed the jar to their mom. She was not happy. She looked at the bug and frowned.

"Why did you catch the bug?" she asked. "Don't you know that bugs need air and space to live?"

Lily and Max felt sorry. They did not think about that. They thought the bug was just a toy.

"Can we keep it, mom?" Max asked. "We will give it some leaves and water."

Mom shook her head. "No, you can't keep it. The bug is not happy in the jar. It is scared and sad. You have to let it go. How would you feel if someone put you in a jar and covered you with a lid?"

Lily and Max imagined being in a jar. They felt scared and sad too. They did not want that.

"OK, mom. We will let it go." Lily said. "We are sorry, bug. We did not mean to hurt you."

They opened the jar and let the bug out. The bug crawled away quickly. It looked happier and freer.

Lily and Max learned a lesson. They learned that bugs are not toys. They learned to respect and care for all living things. They learned to be kind and gentle.

Gaily bedight, A gallant knight, In sunshine and in shadow, Had journeyed long, Singing a song, In search of Eldorado. But he grew old-- This knight so bold-- And o'er his heart a shadow-- Fell as he found No spot of ground That looked like Eldorado. And, as his strength Failed him at length, He met a pilgrim shadow-- 'Shadow,' said he, 'Where can it be-- This land of Eldorado?' 'Over the Mountains Of the Moon, Down the Valley of the Shadow, Ride, boldly ride,' The shade replied,-- 'If you seek for Eldorado!'

One day, a baby was playing in the park. The baby was very happy and excited. Suddenly, the baby saw a rabbit. It was a big, white rabbit. The baby was so happy! The baby wanted to race the rabbit.

The baby started running as fast as he could. The rabbit was very fast, but the baby was trying his best. He ran and ran, but the rabbit was too fast! The baby was panting, he was so tired.

But then, something special happened. The rabbit stopped running and started walking slowly. The baby saw this and smiled. He started running again and soon, he was running even faster than the rabbit!

The baby caught up to the rabbit and then he passed him! The baby was so happy! He had won the race!

The baby had learned that slow and steady can sometimes win the race!

John was a cheerful boy who loved to jog. This morning he was feeling especially energetic, so he decided to take a jog in the park. When he arrived, he noticed a mine near the lake. It was very graceful and it shone in the morning light. 

John decided to explore the mine. He jogged around it and noticed that it was getting bigger and bigger. After a few laps he realised that he could jog all around the mine, and he had so much fun running in a big circle.

Soon he heard a voice behind him. John looked back to see a graceful swan joining his jog. He was so happy to have a friend with him. The swan and John jogged around the mine together, and they made lots of laps.

John was so pleased with his jog. He waved goodbye to the swan before returning home. He had a big smile on his face, feeling very graceful and happy.

name_of_work: The Guy in the Glass by Peter Dale Wimbrow Sr.
content: When you get what you want in your struggle for self And the world makes you king for a day Just go to the mirror and look at yourself And see what that man has to say. For it isn't your father, or mother, or wife Whose judgment upon you must pass The fellow whose verdict counts most in your life Is the one staring back from the glass. He's the fellow to please - never mind all the rest For he's with you, clear to the end And you've passed your most difficult, dangerous test If the man in the glass is your friend. You may fool the whole world down the pathway of years And get pats on the back as you pass But your final reward will be heartache and tears If you've cheated the man in the glass.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to watch films with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy and his family went to see a film at the movie theater. The film was about a big, fearful monster who lived in a castle. 

Timmy loved the movie, but he was scared of the monster. His mommy and daddy told him that the monster was just acting, and that it wasn't real. Timmy felt better knowing that the monster wasn't real, and he enjoyed the rest of the film. 

After the film was over, Timmy and his family went home. Timmy couldn't stop talking about the film and how the monster was just acting. He wanted to watch more films with his family, and he wasn't afraid of any monsters anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved going to the beach. One day, Sarah's mommy and daddy took her to the beach and said "Welcome!"

When Sarah arrived at the beach, she saw the big, blue sea. She ran straight into the water but when she stepped back onto the sand, Sarah noticed her leg was wet. She touched it and it was cold. Just then, she heard a noise - it was a seal pup! It splashed around in the water and Sarah said "Welcome!" 

The seal pup started to swim closer to Sarah. Sarah was so excited! She wiggled her toes in the sand and the seal pup swam away. Sarah laughed and said goodbye!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends and explore the world around her. One day, Lily and her friends were walking in the park when they saw a big, fair wheel. Lily pointed at it and said, "Wow, that looks like so much fun!"

Later that day, Lily's mom called her inside and said, "Lily, it's time to wash your hands for dinner." Lily groaned, but knew she had to do it. As she washed her hands, she remembered the fair wheel and how much she wanted to ride it. She asked her mom, "Can we go to the fair tomorrow, please?" Her mom smiled and said, "Maybe we can, but we'll have to wait and see."

The next day, Lily and her family went to the fair. As they walked around, Lily saw the fair wheel again and ran towards it. She got in line and waited patiently. When it was her turn, she climbed into the seat and held on tight as the wheel started to spin. As she went higher and higher, she remembered how she had to wash her hands before dinner and how it was worth it to have fun at the fair.

Lilly and Anna were walking through the forest. The sun was shining and the trees were tall. They were both excited, with smiles on their faces. 

Suddenly they saw a mighty shelter. It looked like a big and strong house, built out of many pieces of wood. 

Lilly said, "This shelter looks so cool. We should go explore it!" Anna agreed and they both ran closer. 

When they approached the shelter, they saw that it was very old.  They could also see that some of the boards were broken and parts of it were missing. 

Lilly said, "Let's fix it! We can put new boards in and tie the shelter back together!" Anna thought this was a great idea and they worked together to value the shelter. 

When they were done, they both stood back and admired their work. The shelter now looked as mighty as ever, and they knew it was safe and secure. 

Lilly and Anna smiled at each other proudly, happy that they had given the shelter such a valuable upgrade.
