name_of_work: Nothing to fear but fear itself
content: First Inaugural Address, March 4, 1932 This great Nation will endure as it has endured, will revive and will prosper. So, first of all, let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself--nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance... In such a spirit on my part and on yours we face our common difficulties. They concern, thank God, only material things... More important, a host of unemployed citizens face the grim problem of existence, and an equally great number toil with little return. Only a foolish optimist can deny the dark realities of the moment. Yet our distress comes from no failure of substance... Plenty is at our doorstep, but a generous use of it languishes in the very sight of the supply. Primarily this is because the rulers of the exchange of mankind's goods have failed, through their own stubbornness and their own incompetence... This nation asks for action, and action now. Our greatest primary task is to put people to work... It can be accomplished in part by direct recruiting by the Government itself, treating the task as we would treat the emergency of a war, but at the same time, through this employment, accomplishing greatly needed projects to stimulate and reorganize the use of our natural resources... ...These measures, or such other measures as the Congress may build out of its experience and wisdom, I shall seek, within my constitutional authority, to bring to speedy adoption. But in the event that the Congress shall fail to take one of these two courses, and in the event that the national emergency is still critical... I shall ask the Congress for the one remaining instrument to meet the crisis--broad Executive power to wage a war against the emergency, as great as the power that would be given to me if we were in fact invaded by a foreign foe...

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was looking after her dad's tools which were kept in the shed. One day she noticed a tall ladder in the corner. She wanted to see if she could manage it.

So, she walked over and grasped the ladder. She was a little anxious as it was so tall and she was only 3 years old after all. But with a lot of effort she managed to carry it outside.

By the time she had got to the garden she was quite tired. She placed the ladder against the tree and began to climb. Suddenly, Lucy stopped and thought. She had managed to do something she never thought she could. She looked up with a proud smile and thought to herself â€˜I did it!â€™.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Peter and Jane, who loved to play together everyday. 

One afternoon, they were at the park when they noticed a magnet on the ground. 
"Let's keep it!" said Jane excitedly. 
Peter thought it was a great idea and quickly picked it up. 

They decided to put their creative minds together to come up with different ways to use the magnet. 

"Letâ€™s try to pick up paperclips!" said Jane. 
"I know! We can try picking up leaves!" Peter added. 

They had a lot of fun, until one of them suddenly lost the magnet. 
"Oh no! Where did it go?" cried out Jane. 
"Donâ€™t worry, letâ€™s look for it together!" replied Peter. 

They searched the whole park, but they couldn't find the magnet anywhere. They were sad, but they still smiled at each other. 

"That was a lot of fun," said Jane. 
Peter nodded smiling and said, "Let's come back tomorrow and come up with more ideas."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and run in the park. One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog looks happy and friendly.

"Hello, dog!" Lily says. "Do you want to play with us?"

The dog barks and wags its tail. It runs to Lily and Ben and licks their faces. They giggle and pet the dog.

"Can we keep him, please?" Ben asks. "He is so cute and fun!"

Lily nods. "Yes, please! He can stay with us and be our pet!"

They look for a collar or a tag on the dog, but they do not find any. They think the dog has no home or owner.

"Let's take him to our house!" Lily says. "We can give him a name and a treat and a bed!"

They hold the dog's leash and walk to their house. They are very happy and excited. They hope their parents will let them keep the dog.

When they get to their house, they see their mom and dad waiting for them. They smile and wave.

"Hi, kids!" their mom says. "Who is this?"

"This is our new friend!" Lily says. "He is a dog and he is very nice and sweet!"

"We found him in the park!" Ben says. "He has no home or owner. Can he stay with us, please?"

Their mom and dad look at the dog. They see that he is big and furry and friendly. They also see that he has a tag on his ear. The tag has a name and a phone number.

"Kids, this dog is not a stray," their dad says. "He has a name and a phone number. He belongs to someone else. His name is Max."

Lily and Ben are sad and surprised. They did not see the tag on his ear. They like Max and want him to stay with them.

"But we love him!" Lily says. "He loves us too! He played with us and licked us and wagged his tail!"

"We know, honey," their mom says. "But he has a family that loves him too. They must be looking for him and missing him. We have to call them and tell them we have their dog."

Lily and Ben understand. They know it is the right thing to do. They hug Max and say goodbye. They hope he will be happy and safe with his family.

Their mom calls the phone number on the tag. She talks to a lady who is very happy and grateful. She says she is Max's owner and she lost him in the park. She says she will come and get him right away.

Lily and Ben wait for the lady to come. They are sad but brave. They give Max one last treat and one last kiss. They tell him they are glad they met him and they hope to see him again.

The lady arrives and thanks them for finding and taking care of Max. She says he is a good dog and a good friend. She says they can visit him anytime they want. She invites them to come to her house and play with Max and his toys.

Lily and Ben smile and nod. They are happy that Max has a home and a family. They are happy that they can still be his friends. They say yes to the lady's invitation. They think maybe they can find another dog that needs a home and a family. They think maybe they can find a dog that is fit for them.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy. The puppy was brown, like his nose and his eyes. He loved adventure.

One day, the puppy spotted something that looked fun up ahead. It was a deep brown hole! The little pup was excited. He knew he had to explore it. He went to the edge of the hole and took a deep breath. Then, he dived in! 

At first he was scared, but he soon began to have fun. He paddled around looking for something special. Suddenly, he found something sparkly in the water. He felt around with his paws and realized it was pepper! He picked it up, and quickly swam back to the surface.

When he reached the edge of the hole, he took a big, deep breath. Then, he jumped out with his prize in his mouth. He was so proud of himself for finding the pepper and for taking a big dive. He wagged his tail and ran off to show his family his new discovery.

name_of_work: A Late Walk by Robert Frost
content: When I go up through the mowing field, The headless aftermath, Smooth-laid like thatch with the heavy dew, Half closes the garden path. And when I come to the garden ground, The whir of sober birds Up from the tangle of withered weeds Is sadder than any words. A tree beside the wall stands bare, But a leaf that lingered brown, Disturbed, I doubt not, by my thought, Comes softly rattling down. I end not far from my going forth By picking the faded blue Of the last remaining aster flower To carry again to you.

Once upon a time, there was a fat quick fox. He was always so fast, zig zagging all over the place! One day he heard something behind him and he stopped dead in his tracks. He slowly turned around and saw a rabbit who said hello. The fox replied, "Hi there!" with a smile on his face. 

The rabbit asked the fox, "Do you want to play a game?" The fox jumped with excitement and replied, "Yes, let's play!" The rabbit suggested they should play tag and the fox clapped his paws in agreement. The two of them took off running in all kinds of directions! 

The fox was so fast that no matter how hard the rabbit tried it couldn't catch him. The rabbit kept shouting "C'mon fox, you can do it!" but the fox was too quick. Finally, the fox won the game! The rabbit laughed and said, "That was great! Let's play again." The fox replied, "I'd love to, but I'm too tired from running. Let's play again soon." They said goodbye and the fox headed off into the night.

One day, a little boy named Tim went with his mom and dad to a restaurant. The restaurant was big and empty. They sat at a table near the big window.

Tim saw a cat outside the window. The cat looked sad and hungry. Tim wanted to help the cat, so he called to the cat. But the cat did not come in.

Tim's mom saw that he was sad. She told him they could call someone to help the cat. Tim felt happy again. They called a kind man who takes care of animals. The man came and took the cat to a safe and warm home.

In the end, Tim, his mom, and dad enjoyed their meal at the restaurant. They were glad they could help the cat. The restaurant was not empty anymore, and everyone was happy.

When I am an old woman I shall wear purple With a red hat which doesn't go, and doesn't suit me. And I shall spend my pension on brandy and summer gloves And satin sandals, and say we've no money for butter. I shall sit down on the pavement when I'm tired And gobble up samples in shops and press alarm bells And run my stick along the public railings And make up for the sobriety of my youth. I shall go out in my slippers in the rain And pick flowers in other people's gardens And learn to spit. You can wear terrible shirts and grow more fat And eat three pounds of sausages at a go Or only bread and pickle for a week And hoard pens and pencils and beermats and things in boxes. But now we must have clothes that keep us dry And pay our rent and not swear in the street And set a good example for the children. We must have friends to dinner and read the papers. But maybe I ought to practise a little now? So people who know me are not too shocked and surprised When suddenly I am old, and start to wear purple.

Lily and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They are very happy.

"Look, our snowman is so high!" Lily says. "He can see the whole park!"

"Yes, he is very high," Ben says. "But he is also very cold. He needs some powder to keep him warm."

"What is powder?" Lily asks.

"Powder is something you put on your face when you are sick," Ben says. "It makes you feel better. I have some in my pocket. I will show you."

Ben takes out a small bottle of powder from his pocket. He opens it and sprinkles some on the snowman's face.

"See, now he has powder on his face," Ben says. "He will feel better."

But the powder is not good for the snowman. It makes him sneeze. He sneezes so hard that his hat and scarf fly off. His carrot nose and rocks fall off too. He looks very sad.

"Oh no, what did you do?" Lily says. "You made our snowman sick!"

"I'm sorry, I didn't know," Ben says. "I thought it was good powder. Maybe we can fix him."

They try to put the hat and scarf back on the snowman. They try to find the carrot and the rocks. But the snow is too soft and the wind is too strong. The snowman falls apart.

They are very sad. They hug each other and cry.

"Maybe we can make another snowman tomorrow," Lily says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But we will not give him any powder. Powder is bad for snowmen."

Once upon a time, there was a turtle named Timmy. Timmy was very slow and liked to take his time when he walked. One day, Timmy met a frog named Freddy. Freddy wanted to play with Timmy, but Timmy was too slow. Freddy said, "Timmy, can you please walk faster?" Timmy replied, "I can't, I am a slow turtle."

Then, Freddy had an idea. He said, "Timmy, let's play a game. I will tap your shell and you tell me which way to go." Timmy thought that was a great idea, so they started playing. Freddy tapped Timmy's shell and Timmy told him which way to go. They played until the sun went down and had so much fun together. From that day on, Timmy and Freddy were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a driver. He had a car, but it was broken. He wanted to go to the store to buy some food, but he couldn't because his car was broken. 

One day, it started to rain. The driver was sad because he couldn't go to the store. He watched the rain fall from his window. 

The rain got harder and harder. Suddenly, the driver heard a loud noise outside. He looked out the window and saw that a big tree had fallen on his car! 

The driver was very sad because now he couldn't go to the store and his car was even more broken. The end.

My sister rubs the doll's face in mud, then climbs through the truck window. She ignores me as I walk around it, hitting the flat tires with an iron rod. The old man yells for me to help hitch the team, but I keep walking around the truck, hitting harder, until my mother calls. I pick up a rock and throw it at the kitchen window, but it falls short. The old man's voice bounces off the air like a ball I can't lift my leg over. I stand beside him, waiting, but he doesn't look up and I squeeze the rod, raise it, his skull splits open. Mother runs toward us. I stand still, get her across the spine as she bends over him. I drop the rod and take the rifle from the house. Roses are red, violets are blue, one bullet for the black horse, two for the brown. They're down quick. I spit, my tongue's bloody; I've bitten it. I laugh, remember the one out back. I catch her climbing from the truck, shoot. The doll lands on the ground with her. I pick it up, rock it in my arms. Yeah. I'm Jack, Hogarth's son. I'm nimble, I'm quick. In the house, I put on the old man's best suit and his patent leather shoes. I pack my mother's satin nightgown and my sister's doll in the suitcase. Then I go outside and cross the fields to the highway. I'm fourteen. I'm a wind from nowhere. I can break your heart.

Lily and Tom were playing in the backyard. They found a big box and some nails. They wanted to make a house for their toys.

"Can I use the hammer?" Lily asked Tom.

"OK, but be careful. It is heavy and hard," Tom said. He gave Lily the hammer and a nail.

Lily tried to hit the nail with the hammer, but she missed. The hammer hit the box and made a loud noise. Lily felt sad and scared.

"Ouch! That hurt!" she said. She dropped the hammer and started to cry.

Tom saw Lily crying and ran to her. He hugged her and said, "Don't cry, Lily. You can do it. I will help you. You are brave and strong."

Tom encouraged Lily to try again. He held the nail for her and showed her how to hit it with the hammer. Lily hit the nail with the hammer and it went into the box. She felt happy and proud.

"Yay! I did it!" she said. She smiled and hugged Tom.

They worked together and made a house for their toys. They put a blanket on top and some pillows inside. They invited their toys to come in and have a tea party. They shared some cookies and juice. They were delicious.

Lily and Tom had fun playing in their house. They thanked each other for helping and sharing. They were good friends.

name_of_work: This Land Is Your Land by Woody Guthrie
content: This land is your land, this land is my land From California to the New York island, From the redwood forest to the Gulf Stream waters; This land was made for you and me. As I was walking that ribbon of highway I saw above me that endless skyway; I saw below me that golden valley; This land was made for you and me. I've roamed and rambled and I followed my footsteps To the sparkling sands of her diamond deserts; And all around me a voice was sounding; This land was made for you and me. When the sun came shining, and I was strolling, And the wheat fields waving and the dust clouds rolling, As the fog was lifting a voice was chanting: This land was made for you and me. As I went walking I saw a sign there, And on the sign it said "No Trespassing." But on the other side it didn't say nothing. That side was made for you and me. In the shadow of the steeple I saw my people, By the relief office I seen my people; As they stood there hungry, I stood there asking Is this land made for you and me? Nobody living can ever stop me, As I go walking that freedom highway; Nobody living can ever make me turn back This land was made for you and me.

name_of_work: The Laughing Heart by Charles Bukowski
content: Your life is your life Don't let it be clubbed into dank submission. Be on the watch. There are ways out. There is a light somewhere. It may not be much light but It beats the darkness. Be on the watch. The gods will offer you chances. Know them. Take them. You can't beat death but You can beat death in life, sometimes. And the more often you learn to do it, The more light there will be. Your life is your life. Know it while you have it. You are marvelous The gods wait to delight In you.

Once upon a time there was a great bear. He loved to explore the world and guess what he might find. One day he was exploring and he stumbled upon a beautiful velvet box. He was so excited to see what was inside. He couldn't guess what it was, so he decided to open it. When he opened the box, he saw a great big cake! He was so excited that he decided to eat it right away. He enjoyed the delicious cake so much that he guessed he would come back for more soon. The end.

name_of_work: A Silly Poem by Spike Milligan
content: Said Hamlet to Ophelia, I'll draw a sketch of thee, What kind of pencil shall I use? 2B or not 2B?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. Lily loved to play outside and explore the world around her.

One day, Lily was playing in the park when she met a boy named Timmy. They became friends and played together all day long. Timmy told Lily about his hope to travel the world one day and see all the different places.

Lily thought that was a wonderful idea and she too hoped to see the world one day. She told Timmy about her modest dream of becoming a teacher and helping kids learn new things.

As the sun began to set, Lily said goodbye to her new friend and headed home. But on her way, she saw something terrible. There was a big fire in her house and her mommy and daddy were trapped inside.

Lily was so scared and didn't know what to do. She hoped that someone would come and help them, but no one did. The world seemed like a scary and dangerous place to her now. Sadly, Lily lost her mommy and daddy that day and her world would never be the same again.

name_of_work: Grown-up by Edna St. Vicent Millay
content: Was it for this I uttered prayers, And sobbed and cursed and kicked the stairs, That now, domestic as a plate, I should retire at half-past eight?

Once upon a time there was a very thin voice. It was so thin it was almost whispering.
Every day the voice sounded all over the town.
One day everyone started to act a little different. They smiled more, and started to do nice things for each other.

The townspeople soon discovered where the thin voice was coming from. It was coming from a little bird.
The bird would tweet beautiful songs every day and whenever it sang, the townspeople would act nice.

The townspeople were so happy they gave the bird a special nest in the biggest tree of the town. In return, the bird sang extra loud.

From that day on life in the town was always happy and peaceful, all thanks to the little bird's thin voice.

Once upon a time there was a zebra. He was scared and ran away from something he didn't understand. He was running so fast that he didn't see the big hole in the ground. He fell in! He tried to pull himself out, but he was too scared and he was stuck. 

Luckily, a kind elephant saw the poor zebra in the hole. He tried to help him and asked the zebra to grab onto his trunk. He pulled and pulled, but the zebra was too scared and kept slipping. 

Still, the kind elephant didn't give up. He pulled and pulled until finally the zebra was out of the hole. 

But when the zebra jumped out of the hole he landed on a bee hive. The bees were angry and swarmed the zebra. The zebra was so scared that he ran away and never came back. 

The end.

Lyric night of the lingering Indian Summer, Shadowy fields that are scentless but full of singing, Never a bird, but the passionless chant of insects, Ceaseless, insistent. The grasshopper's horn, and far-off, high in the maples, The wheel of a locust leisurely grinding the silence Under a moon waning and worn, broken, Tired with summer. Let me remember you, voices of little insects, Weeds in the moonlight, fields that are tangled with asters, Let me remember, soon will the winter be on us, Snow-hushed and heavy. Over my soul murmur your mute benediction, While I gaze, O fields that rest after harvest, As those who part look long in the eyes they lean to, Lest they forget them.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play outside in the sun. They have a big ball and a kite. They share the ball and the kite. They take turns to kick the ball and fly the kite.

One day, they see a big cloud in the sky. The cloud is white and fluffy. It looks like a bunny. Lily and Ben laugh. They point at the cloud and say, "Look, a bunny!"

They run after the cloud. They want to catch the bunny. They are playful and happy. They forget about the ball and the kite. They leave them on the grass.

A dog sees the ball and the kite. The dog is curious and hungry. He runs to the ball and the kite. He bites the ball and the kite. He makes them pop and tear. He makes a mess.

Lily and Ben hear the noise. They turn around and see the dog. They see the ball and the kite. They are broken and ruined. They are sad and angry. They shout at the dog and say, "Bad dog! Go away!"

The dog runs away. He is scared and sorry. He did not mean to hurt the ball and the kite. He just wanted to play.

Lily and Ben hug each other. They are still friends. They say, "It's OK. We can get a new ball and a kite. We still have each other. We can still play and share."

They look at the sky. They see another cloud. The cloud is pink and sparkly. It looks like a star. Lily and Ben smile. They point at the cloud and say, "Look, a star!"

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and sing songs. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a boy with a shiny medal around his neck. 

Lily asked, "What's that shiny thing on your neck?" 

"It's a medal," the boy replied. "I won it for running fast." 

Lily thought that was really cool. She smiled and said, "I like your medal." 

The boy smiled back and said, "Thanks! Do you want to kiss it for good luck?" 

Lily giggled and kissed the medal. She felt happy and lucky too. From that day on, Lily and the boy became good friends and played together often in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a duck named Ducky. Ducky liked to swim in the pond with his friends. One day, Ducky saw a big fish in the pond. Ducky wanted to see the fish up close, so he decided to dive into the water. 

As Ducky was swimming towards the fish, he saw a frog on the land. The frog looked upset. Ducky asked the frog, "Why are you upset?" The frog replied, "I lost my favorite toy in the pond and I can't find it." Ducky felt sad for the frog and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find it!"

Ducky dove into the water again and searched for the frog's toy. After a few minutes, Ducky found the toy and brought it to the frog. The frog was so happy and thanked Ducky. From that day on, Ducky and the frog became best friends and had many more adventures together in the pond.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was spoiled and always wanted things her way. One day Lucy wanted to go out and play, but her mum said she needed to tidy her room first. Lucy was very unhappy about this and started to cry.

After a while, Lucy went up to her bedroom and tidied. When she was finished, she opened the door and started to go out. Suddenly there was a loud bang. Someone was knocking on the door!

Lucy's mum answered the door and a delivery man was standing there. He handed her a package and said, "This is for Lucy". She opened the package, but was very surprised by what she found. Inside was a pile of rubbish! Lucy had received a pile of rubbish!

Lucy was really angry and started to cry. She ran upstairs to her bedroom and slammed the door shut. That was the end of Lucy's day, and her mum was very angry with her for being so spoiled.
Every child has a madman on their street: The only trouble about our madman is that he's our father.

When the Present has latched its postern behind my tremulous stay, And the May month flaps its glad green leaves like wings, Delicate-filmed as new-spun silk, will the neighbours say, "He was a man who used to notice such things"? If it be in the dusk when, like an eyelid's soundless blink, The dewfall-hawk comes crossing the shades to alight Upon the wind-warped upland thorn, a gazer may think, "To him this must have been a familiar sight." If I pass during some nocturnal blackness, mothy and warm, When the hedgehog travels furtively over the lawn, One may say, "He strove that such innocent creatures should come to no harm, But he could do little for them; and now he is gone." If, when hearing that I have been stilled at last, they stand at the door, Watching the full-starred heavens that winter sees, Will this thought rise on those who will meet my face no more, "He was one who had an eye for such mysteries"? And will any say when my bell of quittance is heard in the gloom, And a crossing breeze cuts a pause in its outrollings, Till they rise again, as they were a new bell's boom, "He hears it not now, but used to notice such things?"

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. Sometimes they see a big bird with red and blue feathers. The bird can talk. It says hello and bye-bye. The bird is rare. Not many people have seen it.

One day, Anna and Ben go to the park. They look for the bird. They do not see it. They are sad. They sit on a bench and wait.

"Where is the bird?" Anna asks.

"I do not know," Ben says. "Maybe it is busy. Maybe it is sleeping. Maybe it is gone."

They wait some more. They are bored. They want to play.

"Let's go to the swings," Anna says.

"OK," Ben says.

They get up and walk to the swings. They do not see the bird.

But the bird sees them. It is hiding in a tree. It is shy. It does not like many people. It only likes Anna and Ben. It waits for the right time. It wants to say hello.

When Anna and Ben are on the swings, the bird flies out of the tree. It lands on the bench. It says hello.

Anna and Ben hear the bird. They are surprised. They are happy. They run to the bench. They say hello back.

The bird smiles. It seems glad. It talks to Anna and Ben. It tells them stories. It makes them laugh. It is their friend.

They have a good time. They forget about the swings. They only want to be with the bird. The bird is rare. But it is not lonely. It has Anna and Ben.

Once upon a time, there was a pink sunflower. The sunflower lived in a big garden with many other flowers. Every day, the sunflower would look up at the sky and smile at the sun.

One day, something new happened. A little girl came to the garden. She saw the pink sunflower and said, "Wow! You are so pretty!" The sunflower felt very happy. The little girl would visit the sunflower every day and they became good friends.

The little girl and the pink sunflower played in the garden all summer long. They laughed and had fun together. When the wind blew, the sunflower would dance for the little girl. They were the best of friends and had the best time together.

Once there was a little boy named Luke. He was only 3 years old. One day, Luke was walking in the park when he saw a dog. He thought it was a friendly dog until it started to growl. Its lip was thick and it made Luke scared.

Then, suddenly, the dog began to bark loudly. Luke started to back away from the dog but it kept barking. Mentioning the word 'go', he ran away as fast as he could.

But sadly, the dog chased after him. The thick lip of the dog made a lot of noise as it followed him. Luke ran and ran but the dog got closer and closer until it caught him. The dog bit him, and it hurt Luke a lot. He started to cry.

The bad ending to this story is that Luke got hurt. He had to go to the hospital and needed bandages on his arm. From then on, Luke was scared of dogs and never wanted to go near one again.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit named Fred. Fred liked to explore the neighbourhood. One day, Fred found a big sign. He was so excited and wanted to learn what it said. He went closer to take a look, but he was so confused. He could not understand the words. Suddenly Fred heard a voice coming from behind. It was a friendly dog who asked Fred what he was looking at.

Fred replied, "I don't know what this sign says!"

The kind dog stared at the sign and smiled. "It says someone is giving away free treats. Would you like to go and get one?"

Fred hopped with excitement. The dog guided him to a nearby house, and the two of them knocked on the door. An old lady opened the door, and she was very surprised to see a rabbit and a dog.

The lady said, "Welcome! I'm so glad you two stopped by. Please, come in and receive your treat!"

Fred couldn't believe his luck. He received a delicious candy, and a tasty apple. He thanked the kind lady, thanked the dog, and hopped away feeling happy.

Tommy liked to hop. He hopped in the morning, he hopped at noon, he hopped in the evening. He hopped with his friends, he hopped with his toys, he hopped with his dog. He hopped everywhere he could.

One day, he found a hat. It was a big hat, with a red feather. It was not an ordinary hat. It was a magic hat. Tommy put it on his head and hopped. He felt something strange. He looked around and saw that he was not in his yard anymore. He was in a forest, with tall trees and colorful birds.

"Wow!" he said. "This hat can take me to different places. I wonder where else I can go."

He hopped again and again, and each time he saw a new place. He saw a farm, with cows and pigs and chickens. He saw a beach, with sand and waves and shells. He saw a city, with cars and buses and buildings. He saw a lot of things he had never seen before.

He was having fun, but he also missed his home. He wanted to see his mom and dad and his dog. He wanted to play with his friends and his toys. He wanted to eat his favorite food and sleep in his own bed. He decided to hop one last time and go back to his yard.

He hopped and hopped, but nothing happened. He was still in the city, with the noise and the crowd. He tried to hop again, but the hat fell off his head. A man picked it up and ran away.

"Hey!" Tommy shouted. "That's my hat! Give it back!"

But the man did not hear him. He was gone. Tommy was sad and scared. He did not know how to get home without his hat. He did not know anyone in the city. He did not know what to do.

He sat on the sidewalk and cried. He wished he had never found the hat. He wished he had never hopped away from his home. He wished he had been happy with his ordinary life.

name_of_work: There Will Come Soft Rains by Sara Teasdale
content: There will come soft rains and the smell of the ground, And swallows circling with their shimmering sound; And frogs in the pools singing at night, And wild plum trees in tremulous white, Robins will wear their feathery fire Whistling their whims on a low fence-wire; And not one will know of the war, not one Will care at last when it is done. Not one would mind, neither bird nor tree If mankind perished utterly; And Spring herself, when she woke at dawn, Would scarcely know that we were gone.

Now we ought to praise the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, The might of the Creator and his conception, The work of the glorious Father, as he of each of the wonders, Eternal Lord, established the beginning. He first created for the sons of men Heaven as a roof, holy Creator; Then the middle-earth, the Guardian of mankind, The eternal Lord, afterwards made The earth for men, the Lord almighty.

Figure it out for yourself, my lad, You've all that the greatest of men have had, Two arms, two hands, two legs, two eyes, And a brain to use if you would be wise. With this equipment they all began, So start for the top and say "I can." Look them over, the wise and great, They take their food from a common plate And similar knives and forks they use, With similar laces they tie their shoes, The world considers them brave and smart. But you've all they had when they made their start. You can triumph and come to skill, You can be great if only you will, You're well equipped for what fight you choose, You have legs and arms and a brain to use, And the man who has risen, great deeds to do Began his life with no more than you. You are the handicap you must face, You are the one who must choose your place, You must say where you want to go. How much you will study the truth to know, God has equipped you for life, But He Lets you decide what you want to be. Courage must come from the soul within, The man must furnish the will to win, So figure it out for yourself, my lad, You were born with all that the great have had, With your equipment they all began. Get hold of yourself, and say: "I can."

An ant on the tablecloth Ran into a dormant moth Of many times his size. He showed not the least surprise. His business wasn't with such. He gave it scarcely a touch, And was off on his duty run. Yet if he encountered one Of the hive's enquiry squad Whose work is to find out God And the nature of time and space, He would put him onto the case. Ants are a curious race; One crossing with hurried tread The body of one of their dead Isn't given a moment's arrest- Seems not even impressed. But he no doubt reports to any With whom he crosses antennae, And they no doubt report To the higher-up at court. Then word goes forth in Formic: "Death's come to Jerry McCormic, Our selfless forager Jerry. Will the special Janizary Whose office it is to bury The dead of the commissary Go bring him home to his people. Lay him in state on a sepal. Wrap him for shroud in a petal. Embalm him with ichor of nettle. This is the word of your Queen." And presently on the scene Appears a solemn mortician; And taking formal position, With feelers calmly atwiddle, Seizes the dead by the middle, And heaving him high in air, Carries him out of there. No one stands round to stare. It is nobody else's affair It couldn't be called ungentle But how thoroughly departmental

name_of_work: Advice to a Girl by Thomas Campion
content: Never love unlesse you can Beare with all the faults of man: Men sometimes will jealous bee Though but little cause they see, And hang the head, as discontent, And speake what straight they will repent. Men that but one Saint adore Make a shew of love to more: Beauty must be scorn'd in none, Though but truely serv'd in one: For what is courtship, but disguise? True hearts may have dissembling eyes. Men, when their affaires require, Must a while themselves retire: Sometimes hunt, and sometimes hawke, And not ever sit and talke. If these, and such like, you can beare, Then like, and love, and never feare.

Once upon a time there was a bunny. His name was Harry and he liked to hop around looking for wool. He hopped from one field to the next without a care in the world.

One day, he hopped into a meadow that was filled with thick, soft wool. He couldn't believe his luck! He hopped around happily and started to pick the wool up with his furry hands.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. He looked around and saw a sheep, standing alert in the corner. "Your wool is mine now, Harry!" the sheep said.

Harry gasped, then cleared his throat to speak. "Please forgive me," he said. "I didn't mean to take your wool."

The sheep looked at Harry and softened his gaze. "I forgive you, my little friend," the sheep said. "But be careful when entering someone else's meadow."

Harry thanked the sheep, then hopped away joyfully, feeling happy and grateful for the sheep's kind forgiveness.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play in the mud. One day, he went to the river to play and saw a big, green crocodile. Timmy was scared and ran away. 

But the crocodile called out, "Don't be afraid, little boy. I won't hurt you. I just want to be your friend." 

Timmy stopped and looked back at the crocodile. He saw that the crocodile's teeth were big and sharp, but his eyes were kind. 

Timmy said, "Okay, we can be friends. But you're so messy. Let me make you clean." 

Timmy went back to his house and got some soap and a brush. He came back to the river and scrubbed the crocodile until he was shiny and clean. From that day on, Timmy and the crocodile played together every day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a cool cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with a rod all day. One day, Tom found a big, shiny rod in the park. He was very happy.

As Tom was playing with the rod, a small dog named Max came by. Max saw the rod and wanted to play with it too. But Tom did not want to share the rod with Max. Max was sad and left.

Tom's mom saw what happened and told Tom that it is good to share with friends. Tom thought about it and decided to find Max. When he found Max, he gave him the rod to play with. Max was very happy and they played together all day.

The moral of the story is that sharing with others can make everyone happy.

Once there was a large bear. He liked to touch things. One day he came across a massage. It felt nice, so he touched it all over. He liked how it felt, so he asked the massage for more. The massage was happy to give him more touches. Every day, the bear would touch the massage. He liked it so much he kept touching it for a long time. The massage was happy to let the bear touch it every day. They were the best of friends!

Once upon a time there was a little ant named Bizzy. Bizzy was a very helpful ant who always went out of her way to help other ants. One day, Bizzy heard some news that spread quickly through the ant hill. All of the ants were extremely excited because the news was that a big picnic was taking place in the forest! 

Bizzy immediately ran to the forest, but when she arrived the picnic was already over. She was so sad and helpless. She felt like she had wasted her time running to the picnic. 

Just then, Bizzy heard a voice. It was an old wise ant. The wise ant told Bizzy, "Sometimes the news spreads faster than what we can do. Even though it is tempting, try not to be too hasty to believe in something". Bizzy was very grateful to the wise ant's words and went home with a lesson. 

The moral of the story is: never spread news until you are sure it is true.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big sack. The sack is modern. It has wheels and a handle. They can put toys inside and pull the sack around.

One day, Ben and Jen decide to play a game. They take turns hiding in the sack and pulling each other. Ben goes first. He climbs into the sack and zips it up. Jen grabs the handle and pulls the sack out of the room. She goes to the kitchen, where Mom is making lunch.

"Look, Mom, I have a sack!" Jen says.

"What's in the sack, Jen?" Mom asks.

"It's a surprise!" Jen says.

Mom smiles and says, "Okay, but be careful with the sack. Don't bump into anything."

Jen nods and pulls the sack to the living room. She sees Dad reading a book on the couch.

"Hi, Dad, I have a sack!" Jen says.

"What's in the sack, Jen?" Dad asks.

"It's a surprise!" Jen says.

Dad chuckles and says, "Okay, but be gentle with the sack. Don't shake it too much."

Jen nods and pulls the sack to the hall. She hears Ben giggling inside the sack. She thinks it's funny. She wants to make him laugh more. She pulls the sack faster and faster. She spins the sack around and around. She jumps with the sack up and down.

"Stop, Jen, stop!" Ben cries. "I feel sick!"

Jen stops and opens the sack. Ben comes out. He is pale and dizzy. He holds his tummy and groans.

"Sorry, Ben, I didn't mean to make you sick," Jen says.

"It's okay, Jen, I forgive you," Ben says.

They hug and say, "I love you, twin."

They go back to their room and play with their toys. They decide to use the sack for something else. They fill it with pillows and blankets and make a cozy nest. They snuggle in the sack and take a nap. They dream of happy things.

We know what is now on History's scales, What is, in the world, going now. The hour of courage shew our clock's hands. Our courage will not bend its brow. name_of_work: Meditation at Lagunitas by Robert Hass
content: All the new thinking is about loss. In this it resembles all the old thinking. The idea, for example, that each particular erases the luminous clarity of a general idea. That the clown- faced woodpecker probing the dead sculpted trunk of that black birch is, by his presence, some tragic falling off from a first world of undivided light. Or the other notion that, because there is in this world no one thing to which the bramble of blackberry corresponds, a word is elegy to what it signifies. We talked about it late last night and in the voice of my friend, there was a thin wire of grief, a tone almost querulous. After a while I understood that, talking this way, everything dissolves: justice, pine, hair, woman, you and I. There was a woman I made love to and I remembered how, holding her small shoulders in my hands sometimes, I felt a violent wonder at her presence like a thirst for salt, for my childhood river with its island willows, silly music from the pleasure boat, muddy places where we caught the little orange-silver fish called pumpkinseed. It hardly had to do with her. Longing, we say, because desire is full of endless distances. I must have been the same to her. But I remember so much, the way her hands dismantled bread, the thing her father said that hurt her, what she dreamed. There are moments when the body is as numinous as words, days that are the good flesh continuing. Such tenderness, those afternoons and evenings, saying blackberry, blackberry, blackberry.

Once there was a painter who loved to paint pictures. Each day she carefully thought of the colors to use and worked hard to make her pictures come alive. One day, as she was painting, she suddenly stopped. She heard a noise coming from outside and she saw something very special. It was a tiny bird that had landed at her window. The painter thought it was so thoughtful of him to come and visit her.

She watched it for a few moments until it flew away. It made her so happy! After that, she went back to painting and enjoyed it very much. She used bright colors for the sky and put a lot of detail into each picture.

The painter kept painting until she suddenly stopped again. This time, something different happened. She felt pain in her arm from using the brush for too long. She decided to take a break and give her arm some rest.

After a few minutes of rest, she felt much better and went back to painting. She was extra careful and thoughtful not to paint too long at one time. The painter was very happy with the pictures she had made and she was very proud of herself.

name_of_work: A Certain Lady by Dorothy Parker
content: Oh, I can smile for you, and tilt my head, And drink your rushing words with eager lips, And paint my mouth for you a fragrant red, And trace your brows with tutored finger-tips. When you rehearse your list of loves to me, Oh, I can laugh and marvel, rapturous-eyed. And you laugh back, nor can you ever see, The thousand little deaths my heart has died. And you believe, so well I know my part, That I am gay as morning, light as snow, And all the straining things within my heart You'll never know. Oh, I can laugh and listen, when we meet, And you bring tales of fresh adventurings,-- Of ladies delicately indiscreet, Of lingering hands, and gently whispered things. And you are pleased with me, and strive anew To sing me sagas of your late delights. Thus do you want me--marveling, gay, and true, Nor do you see my staring eyes of nights. And when, in search of novelty, you stray, Oh, I can kiss you blithely as you go.... And what goes on, my love, while you're away, You'll never know.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. One day, Amy wanted to play a game with her mom. Mom said, "Yes! Let's play a game together." 

Amy smiled and was very happy. Mom and Amy played a game that Amy really liked. She was having a lot of fun.

When the game finished, Amy wanted to play another game but Mom said, "No, not now. Let's stop playing for now."

Amy was naughty and didn't want to stop. She kept asking to keep playing the game. But Mom kept saying, "No and that's final!"

Finally, Mom said, "If you smile, I might let you play another game." Amy knew that it was only fair and smiled. Mom was very happy to see Amy smile and said, "Okay, I will let you play one more game."

The moral of the story is that when people are not willing to do what we want, we should always be nice, smile and listen to them. That way, we can show our respect, and good things can happen.

When the milk-arrow stabs, she comes, water-fluent, down the long green miles. Her milk leaks into the sea - blue blossoming in an opal. The pup lies patient in his cot of stone. They meet with cries, caress as people do. She lies down for his suckling, lifts him with a flipper from the sea's reach when the tide fills his throat with salt. This is the fourteenth day. In two days, no bitch-head will break the brilliance listening for baby-cries. Down in the thunder of that other country, the bulls are calling and her uterus is empty. Alone and hungering in his fallen shawl, He'll nuzzle the Atlantic and be gone. If that day's still, his moult will lie a gleaming ring on the sand, like the noose she slips on the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a pilot. He had a soft plane, and it was all his own. He was very proud of this plane, and he flew it every day.

The pilot loved to look out of the plane's windows. He could see the town, the sea and the sky all in one glance! He imagined what it would be like to be a bird, soaring through the air with the wind in his wings.

One day, the pilot saw something very special flying by. It was a magical, soft unicorn. He wanted to get closer to the beautiful creature.

The pilot flew his plane, following the unicorn. Soon, the unicorn and the plane were flying together through the sky. The pilot and unicorn flew all day, until the sunset.

The magical and soft night was the best day ever for the pilot and his plane. He had made a wonderful new friend, and he proudly started his journey home.

Lily was troubled on Tuesday. She had a bad dream and woke up sad. She did not want to go to school. She wanted to stay with Mom and hug her teddy bear.

Mom said, "Lily, you have to go to school. You will see your friends and learn new things. It will be fun."

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, Mom. I don't want to go. I'm scared."

Mom said, "What are you scared of, Lily?"

Lily said, "I'm scared of the big dog. He barks at me when I walk to school. He is mean and loud. He makes me cry."

Mom said, "I understand, Lily. But the big dog is not mean. He is just lonely and wants to play. He is behind a fence and he can't hurt you. You can be brave and step past him. You can say, 'Hello, dog. I'm Lily. Have a nice day.' Maybe he will be happy and stop barking."

Lily thought about it. She said, "Maybe. But I'm still scared."

Mom said, "How about this? I will walk with you to school today. We can step past the big dog together. We can say hello to him and give him a smile. Maybe he will be friendly and wag his tail. Would you like that?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Mom. Thank you. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go. It's Tuesday and it's a beautiful day."

name_of_work: Song: Love, a child, is ever crying by Lady Mary Wroth
content: LOVE, a child, is ever crying; Please him, and he straight is flying; Give him, he the more is craving, Never satisfied with having. His desires have no measure; Endless folly is his treasure; What he promiseth he breaketh; Trust not one word that he speaketh. He vows nothing but false matter; And to cozen you will flatter; Let him gain the hand, he'll leave you And still glory to deceive you. He will triumph in your wailing; And yet cause be of your failing: These his virtues are, and slighter Are his gifts, his favours lighter. Feathers are as firm in staying; Wolves no fiercer in their preying; As a child then, leave him crying; Nor seek him so given to flying.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ava who had a special urge. She wanted to help people and make them happy. She thought that being kind was the best thing in the world.

One day, Ava was walking in the park when she saw a broken toy car in the mud. She thought she could fix it and give it to the little boy who was playing with the other broken toys nearby. 

"Hello, little boy," said Ava, smiling. "Do you want to have this car? I can restore it for you!"

The boy looked at her with his intelligent eyes. He was about to say something but the mean park keeper interrupted Ava. 

"No, no! You can't do that! This is not your toy!", the park keeper yelled.

Ava was a bit scared, but she was brave and refused to give up. She looked at the park keeper and said, "But it will make him happy". The park keeper looked at her and smiled.

"Ok then, go ahead and fix it. It will be like restoring a little happiness," said the park keeper. 

Ava smiled and quickly got to work. With her smart, quick hands and a little bit of glue, she was able to restore the toy car in no time. The little boy was so happy and thanked Ava with a big smile.
